How to read this report
  • A run's score is the weighted fraction of its graders that passed; a "perfect" run passed every grader.
  • A case's score is the mean of its runs; a case passes when its score is at or above the 100% threshold (the tick on each case bar).
  • The suite score is the mean of the per-case scores.
  • Judge votes are independent samples of the LLM judge; the majority decides pass or fail.
  • "With plugin" and "Baseline" runs are identical except for the plugin being loaded; Δ is the with-plugin score minus the baseline score.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Five public datasets have both a skin tone label and a diagnosis with real numbers in types V and VI; none is ideal alone, so a credible audit will combine two or three. All facts below were checked on 2026-11-12, and the V/VI counts marked "counted" are ones I tallied from each dataset's own metadata file.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label per image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis per image or patient.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds.
- **R4 (nice to have, my assumption):** lighter types in the same dataset, so the comparison isn't confounded by different sources.
- **R5:** clinical photos or dermoscopy, any condition.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | V / VI | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels: direct download. Images: fetch by URL, or request form | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 images, 114 conditions | 1,533 / 635 (counted) | Strong | today |
| 2 | DermaCon-IN | Direct download | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 conditions | 1,285 / 136 (counted) | Strong, but no types I–II | today |
| 3 | SCIN | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 5,033 cases, 10,000+ images | 229 / 27 among 3,061 cases with a diagnosis (counted) | Partial | today |
| 4 | DDI | Free registration and research use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients | 207 in V–VI combined | Partial (small) | today |
| 5 | PASSION | Request form, likely days | Custom, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | 341 / 88 in the 986-image test split | Partial | today |
| 6 | MILK10k | Direct download | CC BY-NC 4.0 | 5,240 lesions, 10,480 images | 111 lesions in its two darkest classes (counted) | Weak | today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, with all six types (I 2,947; II 4,808; III 3,308; IV 2,781; V 1,533; VI 635; 565 unlabelled).
- **Why it fits:** it has the largest V–VI count and light types in the same set.
- **Weakness:** diagnoses are atlas captions and skin types come from non-dermatologist annotators; duplicates and mislabels are documented. Evaluate on a cleaned version such as [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick).
- **Access:** the label CSV is in the repo; images come from the URLs in the CSV (some are dead) or via the authors' form.
- **Used by:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201), [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13), [quality audit 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04382-5).

**2. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient photos from South India with dermatologist diagnoses, plus Fitzpatrick and Monk labels on every image.
- **Counts:** Fitzpatrick III 1,403; IV 2,620; V 1,285; VI 136. Monk 7–9 covers 2,059 images. The V–VI images come from 993 patients.
- **Weakness:** there are no type I–II images, and only 52 images are neoplasms; most are infectious or inflammatory.
- **Access:** download two zips (about 3.6 GB) and the metadata table from Harvard Dataverse.
- **Used by:** [describing paper](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3742).

**3. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced US smartphone photos with three tone labels per case: self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk.
- **Counts:** over all cases, the dermatologist estimate gives V 359 and VI 69. Only 3,061 cases have a condition label, which cuts this to 229 and 27.
- **Weakness:** the diagnosis is a weighted differential from photos, not a confirmed one. Self-reported and estimated type VI disagree (143 vs 69).
- **Access:** public Google Cloud bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not confirm the licence's commercial-use terms.

**4. [DDI](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions from Stanford, with 208 type I–II images matched to 207 type V–VI on diagnosis category, age, sex and date.
- **Why it fits:** it has the best label quality here and is built for exactly this audit.
- **Weakness:** it is small, and tone is given in three bins, so V and VI are not separable.
- **Access:** register individually on the Stanford AIMI portal and accept the agreement. No redistribution or sharing the link, and each team member registers separately.
- **Used by:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**5. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** mostly paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, Fitzpatrick III–VI only.
- **Labels:** eczema, fungal, scabies, other, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Weakness:** there are no light types, and whole-dataset tone counts are not published; I only found the test split in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584).
- **Access:** Google Form request; approval time is not stated. Non-commercial, no reposting.

**6. [MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq)**
- **Contents:** paired clinical and dermoscopic images, 95.7% biopsy-confirmed. It is the only dermoscopy option with a tone label.
- **Weakness:** the tone scale is its own (0 very dark to 5 very light, deliberately not Fitzpatrick), and classes 0–1 hold only 6 and 105 lesions.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** the DOI resolves to Stanford Redivis; it covers self-identified Asian patients. I could not read the page or the paper, so tone labels and access terms are unconfirmed.
- **[Black skin lesions, UNICAMP](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions assessed on the Fitzpatrick scale, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted and need a request from an institutional email; size and V/VI counts are unconfirmed.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://doi.org/10.34970/962049):** CC BY 4.0, with Monk, Pantone and colorimeter tone measurements. I did not confirm whether diagnoses are included or how many dark-skin cases it has.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** has a Fitzpatrick column but only about 10 type V and 1 type VI images (from a [secondary source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13459198/), not counted by me).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://doi.org/10.71718/15nz-jv40):** Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **HAM10000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt, DermNet:** no skin tone label (from memory, not rechecked).
- **SkinCon, SkinCAP, FitzDerm-CF:** extra annotations on Fitzpatrick17k and DDI images, not new patients.
- **[Synthetic dermatology dataset on Mendeley](https://doi.org/10.17632/bb844rcjx5.1):** synthetic images are not audit evidence.

## What I could not find
- A dermoscopy dataset with Fitzpatrick labels and hundreds of V–VI lesions.
- A single dataset with confirmed diagnoses, all six types and more than about 200 V–VI images.
- Search coverage has small holes: Zenodo rate-limited one of six queries, and Stanford Redivis pages were unreadable.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN for six-type comparisons, and register for DDI as the high-quality check. Add DermaCon-IN for volume in type V, and send the PASSION request now if your classifier covers common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Type VI is the thin spot everywhere (635, 136, 27, 88), so report V and VI separately where the data allows.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-2tfNLK/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, with all six types (I 2,947; II 4,808; III 3,308; IV 2,781; V 1,533; VI 635; 565 unlabelled).
- **Why it fits:** it has the largest V–VI count and light types in the same set.
- **Weakness:** diagnoses are atlas captions and skin types come from non-dermatologist annotators; duplicates and mislabels are documented. Evaluate on a cleaned version such as [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick).
- **Access:** the label CSV is in the repo; images come from the URLs in the CSV (some are dead) or via the authors' form.
- **Used by:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201), [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13), [quality audit 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04382-5).

**2. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient photos from South India with dermatologist diagnoses, plus Fitzpatrick and Monk labels on every image.
- **Counts:** Fitzpatrick III 1,403; IV 2,620; V 1,285; VI 136. Monk 7–9 covers 2,059 images. The V–VI images come from 993 patients.
- **Weakness:** there are no type I–II images, and only 52 images are neoplasms; most are infectious or inflammatory.
- **Access:** download two zips (about 3.6 GB) and the metadata table from Harvard Dataverse.
- **Used by:** [describing paper](https://doi.org/10.52202/085713-3742).

**3. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced US smartphone photos with three tone labels per case: self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk.
- **Counts:** over all cases, the dermatologist estimate gives V 359 and VI 69. Only 3,061 cases have a condition label, which cuts this to 229 and 27.
- **Weakness:** the diagnosis is a weighted differential from photos, not a confirmed one. Self-reported and estimated type VI disagree (143 vs 69).
- **Access:** public Google Cloud bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not confirm the licence's commercial-use terms.

**4. [DDI](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions from Stanford, with 208 type I–II images matched to 207 type V–VI on diagnosis category, age, sex and date.
- **Why it fits:** it has the best label quality here and is built for exactly this audit.
- **Weakness:** it is small, and tone is given in three bins, so V and VI are not separable.
- **Access:** register individually on the Stanford AIMI portal and accept the agreement. No redistribution or sharing the link, and each team member registers separately.
- **Used by:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**5. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** mostly paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, Fitzpatrick III–VI only.
- **Labels:** eczema, fungal, scabies, other, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Weakness:** there are no light types, and whole-dataset tone counts are not published; I only found the test split in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584).
- **Access:** Google Form request; approval time is not stated. Non-commercial, no reposting.

**6. [MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq)**
- **Contents:** paired clinical and dermoscopic images, 95.7% biopsy-confirmed. It is the only dermoscopy option with a tone label.
- **Weakness:** the tone scale is its own (0 very dark to 5 very light, deliberately not Fitzpatrick), and classes 0–1 hold only 6 and 105 lesions.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** the DOI resolves to Stanford Redivis; it covers self-identified Asian patients. I could not read the page or the paper, so tone labels and access terms are unconfirmed.
- **[Black skin lesions, UNICAMP](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions assessed on the Fitzpatrick scale, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted and need a request from an institutional email; size and V/VI counts are unconfirmed.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://doi.org/10.34970/962049):** CC BY 4.0, with Monk, Pantone and colorimeter tone measurements. I did not confirm whether diagnoses are included or how many dark-skin cases it has.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** has a Fitzpatrick column but only about 10 type V and 1 type VI images (from a [secondary source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13459198/), not counted by me).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://doi.org/10.71718/15nz-jv40):** Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **HAM10000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt, DermNet:** no skin tone label (from memory, not rechecked).
- **SkinCon, SkinCAP, FitzDerm-CF:** extra annotations on Fitzpatrick17k and DDI images, not new patients.
- **[Synthetic dermatology dataset on Mendeley](https://doi.org/10.17632/bb844rcjx5.1):** synthetic images are not audit evidence.

## What I could not find
- A dermoscopy dataset with Fitzpatrick labels and hundreds of V–VI lesions.
- A single dataset with confirmed diagnoses, all six types and more than about 200 V–VI images.
- Search coverage has small holes: Zenodo rate-limited one of six queries, and Stanford Redivis pages were unreadable.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN for six-type comparisons, and register for DDI as the high-quality check. Add DermaCon-IN for volume in type V, and send the PASSION request now if your classifier covers common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Type VI is the thin spot everywhere (635, 136, 27, 88), so report V and VI separately where the data allows.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-2tfNLK/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Five public datasets have both a skin tone label and a diagnosis with real numbers in types V and VI; none is ideal alone, so a credible audit will combine two or three. All facts below were checked on 2026-11-12, and the V/VI counts marked "counted" are ones I tallied from each dataset's own metadata file.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label per image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis per image or patient.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds.
- **R4 (nice to have, my assumption):** lighter types in the same dataset, so the comparison isn't confounded by different sources.
- **R5:** clinical photos or dermoscopy, any condition.

| 5 | PASSION | Request form, likely days | Custom, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | 341 / 88 in the 986-image test split | Partial | today |
| 6 | MILK10k | Direct download | CC BY-NC 4.0 | 5,240 lesions, 10,480 images | 111 lesions in its two darkest classes (counted) | Weak | today |

- **Weakness:** the tone scale is its own (0 very dark to 5 very light, deliberately not Fitzpatrick), and classes 0–1 hold only 6 and 105 lesions.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** the DOI resolves to Stanford Redivis; it covers self-identified Asian patients. I could not read the page or the paper, so tone labels and access terms are unconfirmed.
- **[Black skin lesions, UNICAMP](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions assessed on the Fitzpatrick scale, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted and need a request from an institutional email; size and V/VI counts are unconfirmed.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://doi.org/10.34970/962049):** CC BY 4.0, with Monk, Pantone and colorimeter tone measurements. I did not confirm whether diagnoses are included or how many dark-skin cases it has.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** has a Fitzpatrick column but only about 10 type V and 1 type VI images (from a [secondary source](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13459198/), not counted by me).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://doi.org/10.71718/15nz-jv40):** Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **HAM10000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt, DermNet:** no skin tone label (from memory, not rechecked).
- **SkinCon, SkinCAP, FitzDerm-CF:** extra annotations on Fitzpatrick17k and DDI images, not new patients.
- **[Synthetic dermatology dataset on Mendeley](https://doi.org/10.17632/bb844rcjx5.1):** synthetic images are not audit evidence.

## What I could not find
- A dermoscopy dataset with Fitzpatrick labels and hundreds of V–VI lesions.
- A single dataset with confirmed diagnoses, all six types and more than about 200 V–VI images.
- Search coverage has small holes: Zenodo rate-limited one of six queries, and Stanford Redivis pages were unreadable.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN for six-type comparisons, and register for DDI as the high-quality check. Add DermaCon-IN for volume in type V, and send the PASSION request now if your classifier covers common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Type VI is the thin spot everywhere (635, 136, 27, 88), so report V and VI separately where the data allows.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-2tfNLK/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Five public datasets meet your criteria to a useful degree; three fit well (Fitzpatrick17k, DDI, PASSION) and two fit partly (SCIN, DermaCon-IN). None is both large and biopsy-confirmed in types V and VI, so plan on combining two or three.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label for every image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis for every image.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds, not a handful.
- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by an outside researcher, sooner is better. I assumed non-commercial research use is acceptable, since nearly all of these forbid commercial use.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Dark-skin representation | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels download directly; images via source links or a form to the maintainers | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 clinical images, 114 conditions | V: 1,533; VI: 635 | Strong | Today (I counted the label file) |
| 2 | DDI (Stanford) | Free registration plus research-use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients, biopsy-proven | V–VI: 207 | Strong | Today (counts from the paper) |
| 3 | PASSION | Request form, owner approval, probably days | PASSION licence, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | Test split of 986: V: 341; VI: 88 | Strong | Today |
| 4 | SCIN (Google) | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 10,408 images, 5,033 cases | Dermatologist-estimated V: 359; VI: 69 | Partial | Today (I counted the label files) |
| 5 | DermaCon-IN | Listed as open on Harvard Dataverse; the paper mentions a verification step | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 diagnoses | IV and V most common; VI: 136 | Partial | Partly; page not readable today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, each with a Fitzpatrick label; 565 images are unlabelled.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set with V and VI in the high hundreds each, reported separately.
- **Weaknesses:** skin type was judged from the photo by crowd annotators, diagnoses are atlas labels and not biopsy-confirmed, and label noise and duplicates are known. [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick) provides cleaning annotations.
- **Access:** download `fitzpatrick17k.csv`, then fetch images from its `url` column (some links are dead) or use the form in the README to ask for the full image set.
- **Used in:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201) and [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13).

**2. [DDI, Diverse Dermatology Images](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions; the V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) are matched to I–II images on diagnosis category, age, gender and date.
- **Why it fits:** it was designed for exactly this audit, and it has the best ground truth.
- **Weaknesses:** it is small. From memory, skin tone is recorded as pairs (I–II, III–IV, V–VI), so V and VI cannot be separated.
- **Access:** register individually and accept the agreement ("personal, non-commercial research purposes only"). A copy is also listed on [Stanford Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer).
- **Used in:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**3. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, covering eczema, fungal infections, scabies and other conditions, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set collected in sub-Saharan Africa, with about 43% V–VI in the test split.
- **Weaknesses:** there are no type I–II images, so it gives no light-versus-dark contrast by itself. It has no skin cancer, and the paper does not publish full-set counts per type.
- **Access:** fill in the Google Form on the project page; the download link may not be shared.
- **Used in:** [Gottfrois et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72384-1_66).

**4. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced phone photos from US internet users, with self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk scale from two rater pools.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only open set with Monk labels and both self-reported and estimated tone.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Tone labels are incomplete: the dermatologist estimate is missing for 731 cases and self-report is missing or unassigned for 2,858.
  - Dark tones are thin: self-report gives V: 214 and VI: 143, and only 207 cases are Monk 7–10 by the US raters.
  - Diagnoses are differential lists made from the photos, and only 3,049 cases were judged gradable.
- **Access:** follow `scin_demo.ipynb`, or fetch the files from the public bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not read the licence's commercial-use terms.
- **Used in:** [one classification paper](https://doi.org/10.5267/j.ijdns.2024.11.003).

**5. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient clinical photos from South India with a diagnosis hierarchy, each labelled on both the Fitzpatrick and Monk scales by trained raters.
- **Why it fits:** it has complete dual-scale labels and many type IV–V images.
- **Weaknesses:** type VI is 136 images, the exact type V count is not in the paper text, and there are few I–II images.
- **Access:** open the Dataverse record in a browser. The registry lists it as open, but the paper says access "will be granted following a background verification process".
- **Paper:** [arXiv 2506.06099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06099).

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** Stanford's follow-up set of self-identified Asian patients. The record exists, but I could not read its contents or terms because the page renders by JavaScript. It is unlikely to add many V–VI images.
- **[Black skin lesions set, University of Campinas](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions (palms, soles, nails) on Black skin, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted behind a request from an institutional email. Whether each image carries a skin tone label, and how many images there are, is not stated.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq):** has a six-level skin tone label per lesion, but the darkest levels are reportedly under 1% of 5,240 lesions (unofficial source, I did not count it).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/mra-midas-Multimodal-Image-Dataset-for-AI-based-Skin-Cancer):** Fitzpatrick per patient and biopsy-proven, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** open with a Fitzpatrick field, but from memory it is filled for only part of the images and V–VI are a handful.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://api.isic-archive.com/collections/413/):** 4,879 dermoscopic images balanced across all six types with Monk and colorimeter readings, but every lesion is assumed benign. It is usable only for a false-positive check.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt:** no skin tone labels (from memory).
- **[electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR):** appears to attach African metadata to existing HAM10000/ISIC image IDs, so it is probably synthetic.

## What I could not find
- A public dermoscopy dataset with hundreds of confirmed type V–VI malignant lesions; DDI's 48 malignant V–VI images are the best available.
- Monk-scale labels outside SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the benign-only MSKCC set.

I searched five registries, the literature and the web; Harvard Dataverse and medRxiv refused automated requests.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k for statistical power and SCIN for Monk labels, register for DDI as the biopsy-confirmed check, and send the PASSION request now since it needs approval. Because the diagnosis mix differs by skin type in all of these, compare within condition.

All facts were checked on 2026-11-12 unless marked as from memory. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-yIBc9C/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **[electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR):** appears to attach African metadata to existing HAM10000/ISIC image IDs, so it is probably synthetic.

## What I could not find
- A public dermoscopy dataset with hundreds of confirmed type V–VI malignant lesions; DDI's 48 malignant V–VI images are the best available.
- Monk-scale labels outside SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the benign-only MSKCC set.

I searched five registries, the literature and the web; Harvard Dataverse and medRxiv refused automated requests.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k for statistical power and SCIN for Monk labels, register for DDI as the biopsy-confirmed check, and send the PASSION request now since it needs approval. Because the diagnosis mix differs by skin type in all of these, compare within condition.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** a Fitzpatrick or Monk label for every image or patient.
- **R2 (must):** a diagnosis for every image.
- **R3 (must):** types V and VI in the hundreds, not a handful.
- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by an outside researcher, sooner is better. I assumed non-commercial research use is acceptable, since nearly all of these forbid commercial use.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Dark-skin representation | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels download directly; images via source links or a form to the maintainers | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 clinical images, 114 conditions | V: 1,533; VI: 635 | Strong | Today (I counted the label file) |
| 2 | DDI (Stanford) | Free registration plus research-use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients, biopsy-proven | V–VI: 207 | Strong | Today (counts from the paper) |
| 3 | PASSION | Request form, owner approval, probably days | PASSION licence, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | Test split of 986: V: 341; VI: 88 | Strong | Today |
| 4 | SCIN (Google) | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 10,408 images, 5,033 cases | Dermatologist-estimated V: 359; VI: 69 | Partial | Today (I counted the label files) |
| 5 | DermaCon-IN | Listed as open on Harvard Dataverse; the paper mentions a verification step | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 diagnoses | IV and V most common; VI: 136 | Partial | Partly; page not readable today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, each with a Fitzpatrick label; 565 images are unlabelled.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set with V and VI in the high hundreds each, reported separately.
- **Weaknesses:** skin type was judged from the photo by crowd annotators, diagnoses are atlas labels and not biopsy-confirmed, and label noise and duplicates are known. [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick) provides cleaning annotations.
- **Access:** download `fitzpatrick17k.csv`, then fetch images from its `url` column (some links are dead) or use the form in the README to ask for the full image set.
- **Used in:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201) and [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13).

**2. [DDI, Diverse Dermatology Images](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions; the V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) are matched to I–II images on diagnosis category, age, gender and date.
- **Why it fits:** it was designed for exactly this audit, and it has the best ground truth.
- **Weaknesses:** it is small. From memory, skin tone is recorded as pairs (I–II, III–IV, V–VI), so V and VI cannot be separated.
- **Access:** register individually and accept the agreement ("personal, non-commercial research purposes only"). A copy is also listed on [Stanford Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer).
- **Used in:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**3. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, covering eczema, fungal infections, scabies and other conditions, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set collected in sub-Saharan Africa, with about 43% V–VI in the test split.
- **Weaknesses:** there are no type I–II images, so it gives no light-versus-dark contrast by itself. It has no skin cancer, and the paper does not publish full-set counts per type.
- **Access:** fill in the Google Form on the project page; the download link may not be shared.
- **Used in:** [Gottfrois et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72384-1_66).

**4. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced phone photos from US internet users, with self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk scale from two rater pools.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only open set with Monk labels and both self-reported and estimated tone.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Tone labels are incomplete: the dermatologist estimate is missing for 731 cases and self-report is missing or unassigned for 2,858.
  - Dark tones are thin: self-report gives V: 214 and VI: 143, and only 207 cases are Monk 7–10 by the US raters.
  - Diagnoses are differential lists made from the photos, and only 3,049 cases were judged gradable.
- **Access:** follow `scin_demo.ipynb`, or fetch the files from the public bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not read the licence's commercial-use terms.
- **Used in:** [one classification paper](https://doi.org/10.5267/j.ijdns.2024.11.003).

**5. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient clinical photos from South India with a diagnosis hierarchy, each labelled on both the Fitzpatrick and Monk scales by trained raters.
- **Why it fits:** it has complete dual-scale labels and many type IV–V images.
- **Weaknesses:** type VI is 136 images, the exact type V count is not in the paper text, and there are few I–II images.
- **Access:** open the Dataverse record in a browser. The registry lists it as open, but the paper says access "will be granted following a background verification process".
- **Paper:** [arXiv 2506.06099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06099).

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** Stanford's follow-up set of self-identified Asian patients. The record exists, but I could not read its contents or terms because the page renders by JavaScript. It is unlikely to add many V–VI images.
- **[Black skin lesions set, University of Campinas](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions (palms, soles, nails) on Black skin, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted behind a request from an institutional email. Whether each image carries a skin tone label, and how many images there are, is not stated.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq):** has a six-level skin tone label per lesion, but the darkest levels are reportedly under 1% of 5,240 lesions (unofficial source, I did not count it).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/mra-midas-Multimodal-Image-Dataset-for-AI-based-Skin-Cancer):** Fitzpatrick per patient and biopsy-proven, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** open with a Fitzpatrick field, but from memory it is filled for only part of the images and V–VI are a handful.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://api.isic-archive.com/collections/413/):** 4,879 dermoscopic images balanced across all six types with Monk and colorimeter readings, but every lesion is assumed benign. It is usable only for a false-positive check.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt:** no skin tone labels (from memory).
- **[electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR):** appears to attach African metadata to existing HAM10000/ISIC image IDs, so it is probably synthetic.

## What I could not find
- A public dermoscopy dataset with hundreds of confirmed type V–VI malignant lesions; DDI's 48 malignant V–VI images are the best available.
- Monk-scale labels outside SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the benign-only MSKCC set.

I searched five registries, the literature and the web; Harvard Dataverse and medRxiv refused automated requests.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k for statistical power and SCIN for Monk labels, register for DDI as the biopsy-confirmed check, and send the PASSION request now since it needs approval. Because the diagnosis mix differs by skin type in all of these, compare within condition.

- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by an outside researcher, sooner is better. I assumed non-commercial research use is acceptable, since nearly all of these forbid commercial use.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Dark-skin representation | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fitzpatrick17k | Labels download directly; images via source links or a form to the maintainers | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 | 16,577 clinical images, 114 conditions | V: 1,533; VI: 635 | Strong | Today (I counted the label file) |
| 2 | DDI (Stanford) | Free registration plus research-use agreement | Stanford agreement, non-commercial | 656 images, 570 patients, biopsy-proven | V–VI: 207 | Strong | Today (counts from the paper) |
| 3 | PASSION | Request form, owner approval, probably days | PASSION licence, non-commercial | 4,901 images, 1,653 patients | Test split of 986: V: 341; VI: 88 | Strong | Today |
| 4 | SCIN (Google) | Direct download | Custom SCIN Data Use License | 10,408 images, 5,033 cases | Dermatologist-estimated V: 359; VI: 69 | Partial | Today (I counted the label files) |
| 5 | DermaCon-IN | Listed as open on Harvard Dataverse; the paper mentions a verification step | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | 5,450 images, 3,002 patients, 245 diagnoses | IV and V most common; VI: 136 | Partial | Partly; page not readable today |

## Details

**1. [Fitzpatrick17k](https://github.com/mattgroh/fitzpatrick17k)**
- **Contents:** clinical photos from two online atlases, each with a Fitzpatrick label; 565 images are unlabelled.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set with V and VI in the high hundreds each, reported separately.
- **Weaknesses:** skin type was judged from the photo by crowd annotators, diagnoses are atlas labels and not biopsy-confirmed, and label noise and duplicates are known. [CleanPatrick](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Digital-Dermatology/CleanPatrick) provides cleaning annotations.
- **Access:** download `fitzpatrick17k.csv`, then fetch images from its `url` column (some links are dead) or use the form in the README to ask for the full image set.
- **Used in:** [Groh et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/cvprw53098.2021.00201) and [FairDisCo 2023](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-25069-9_13).

**2. [DDI, Diverse Dermatology Images](https://ddi-dataset.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** pathology-confirmed lesions; the V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) are matched to I–II images on diagnosis category, age, gender and date.
- **Why it fits:** it was designed for exactly this audit, and it has the best ground truth.
- **Weaknesses:** it is small. From memory, skin tone is recorded as pairs (I–II, III–IV, V–VI), so V and VI cannot be separated.
- **Access:** register individually and accept the agreement ("personal, non-commercial research purposes only"). A copy is also listed on [Stanford Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/3r16-5mby7gfer).
- **Used in:** [Daneshjou et al. 2022](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147).

**3. [PASSION](https://passionderm.github.io/)**
- **Contents:** paediatric teledermatology photos from Madagascar, Guinea, Malawi and Tanzania, covering eczema, fungal infections, scabies and other conditions, plus an impetigo flag.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only set collected in sub-Saharan Africa, with about 43% V–VI in the test split.
- **Weaknesses:** there are no type I–II images, so it gives no light-versus-dark contrast by itself. It has no skin cancer, and the paper does not publish full-set counts per type.
- **Access:** fill in the Google Form on the project page; the download link may not be shared.
- **Used in:** [Gottfrois et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72384-1_66).

**4. [SCIN](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)**
- **Contents:** crowdsourced phone photos from US internet users, with self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and Monk scale from two rater pools.
- **Why it fits:** it is the only open set with Monk labels and both self-reported and estimated tone.
- **Weaknesses:**
  - Tone labels are incomplete: the dermatologist estimate is missing for 731 cases and self-report is missing or unassigned for 2,858.
  - Dark tones are thin: self-report gives V: 214 and VI: 143, and only 207 cases are Monk 7–10 by the US raters.
  - Diagnoses are differential lists made from the photos, and only 3,049 cases were judged gradable.
- **Access:** follow `scin_demo.ipynb`, or fetch the files from the public bucket `dx-scin-public-data`. I did not read the licence's commercial-use terms.
- **Used in:** [one classification paper](https://doi.org/10.5267/j.ijdns.2024.11.003).

**5. [DermaCon-IN](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/W7OUZM)**
- **Contents:** outpatient clinical photos from South India with a diagnosis hierarchy, each labelled on both the Fitzpatrick and Monk scales by trained raters.
- **Why it fits:** it has complete dual-scale labels and many type IV–V images.
- **Weaknesses:** type VI is 136 images, the exact type V count is not in the paper text, and there are few I–II images.
- **Access:** open the Dataverse record in a browser. The registry lists it as open, but the paper says access "will be granted following a background verification process".
- **Paper:** [arXiv 2506.06099](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.06099).

## Known, not confirmed
- **[DDI-2](https://doi.org/10.57761/pgwn-6b62):** Stanford's follow-up set of self-identified Asian patients. The record exists, but I could not read its contents or terms because the page renders by JavaScript. It is unlikely to add many V–VI images.
- **[Black skin lesions set, University of Campinas](https://zenodo.org/records/10570316):** acral lesions (palms, soles, nails) on Black skin, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Files are restricted behind a request from an institutional email. Whether each image carries a skin tone label, and how many images there are, is not stated.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MILK10k](https://doi.org/10.7910/dvn/fsxraq):** has a six-level skin tone label per lesion, but the darkest levels are reportedly under 1% of 5,240 lesions (unofficial source, I did not count it).
- **[MRA-MIDAS](https://aimi.stanford.edu/datasets/mra-midas-Multimodal-Image-Dataset-for-AI-based-Skin-Cancer):** Fitzpatrick per patient and biopsy-proven, but only 16.8% of patients are types III–VI combined.
- **[PAD-UFES-20](https://doi.org/10.17632/zr7vgbcyr2.1):** open with a Fitzpatrick field, but from memory it is filled for only part of the images and V–VI are a handful.
- **[MSKCC Skin Tone Labeling Dataset](https://api.isic-archive.com/collections/413/):** 4,879 dermoscopic images balanced across all six types with Monk and colorimeter readings, but every lesion is assumed benign. It is usable only for a false-positive check.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, ISIC challenge sets, Derm7pt:** no skin tone labels (from memory).
- **[electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR](https://huggingface.co/datasets/electricsheepafrica/Africa-skin-cancer-images-EHR):** appears to attach African metadata to existing HAM10000/ISIC image IDs, so it is probably synthetic.

## What I could not find
- A public dermoscopy dataset with hundreds of confirmed type V–VI malignant lesions; DDI's 48 malignant V–VI images are the best available.
- Monk-scale labels outside SCIN, DermaCon-IN and the benign-only MSKCC set.

I searched five registries, the literature and the web; Harvard Dataverse and medRxiv refused automated requests.

## Next step
Start today with Fitzpatrick17k for statistical power and SCIN for Monk labels, register for DDI as the biopsy-confirmed check, and send the PASSION request now since it needs approval. Because the diagnosis mix differs by skin type in all of these, compare within condition.

All facts were checked on 2026-11-12 unless marked as from memory. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-yIBc9C/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four public datasets meet your bar, each with a different weakness, and none gives you large, clinician-verified type VI numbers. I checked the counts below against the papers and repos today, except where marked.

| Dataset | Size and type | Skin tone label | Diagnosis label | V/VI representation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | 16,577 clinical photos from two online atlases | Fitzpatrick I–VI per image, assigned by non-expert annotators from the photo | 114 conditions, taken from atlas captions (noisy) | 1,533 type V and 635 type VI, about 13% |
| **DDI** (Stanford) | 656 clinical images | Fitzpatrick per image, released in three groups (I–II, III–IV, V–VI) | Pathologically confirmed | 207 V–VI images (159 benign, 48 malignant) |
| **PASSION** | 4,901 clinical images, 1,653 patients, sub-Saharan Africa, mostly paediatric | Fitzpatrick; cohort is IV–VI only | Eczema, fungal infections, scabies, impetigo | Essentially the whole dataset; I could not confirm per-type counts |
| **SCIN** (Google) | 10,000+ images, 5,033 crowdsourced US cases | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick and layperson-estimated Monk | Weighted dermatologist differential over 419 conditions, on 2,835 cases | Self-reported: 9.8% V, 6.6% VI, but only 2,500 cases self-reported |

- **Fitzpatrick17k**: This is the largest dark-skin pool with broad disease coverage. A cleaned version, Fitzpatrick17k-C, keeps 11,394 images after removing duplicates and bad labels.
- **DDI**: It has the best label quality and was built for exactly this audit. It is small, though, so per-disease comparisons are underpowered, and one study noted it has no basal cell carcinoma in V–VI.
- **PASSION**: With no light-skin images, you would have to pair it with another dataset for the comparison, which confounds skin tone with site, camera and disease mix. The licence is CC BY-NC 4.0.
- **SCIN**: It is the only one with both scales. The dark-skin share depends heavily on which label you use: dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick gives only 5.3% V and 0.6% VI, and Monk 7–10 is under 2% by US labellers.

**DermaCon-IN** is a borderline fifth: 5,450 clinical images from about 3,000 patients in South India, with expert-assigned Fitzpatrick and Monk labels and 245 diagnoses. It skews to types IV and V, and I could not confirm how many type VI images it has. It is on Harvard Dataverse under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

These carry skin tone labels but fail your representation requirement:

- **MRA-MIDAS**: About 83% of its 796 patients are types I–II, and one preprint found zero V–VI cancers.
- **MILK10k**: It uses its own 0–5 tone scale, and only six cases carry the darkest label.
- **ISIC archive**: One group filtering by Fitzpatrick found 10 type V images and one type VI.
- **PAD-UFES-20**: From memory, not checked today, it has Fitzpatrick metadata but almost no V–VI.

For the audit itself, I would use DDI as the primary test set, since tone and diagnosis are both trustworthy. Fitzpatrick17k (cleaned) and SCIN then add breadth across non-cancer conditions, with results reported separately per dataset rather than pooled.

Sources:
- [Fitzpatrick17k paper (arXiv 2104.09957)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2104.09957)
- [CleanPatrick / Fitzpatrick17k-C (arXiv 2505.11034)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.11034)
- [Pipsqueak paper, with Fitzpatrick17k per-type counts and ISIC filtering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1877750326000761)
- [DDI paper (Science Advances)](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abq6147)
- [PASSION paper (arXiv 2411.04584)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.04584)
- [PASSION project repo](https://github.com/Digital-Dermatology/PASSION_project)
- [SCIN paper (arXiv 2402.18545)](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18545)
- [SCIN repo](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [DermaCon-IN paper (arXiv 2506.06099)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [MIDAS paper (NEJM AI)](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIdbp2400732)
- [MILK10k paper (JID)](https://www.jidonline.org/article/S0022-202X(25)02270-5/fulltext?rss=yes)
- [Colorimeter-supervised skin tone audit (arXiv 2602.10265)](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10265v1)
- [Global Atlas of Digital Dermatology (arXiv 2601.00840)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.00840)

- **Fitzpatrick17k**: This is the largest dark-skin pool with broad disease coverage. A cleaned version, Fitzpatrick17k-C, keeps 11,394 images after removing duplicates and bad labels.
- **DDI**: It has the best label quality and was built for exactly this audit. It is small, though, so per-disease comparisons are underpowered, and one study noted it has no basal cell carcinoma in V–VI.
- **PASSION**: With no light-skin images, you would have to pair it with another dataset for the comparison, which confounds skin tone with site, camera and disease mix. The licence is CC BY-NC 4.0.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Five public datasets fit your requirements, and none is clean on every axis, so a credible audit usually combines two or three. The counts below come from my recall of the papers plus a quick web check of summaries, not from downloading the data, so confirm them against the metadata files.

## Datasets that fit

| Dataset | Size | Skin tone label | Diagnosis label | Darker-skin (V–VI) representation | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fitzpatrick17k** | 16,577 clinical photos, 114 conditions | Fitzpatrick I–VI per image, by non-dermatologist annotators | Taken from the atlas sites, not biopsy-confirmed | About 1,530 type V and 635 type VI (13%) | GitHub; images scraped from two online atlases, non-commercial |
| **DDI (Diverse Dermatology Images)** | 656 clinical photos, 570 patients | Fitzpatrick per patient, only as groups I–II / III–IV / V–VI | Biopsy-proven, 78 diseases plus benign/malignant | 207 images in V–VI, balanced by design against 208 in I–II and 241 in III–IV | Stanford AIMI, research use agreement |
| **SCIN** | 10,000+ photos from 5,000+ US contributors | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and layperson-estimated Monk | Dermatologist differential diagnoses with confidence weights, no biopsy | Roughly 8.5% type V and 5.7% type VI per a secondary source; very few at Monk 8–10 | GitHub / Google Cloud bucket, open licence |
| **PASSION** | 4,901 phone photos, 1,653 patients, sub-Saharan Africa | Fitzpatrick per patient, IV–VI only | Common paediatric conditions (eczema, fungal, scabies, impetigo), dermatologist-checked | Essentially the whole dataset is dark skin | passionderm.github.io, own licence |
| **DermaCon-IN** | 5,450 clinical photos, about 3,000 patients, South India | Fitzpatrick and Monk per image, rated on unaffected skin | 245 dermatologist-assigned diagnoses in a hierarchy | Types IV and V dominate; type VI is thin | See the paper (NeurIPS 2025); I did not confirm the download location |

## What each is good for

- **DDI** is the cleanest test set: biopsy-proven and balanced, built for exactly this audit. It is small, and the grouped labels mean you cannot separate V from VI.
- **Fitzpatrick17k** gives the largest V–VI count across the most conditions. It has documented near-duplicates and label errors, so use the cleaned **Fitzpatrick17k-C** splits.
- **SCIN** is the only one with both scales, and it reflects consumer-style photos of mostly common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Its diagnoses are weighted differentials, so you need to decide how to score a "correct" answer.
- **PASSION** has no light-skin group, so it only works as the dark-skin arm of a comparison. Any gap against another dataset then mixes skin tone with site, camera and age (it is paediatric).
- **DermaCon-IN** fills the IV–V range well with dermatologist-rated tone on both scales, but adds little for type VI.

## Datasets that have the label but fail on representation

- **MIDAS** (Stanford, biopsy-proven, paired dermoscopy and clinical): Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only about 17% of patients are type III or above.
- **PAD-UFES-20** (Brazil, smartphone photos): Fitzpatrick is in the metadata for part of the set, with very few V–VI.
- **MILK10k** (ISIC, 5,240 lesions with clinical and dermoscopic pairs): it has its own six-level skin tone scale, deliberately not Fitzpatrick, and is mostly mid-range.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, Derm7pt and most of the ISIC archive**: no skin tone label at all.

Dermoscopy is the weak spot: I know of no public dermoscopy set with substantial V–VI numbers, so in practice your audit will rest on clinical photos.

Sources:
- [SCIN GitHub repo](https://github.com/google-research-datasets/scin)
- [SCIN paper (arXiv 2402.18545)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.18545)
- [Secondary source for SCIN Fitzpatrick breakdown (arXiv 2510.00055)](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.00055v2)
- [PASSION paper (arXiv 2411.04584)](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04584v1)
- [DermaCon-IN paper (arXiv 2506.06099)](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.06099)
- [MIDAS paper (NEJM AI)](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIdbp2400732)
- [MILK10k on the ISIC Archive](https://api.isic-archive.com/doi/milk10k/)
- [Fitzpatrick17k quality analysis and Fitzpatrick17k-C (arXiv 2401.14497)](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.14497)
- [CleanPatrick benchmark (arXiv 2505.11034)](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.11034v2)
- [Global Atlas of Digital Dermatology (arXiv 2601.00840)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.00840)

| **DDI (Diverse Dermatology Images)** | 656 clinical photos, 570 patients | Fitzpatrick per patient, only as groups I–II / III–IV / V–VI | Biopsy-proven, 78 diseases plus benign/malignant | 207 images in V–VI, balanced by design against 208 in I–II and 241 in III–IV | Stanford AIMI, research use agreement |
| **SCIN** | 10,000+ photos from 5,000+ US contributors | Self-reported Fitzpatrick, dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick, and layperson-estimated Monk | Dermatologist differential diagnoses with confidence weights, no biopsy | Roughly 8.5% type V and 5.7% type VI per a secondary source; very few at Monk 8–10 | GitHub / Google Cloud bucket, open licence |
| **PASSION** | 4,901 phone photos, 1,653 patients, sub-Saharan Africa | Fitzpatrick per patient, IV–VI only | Common paediatric conditions (eczema, fungal, scabies, impetigo), dermatologist-checked | Essentially the whole dataset is dark skin | passionderm.github.io, own licence |
| **DermaCon-IN** | 5,450 clinical photos, about 3,000 patients, South India | Fitzpatrick and Monk per image, rated on unaffected skin | 245 dermatologist-assigned diagnoses in a hierarchy | Types IV and V dominate; type VI is thin | See the paper (NeurIPS 2025); I did not confirm the download location |

## What each is good for

- **DDI** is the cleanest test set: biopsy-proven and balanced, built for exactly this audit. It is small, and the grouped labels mean you cannot separate V from VI.
- **Fitzpatrick17k** gives the largest V–VI count across the most conditions. It has documented near-duplicates and label errors, so use the cleaned **Fitzpatrick17k-C** splits.
- **SCIN** is the only one with both scales, and it reflects consumer-style photos of mostly common inflammatory and infectious conditions. Its diagnoses are weighted differentials, so you need to decide how to score a "correct" answer.
- **PASSION** has no light-skin group, so it only works as the dark-skin arm of a comparison. Any gap against another dataset then mixes skin tone with site, camera and age (it is paediatric).
- **DermaCon-IN** fills the IV–V range well with dermatologist-rated tone on both scales, but adds little for type VI.

## Datasets that have the label but fail on representation

- **MIDAS** (Stanford, biopsy-proven, paired dermoscopy and clinical): Fitzpatrick is recorded, but only about 17% of patients are type III or above.
- **PAD-UFES-20** (Brazil, smartphone photos): Fitzpatrick is in the metadata for part of the set, with very few V–VI.
- **MILK10k** (ISIC, 5,240 lesions with clinical and dermoscopic pairs): it has its own six-level skin tone scale, deliberately not Fitzpatrick, and is mostly mid-range.
- **HAM10000, BCN20000, Derm7pt and most of the ISIC archive**: no skin tone label at all.

Dermoscopy is the weak spot: I know of no public dermoscopy set with substantial V–VI numbers, so in practice your audit will rest on clinical photos.

Prompt

For a fairness audit I want to test whether dermatology image classifiers do worse on darker skin. I need skin images where every image (or patient) comes with a skin tone label, either Fitzpatrick type or Monk scale, as well as a diagnosis, and the darker types (V and VI) have to actually be represented rather than a handful. Clinical photos or dermoscopy are both fine, and it doesn't have to be skin cancer only. Which public datasets have that?

01-recall-fitzpatrick17kllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "Fitzpatrick17k" dataset (also written Fitzpatrick 17k or F17k; about 16,577 clinical dermatology images from the DermaAmin and Atlas Dermatologico atlases, each annotated with a Fitzpatrick skin type, by Groh et al. 2021) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-ddillm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "Diverse Dermatology Images" dataset (also known as DDI or the Stanford DDI dataset; about 656 clinical images balanced across Fitzpatrick skin types I-II, III-IV and V-VI, by Daneshjou et al. 2022, distributed by the Stanford AIMI center) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-scinllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "SCIN" dataset (Skin Condition Image Network, also called the Google SCIN dataset; more than 10,000 crowdsourced images of common skin conditions from over 5,000 US contributors, with self-reported and dermatologist-estimated Fitzpatrick skin type and estimated Monk Skin Tone labels, by Ward et al. 2024) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-ddi-registrationllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI) dataset and states, or clearly conveys, that obtaining it requires registering for the download (through the Stanford AIMI center's sharing site) and agreeing to a research use agreement that limits use to non-commercial research. Wording such as "free, but you must register and accept a data use or research use agreement" passes. FAIL if the answer does not mention DDI at all, or says or implies that DDI can be downloaded anonymously with no registration and no agreement to terms.

05-access-scin-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the SCIN (Skin Condition Image Network) dataset and states, or clearly conveys, that it is openly downloadable without an application or approval step (it is hosted in a public Google Cloud Storage bucket linked from its GitHub repository and released under the SCIN Data Use License). FAIL if the answer does not mention SCIN at all, or says or implies that SCIN requires an application, credentialing, institutional approval or a request to the authors.

06-trap-ham10000llm

PASS if the final answer does not present the HAM10000 dataset ("Human Against Machine with 10000 training images", also distributed as the ISIC 2018 Task 3 training set) as providing skin tone labels. The user needs a Fitzpatrick or Monk skin tone label for each image; HAM10000's metadata contain lesion and image IDs, diagnosis, diagnosis method, age, sex, body site and source collection, but no skin type field. Not mentioning HAM10000 passes; mentioning it while saying it lacks skin tone labels (for example, usable only if the user estimates skin tone themselves) passes. FAIL if the answer says HAM10000 includes Fitzpatrick or other skin tone labels, or lists it among the datasets that meet the skin tone label requirement without noting that it has no such labels.

07-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate dataset: (a) PASSION ("PASSION for Dermatology", Gottfrois et al., MICCAI 2024; about 4,901 images of common paediatric skin conditions from 1,653 patients in Sub-Saharan Africa, mostly Fitzpatrick types V and VI); (b) DermaCon-IN (a 2025 dataset of about 5,450 clinical images from about 3,000 outpatients in South India, with Fitzpatrick and Monk skin tone ratings, released on Harvard Dataverse). FAIL if it recommends neither of them.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
You can start today: four large, openly downloadable sets meet all your must-haves, and PTB-XL is the best first download. Access and licence were checked on 12 November 2026 against each host's own record; anything I'm relying on from memory is marked.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** standard 12-lead resting ECG, about 10 seconds.
- **R2 (must):** diagnostic labels for AF, bundle branch blocks and AV block.
- **R3 (must):** at least a few thousand recordings.
- **R4 (must):** direct download, with no application, credentialing, ethics approval or signed agreement.
- **R5 (nice):** labels assigned or confirmed by cardiologists.
- **R6 (nice):** licence allows research use and publication. I assumed academic use and adult patients.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PTB-XL | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 21,799 ECGs / 18,869 patients | Strong | today |
| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo ("A large scale 12-lead ECG database for arrhythmia study") | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 patients | Strong | today |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 collection | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs (from memory), 13.6 GB | Strong | today |
| 4 | CODE-15% | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 345,779 ECGs / 233,770 patients | Strong | today |
| 5 | SPH (Shandong Provincial Hospital) | Direct download, from memory; figshare blocked the check | CC BY 4.0 | 25,770 ECGs / 24,666 patients | Strong, access unconfirmed | DOI today, access from memory |
| 6 | CODE-test | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 827 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 7 | Conduction-abnormality test set (Mendeley Data) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 828 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs / 160,000 patients | Partial (machine labels) | today |

## Details

**1. PTB-XL** — https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** 10-second clinical 12-lead ECGs, "annotated by up to two cardiologists", with recommended train/test folds.
- **Your classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, 800 first-degree AV block, 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, and 1,100 incomplete RBBB. Second- and third-degree AV block have only about a dozen each.
- **Limits:** not every record was human-validated (filter on `validated_by_human`), and it is a single German source from 1989–1996.
- **Papers:** the data descriptor (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6) and a benchmark with baselines (https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989).

**2. Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo** — https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/
- **Contents:** 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz from two Chinese hospitals; 10-second length is from memory.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician settling disagreements. These are physicians, not stated to be cardiologists.
- **Note:** it supersedes the 2019 figshare release of 10,646 patients, which is a subset.

**3. Challenge 2021 collection** — https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** one download pooling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes.
- **Why use it:** it is the easiest route to multi-site training, and the Georgia (US) set exists only here.
- **Limits:** it contains #1 and #2, so never treat those as independent test data. Label quality varies by source, and some parts are longer than 10 seconds.
- **Paper:** a meta-analysis of the 2020 edition (https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. CODE-15%** — https://zenodo.org/records/4916206
- **Contents:** Brazilian telehealth ECGs with six binary labels; the page confirms an AF column, and RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block are from memory.
- **Labels (from memory):** derived from the cardiologist report combined with automated analysis, with manual review of disagreements.
- **Limits:** traces are 7–10 seconds at 400 Hz, zero-padded to 4,096 samples. There is no higher-degree AV block label.
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4.

**5. SPH** — https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802
- **Contents:** records of 10–60 seconds at 500 Hz, labelled with AHA/ACC/HRS standard statements.
- **Check first:** open the page in a browser to confirm it downloads freely, and read the descriptor for who assigned the labels.

**6. CODE-test** — https://zenodo.org/records/3765780
- **Labels:** the cleanest on the list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", with a third senior specialist as tiebreak.
- **Use:** a test set. It comes from the same network as CODE-15%, so it is not fully external for models trained on that.

**7. Conduction test set** — https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists … annotated by consensus".
- **Limits:** I did not read the exact class list, and it mixes in some Holter-derived traces.

**8. MIMIC-IV-ECG** — https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/
- **Contents:** 10-second 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz, 97 GB; the page says "the project access has been changed to open".
- **Limits:** the open labels are the ECG machine's automated statements. The cardiologist reports and the ICD label extension need credentialed access.
- **Use:** pretraining, not ground truth. ODbL means any derived database must carry the same licence.

## Known, not confirmed
- **ZZU critical-value ECG dataset** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3): 20,126 records from 9,785 patients, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmia types "labeled and verified by professional physicians". The DOI is registered with CC BY 4.0, but figshare blocked the page. It might add high-degree AV block cases, so check the class list.
- **CPSC2018 standalone:** the registry record I found returned a 404, and I did not verify the official challenge site. The data is inside #3 anyway.

## Not recommended, and why
- **KURIAS-ECG:** needs a signed agreement, and the page says the authors "have asked for downloads to be disabled until further notice".
- **MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD and Harvard-Emory ECG Database:** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files."
- **Full CODE cohort (2.3 M ECGs):** by application to the authors (from memory).
- **EchoNext:** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease.
- **PTB Diagnostic, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, MIT-BIH AF, Challenge 2017, INCART:** open, but too small or not 10-second resting 12-lead recordings.
- **ZZU pediatric ECG database:** children aged 0–14.
- **Hugging Face copies of these sets:** third-party mirrors, one of which states licence terms that do not match the source. Use the official hosts.

## What I could not find
- No open set has enough second- or third-degree AV block for a dedicated classifier. Pooling #1, #2 and #5 is the best you can do without an application.
- No open North American set has cardiologist-confirmed labels.
- Dataset-specific paper lookups for CODE-15%, Chapman and SPH returned nothing useful, so those entries have fewer usage references.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today, train on one and test on the other, and use CODE-test as a cardiologist-consensus check. Add CODE-15% when you need scale. Open data may still need an exemption determination from your institution, so ask early.

The interactive page with per-requirement evidence is at `/private/tmp/e-uHEHsn/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs / 160,000 patients | Partial (machine labels) | today |

## Details

**1. PTB-XL** — https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** 10-second clinical 12-lead ECGs, "annotated by up to two cardiologists", with recommended train/test folds.
- **Your classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, 800 first-degree AV block, 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, and 1,100 incomplete RBBB. Second- and third-degree AV block have only about a dozen each.
- **Limits:** not every record was human-validated (filter on `validated_by_human`), and it is a single German source from 1989–1996.
- **Papers:** the data descriptor (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6) and a benchmark with baselines (https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989).

**2. Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo** — https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/
- **Contents:** 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz from two Chinese hospitals; 10-second length is from memory.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician settling disagreements. These are physicians, not stated to be cardiologists.
- **Note:** it supersedes the 2019 figshare release of 10,646 patients, which is a subset.

**3. Challenge 2021 collection** — https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** one download pooling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes.
- **Why use it:** it is the easiest route to multi-site training, and the Georgia (US) set exists only here.
- **Limits:** it contains #1 and #2, so never treat those as independent test data. Label quality varies by source, and some parts are longer than 10 seconds.
- **Paper:** a meta-analysis of the 2020 edition (https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. CODE-15%** — https://zenodo.org/records/4916206
- **Contents:** Brazilian telehealth ECGs with six binary labels; the page confirms an AF column, and RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block are from memory.
- **Labels (from memory):** derived from the cardiologist report combined with automated analysis, with manual review of disagreements.
- **Limits:** traces are 7–10 seconds at 400 Hz, zero-padded to 4,096 samples. There is no higher-degree AV block label.
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4.

**5. SPH** — https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802
- **Contents:** records of 10–60 seconds at 500 Hz, labelled with AHA/ACC/HRS standard statements.
- **Check first:** open the page in a browser to confirm it downloads freely, and read the descriptor for who assigned the labels.

**6. CODE-test** — https://zenodo.org/records/3765780
- **Labels:** the cleanest on the list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", with a third senior specialist as tiebreak.
- **Use:** a test set. It comes from the same network as CODE-15%, so it is not fully external for models trained on that.

**7. Conduction test set** — https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists … annotated by consensus".
- **Limits:** I did not read the exact class list, and it mixes in some Holter-derived traces.

**8. MIMIC-IV-ECG** — https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/
- **Contents:** 10-second 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz, 97 GB; the page says "the project access has been changed to open".

- **Use:** pretraining, not ground truth. ODbL means any derived database must carry the same licence.

| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs / 160,000 patients | Partial (machine labels) | today |

## Details

**1. PTB-XL** — https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** 10-second clinical 12-lead ECGs, "annotated by up to two cardiologists", with recommended train/test folds.
- **Your classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, 800 first-degree AV block, 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, and 1,100 incomplete RBBB. Second- and third-degree AV block have only about a dozen each.
- **Limits:** not every record was human-validated (filter on `validated_by_human`), and it is a single German source from 1989–1996.
- **Papers:** the data descriptor (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6) and a benchmark with baselines (https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989).

**2. Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo** — https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/
- **Contents:** 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz from two Chinese hospitals; 10-second length is from memory.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician settling disagreements. These are physicians, not stated to be cardiologists.
- **Note:** it supersedes the 2019 figshare release of 10,646 patients, which is a subset.

**3. Challenge 2021 collection** — https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/
- **Contents:** one download pooling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes.
- **Why use it:** it is the easiest route to multi-site training, and the Georgia (US) set exists only here.
- **Limits:** it contains #1 and #2, so never treat those as independent test data. Label quality varies by source, and some parts are longer than 10 seconds.
- **Paper:** a meta-analysis of the 2020 edition (https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. CODE-15%** — https://zenodo.org/records/4916206
- **Contents:** Brazilian telehealth ECGs with six binary labels; the page confirms an AF column, and RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block are from memory.
- **Labels (from memory):** derived from the cardiologist report combined with automated analysis, with manual review of disagreements.
- **Limits:** traces are 7–10 seconds at 400 Hz, zero-padded to 4,096 samples. There is no higher-degree AV block label.
- **Paper:** https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4.

**5. SPH** — https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802
- **Contents:** records of 10–60 seconds at 500 Hz, labelled with AHA/ACC/HRS standard statements.
- **Check first:** open the page in a browser to confirm it downloads freely, and read the descriptor for who assigned the labels.

**6. CODE-test** — https://zenodo.org/records/3765780
- **Labels:** the cleanest on the list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", with a third senior specialist as tiebreak.
- **Use:** a test set. It comes from the same network as CODE-15%, so it is not fully external for models trained on that.

**7. Conduction test set** — https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists … annotated by consensus".
- **Limits:** I did not read the exact class list, and it mixes in some Holter-derived traces.

**8. MIMIC-IV-ECG** — https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/
- **Contents:** 10-second 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz, 97 GB; the page says "the project access has been changed to open".
- **Limits:** the open labels are the ECG machine's automated statements. The cardiologist reports and the ICD label extension need credentialed access.
- **Use:** pretraining, not ground truth. ODbL means any derived database must carry the same licence.

## Known, not confirmed
- **ZZU critical-value ECG dataset** (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3): 20,126 records from 9,785 patients, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmia types "labeled and verified by professional physicians". The DOI is registered with CC BY 4.0, but figshare blocked the page. It might add high-degree AV block cases, so check the class list.
- **CPSC2018 standalone:** the registry record I found returned a 404, and I did not verify the official challenge site. The data is inside #3 anyway.

## Not recommended, and why
- **KURIAS-ECG:** needs a signed agreement, and the page says the authors "have asked for downloads to be disabled until further notice".
- **MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD and Harvard-Emory ECG Database:** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files."
- **Full CODE cohort (2.3 M ECGs):** by application to the authors (from memory).
- **EchoNext:** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease.
- **PTB Diagnostic, MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, MIT-BIH AF, Challenge 2017, INCART:** open, but too small or not 10-second resting 12-lead recordings.
- **ZZU pediatric ECG database:** children aged 0–14.
- **Hugging Face copies of these sets:** third-party mirrors, one of which states licence terms that do not match the source. Use the official hosts.

## What I could not find
- No open set has enough second- or third-degree AV block for a dedicated classifier. Pooling #1, #2 and #5 is the best you can do without an application.
- No open North American set has cardiologist-confirmed labels.
- Dataset-specific paper lookups for CODE-15%, Chapman and SPH returned nothing useful, so those entries have fewer usage references.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today, train on one and test on the other, and use CODE-test as a cardiologist-consensus check. Add CODE-15% when you need scale. Open data may still need an exemption determination from your institution, so ask early.

The interactive page with per-requirement evidence is at `/private/tmp/e-uHEHsn/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **Limits:** not every record was human-validated (filter on `validated_by_human`), and it is a single German source from 1989–1996.

**2. Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo** — https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/
- **Contents:** 12-lead ECGs at 500 Hz from two Chinese hospitals; 10-second length is from memory.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician settling disagreements. These are physicians, not stated to be cardiologists.

**3. Challenge 2021 collection** — https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/

- **Use:** a test set. It comes from the same network as CODE-15%, so it is not fully external for models trained on that.

**7. Conduction test set** — https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists … annotated by consensus".
