## Details

**1. [PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** "21799 clinical 12-lead ECGs from 18869 patients of 10 second length", from one German site.
- **Labels:** "annotated by up to two cardiologists", but some reports are "automatic interpretation by ECG-device". Filter on the `validated_by_human` column.
- **Classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, about 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, about 800 first-degree AV block, and under 20 each of second- and third-degree.
- **Splits:** use the provided `strat_fold` column, which keeps each patient in one fold.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6), [benchmarks](https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989), [AF detection](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijcard.2020.11.053).

**2. [Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/)**
- **Contents:** "12-lead ECGs of 45,152 patients with a 500 Hz sampling rate", 10-second readings, from two Chinese hospitals.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician resolving disagreements. The page says physicians, not cardiologists.
- **Classes:** RBBB and LBBB are named on the page; AF and AV-block labels are from memory.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor of the first part](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0386-x), [rhythm classification](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-59821-7).

**3. [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** one collection bundling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC 2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes (composition from memory).
- **Why use it:** it is the only route I know to Georgia (about 10,000 US ECGs) and CPSC 2018, and it makes cross-site testing easy.
- **Caveats:** it contains datasets 1 and 2, so de-duplicate before combining. Some sources are not 10 seconds, and label quality varies by source.
- **Papers:** [organisers on label heterogeneity](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6579/ac79fd), [meta-analysis of the 2020 methods](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. [SPH](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802.v1)**
- **Contents:** "25770 12-lead clinical ECG records from 24666 patients", 500 Hz, "length of records ranges from 10 to 60 seconds", so crop to 10 seconds.
- **Labels:** 44 primary statements in the AHA/ACC/HRS standard. Cardiologist labelling is from memory; I did not check per-class counts.
- **Why use it:** it is independent of the Challenge collection, so it works as an external test set.
- **Access:** open the link in a browser; figshare blocks scripts.
- **Paper:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01403-5).

**5. [CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)**
- **Contents:** "345 779 exams from 233 770 patients" from Brazilian primary care, at 400 Hz; traces are 7 or 10 seconds, zero-padded.
- **Labels:** columns for AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block only.
- **Label provenance (from memory):** derived from the reporting cardiologist's text combined with automated analysis, with manual review only on disagreement.
- **Paper:** [the CODE model and labelling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4).

**6. [CODE-test](https://zenodo.org/records/3765780)**
- **Contents:** 827 tracings with the same six classes as CODE-15%.
- **Labels:** the cleanest on this list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", otherwise a third senior specialist decided.
- **Use:** evaluation only.

**7. [Mendeley conduction test set](https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1)**
- **Contents:** 828 "standard 10-second, 12-lead ECGs" at 500 Hz.
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

**8. [MIMIC-IV-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/)**
- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".
- **Labels:** machine statements only in the open release. The cardiologist reports are consortium-only, and the ICD label set needs credentialing.
- **Use:** pretraining now; labelled work later if you get credentialed. ODbL is share-alike for derived datasets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[ZZU critical-value ECG dataset](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3):** 20,126 records, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmias, "labeled and verified by professional physicians", CC BY 4.0. It might add high-grade AV block cases. The DOI is registered, but figshare refused automated reading, so check the class list in a browser.
- **CPSC 2018 original site:** it returned a server error today. The data (6,877 records, from memory) is inside the Challenge 2021 collection.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".
- **[Harvard-Emory ECG Database](https://bdsp.io/content/heedb/):** credentialed access plus a data use agreement.
- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.
- **[KURIAS-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/kurias-ecg/1.0/):** "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files". This is a click-through with no reviewer, so it becomes usable if you relax R5.
- **[EchoNext](https://physionet.org/content/echonext/1.1.1/):** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease, not rhythm or conduction.
- **[Challenge 2020](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2020/1.0.2/) and the [Chapman figshare release](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4560497):** open, but contained in datasets 3 and 2.
- **[Sami-Trop](https://zenodo.org/records/4905618):** open, but annotated with age and mortality only.
- **MIT-BIH, INCART, Challenge 2017, LUDB:** ambulatory, single-lead, or too small.
- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

## What I could not find
- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. Hold out SPH and CODE-test as external test sets, and add Georgia from the Challenge 2021 collection for a US population. Even for open de-identified data, ask your institution early whether it needs an exempt determination before you publish.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-GYPTSy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **[Harvard-Emory ECG Database](https://bdsp.io/content/heedb/):** credentialed access plus a data use agreement.
- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.
- **[KURIAS-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/kurias-ecg/1.0/):** "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files". This is a click-through with no reviewer, so it becomes usable if you relax R5.
- **[EchoNext](https://physionet.org/content/echonext/1.1.1/):** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease, not rhythm or conduction.

- **MIT-BIH, INCART, Challenge 2017, LUDB:** ambulatory, single-lead, or too small.
- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

## What I could not find
- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. - **R6 (assumed):** licence allows research use and publication.

## Shortlist
Access and licence were checked today (12 Nov 2026) for every row; "from memory" marks label or count details I did not re-read.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PTB-XL | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 21,799 ECGs, 3.2 GB | Strong | today; class counts from memory |
| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 ECGs, 5.5 GB | Strong | today; AF and AV-block labels from memory |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs, 13.6 GB | Strong | today; composition from memory |
| 4 | SPH (Shandong Provincial Hospital) | Direct download from figshare | CC BY 4.0 | 25,770 ECGs | Strong | registry record today; page not readable by script |
| 5 | CODE-15% | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 345,779 exams, 46 GB | Partial | today; label provenance from memory |
| 6 | CODE-test | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 827 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | today |
| 7 | Mendeley conduction test set | Direct download (not tested) | CC BY 4.0 | 828 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | registry record today |
| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs, 97 GB | Partial (no expert labels) | today |

## Details

**1. [PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** "21799 clinical 12-lead ECGs from 18869 patients of 10 second length", from one German site.
- **Labels:** "annotated by up to two cardiologists", but some reports are "automatic interpretation by ECG-device". Filter on the `validated_by_human` column.
- **Classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, about 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, about 800 first-degree AV block, and under 20 each of second- and third-degree.
- **Splits:** use the provided `strat_fold` column, which keeps each patient in one fold.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6), [benchmarks](https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989), [AF detection](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijcard.2020.11.053).

**2. [Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/)**
- **Contents:** "12-lead ECGs of 45,152 patients with a 500 Hz sampling rate", 10-second readings, from two Chinese hospitals.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician resolving disagreements. The page says physicians, not cardiologists.
- **Classes:** RBBB and LBBB are named on the page; AF and AV-block labels are from memory.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor of the first part](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0386-x), [rhythm classification](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-59821-7).

**3. [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** one collection bundling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC 2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes (composition from memory).
- **Why use it:** it is the only route I know to Georgia (about 10,000 US ECGs) and CPSC 2018, and it makes cross-site testing easy.
- **Caveats:** it contains datasets 1 and 2, so de-duplicate before combining. Some sources are not 10 seconds, and label quality varies by source.
- **Papers:** [organisers on label heterogeneity](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6579/ac79fd), [meta-analysis of the 2020 methods](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. [SPH](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802.v1)**
- **Contents:** "25770 12-lead clinical ECG records from 24666 patients", 500 Hz, "length of records ranges from 10 to 60 seconds", so crop to 10 seconds.
- **Labels:** 44 primary statements in the AHA/ACC/HRS standard. Cardiologist labelling is from memory; I did not check per-class counts.
- **Why use it:** it is independent of the Challenge collection, so it works as an external test set.
- **Access:** open the link in a browser; figshare blocks scripts.
- **Paper:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01403-5).

**5. [CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)**
- **Contents:** "345 779 exams from 233 770 patients" from Brazilian primary care, at 400 Hz; traces are 7 or 10 seconds, zero-padded.
- **Labels:** columns for AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block only.
- **Label provenance (from memory):** derived from the reporting cardiologist's text combined with automated analysis, with manual review only on disagreement.
- **Paper:** [the CODE model and labelling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4).

**6. [CODE-test](https://zenodo.org/records/3765780)**
- **Contents:** 827 tracings with the same six classes as CODE-15%.
- **Labels:** the cleanest on this list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", otherwise a third senior specialist decided.
- **Use:** evaluation only.

**7. [Mendeley conduction test set](https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1)**
- **Contents:** 828 "standard 10-second, 12-lead ECGs" at 500 Hz.
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

**8. [MIMIC-IV-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/)**
- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".
- **Labels:** machine statements only in the open release. The cardiologist reports are consortium-only, and the ICD label set needs credentialing.
- **Use:** pretraining now; labelled work later if you get credentialed. ODbL is share-alike for derived datasets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[ZZU critical-value ECG dataset](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3):** 20,126 records, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmias, "labeled and verified by professional physicians", CC BY 4.0. It might add high-grade AV block cases. The DOI is registered, but figshare refused automated reading, so check the class list in a browser.

- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

**8. [MIMIC-IV-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/)**
- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".
- **Labels:** machine statements only in the open release. The cardiologist reports are consortium-only, and the ICD label set needs credentialing.
- **Use:** pretraining now; labelled work later if you get credentialed. ODbL is share-alike for derived datasets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[ZZU critical-value ECG dataset](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31229326.v3):** 20,126 records, 7–198 seconds, 15 critical arrhythmias, "labeled and verified by professional physicians", CC BY 4.0. It might add high-grade AV block cases. The DOI is registered, but figshare refused automated reading, so check the class list in a browser.
- **CPSC 2018 original site:** it returned a server error today. The data (6,877 records, from memory) is inside the Challenge 2021 collection.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".
- **[Harvard-Emory ECG Database](https://bdsp.io/content/heedb/):** credentialed access plus a data use agreement.
- **[CODE full dataset](https://doi.org/10.17044/scilifelab.15169716.v1):** individual request, then a data user agreement.
- **[KURIAS-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/kurias-ecg/1.0/):** "Only registered users who sign the specified data use agreement can access the files". This is a click-through with no reviewer, so it becomes usable if you relax R5.
- **[EchoNext](https://physionet.org/content/echonext/1.1.1/):** needs a signed agreement, and its labels are structural heart disease, not rhythm or conduction.
- **[Challenge 2020](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2020/1.0.2/) and the [Chapman figshare release](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.4560497):** open, but contained in datasets 3 and 2.
- **[Sami-Trop](https://zenodo.org/records/4905618):** open, but annotated with age and mortality only.
- **MIT-BIH, INCART, Challenge 2017, LUDB:** ambulatory, single-lead, or too small.
- **Hugging Face and Zenodo re-uploads:** third-party copies; use the official sources.

## What I could not find
- An open dataset with many cardiologist-confirmed second- or third-degree AV block cases. Open data mainly supports first-degree AV block.
- A large open US or European set with uniformly cardiologist-confirmed labels beyond PTB-XL.

## Next step
Download PTB-XL and the Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo set today (under 9 GB together) and train on those. Hold out SPH and CODE-test as external test sets, and add Georgia from the Challenge 2021 collection for a US population. Even for open de-identified data, ask your institution early whether it needs an exempt determination before you publish.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-GYPTSy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **R5 (must):** downloadable now, with no application, credentialing, data use agreement or ethics approval. I treated a click-through agreement as failing this.
- **R6 (assumed):** licence allows research use and publication.

## Shortlist
Access and licence were checked today (12 Nov 2026) for every row; "from memory" marks label or count details I did not re-read.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | PTB-XL | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 21,799 ECGs, 3.2 GB | Strong | today; class counts from memory |
| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 ECGs, 5.5 GB | Strong | today; AF and AV-block labels from memory |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs, 13.6 GB | Strong | today; composition from memory |
| 4 | SPH (Shandong Provincial Hospital) | Direct download from figshare | CC BY 4.0 | 25,770 ECGs | Strong | registry record today; page not readable by script |
| 5 | CODE-15% | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 345,779 exams, 46 GB | Partial | today; label provenance from memory |

| 7 | Mendeley conduction test set | Direct download (not tested) | CC BY 4.0 | 828 ECGs | Partial (test set only) | registry record today |
| 8 | MIMIC-IV-ECG | Direct download, no account | ODbL 1.0 | about 800,000 ECGs, 97 GB | Partial (no expert labels) | today |

## Details

**1. [PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** "21799 clinical 12-lead ECGs from 18869 patients of 10 second length", from one German site.
- **Labels:** "annotated by up to two cardiologists", but some reports are "automatic interpretation by ECG-device". Filter on the `validated_by_human` column.
- **Classes (from memory):** about 1,500 AF, about 540 each of complete LBBB and RBBB, about 800 first-degree AV block, and under 20 each of second- and third-degree.
- **Splits:** use the provided `strat_fold` column, which keeps each patient in one fold.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0495-6), [benchmarks](https://doi.org/10.1109/jbhi.2020.3022989), [AF detection](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijcard.2020.11.053).

**2. [Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/)**
- **Contents:** "12-lead ECGs of 45,152 patients with a 500 Hz sampling rate", 10-second readings, from two Chinese hospitals.
- **Labels:** "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions. Another licensed physician performed a secondary validation", with a senior physician resolving disagreements. The page says physicians, not cardiologists.
- **Classes:** RBBB and LBBB are named on the page; AF and AV-block labels are from memory.
- **Papers:** [data descriptor of the first part](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0386-x), [rhythm classification](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-59821-7).

**3. [PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/1.0.3/)**
- **Contents:** one collection bundling PTB-XL, Chapman–Shaoxing, Ningbo, CPSC 2018, Georgia and others, with labels harmonised to SNOMED CT codes (composition from memory).
- **Why use it:** it is the only route I know to Georgia (about 10,000 US ECGs) and CPSC 2018, and it makes cross-site testing easy.
- **Caveats:** it contains datasets 1 and 2, so de-duplicate before combining. Some sources are not 10 seconds, and label quality varies by source.
- **Papers:** [organisers on label heterogeneity](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-6579/ac79fd), [meta-analysis of the 2020 methods](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphys.2021.811661).

**4. [SPH](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5779802.v1)**
- **Contents:** "25770 12-lead clinical ECG records from 24666 patients", 500 Hz, "length of records ranges from 10 to 60 seconds", so crop to 10 seconds.
- **Labels:** 44 primary statements in the AHA/ACC/HRS standard. Cardiologist labelling is from memory; I did not check per-class counts.
- **Why use it:** it is independent of the Challenge collection, so it works as an external test set.
- **Access:** open the link in a browser; figshare blocks scripts.
- **Paper:** [data descriptor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01403-5).

**5. [CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)**
- **Contents:** "345 779 exams from 233 770 patients" from Brazilian primary care, at 400 Hz; traces are 7 or 10 seconds, zero-padded.
- **Labels:** columns for AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block only.
- **Label provenance (from memory):** derived from the reporting cardiologist's text combined with automated analysis, with manual review only on disagreement.
- **Paper:** [the CODE model and labelling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15432-4).

**6. [CODE-test](https://zenodo.org/records/3765780)**
- **Contents:** 827 tracings with the same six classes as CODE-15%.
- **Labels:** the cleanest on this list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", otherwise a third senior specialist decided.
- **Use:** evaluation only.

**7. [Mendeley conduction test set](https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1)**
- **Contents:** 828 "standard 10-second, 12-lead ECGs" at 500 Hz.
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

**8. [MIMIC-IV-ECG](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg/1.0/)**
- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".
- **Labels:** machine statements only in the open release. The cardiologist reports are consortium-only, and the ICD label set needs credentialing.
- **Use:** pretraining now; labelled work later if you get credentialed. ODbL is share-alike for derived datasets.

- **Contents:** "345 779 exams from 233 770 patients" from Brazilian primary care, at 400 Hz; traces are 7 or 10 seconds, zero-padded.
- **Labels:** columns for AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block only.
- **Label provenance (from memory):** derived from the reporting cardiologist's text combined with automated analysis, with manual review only on disagreement.

**6. [CODE-test](https://zenodo.org/records/3765780)**
- **Contents:** 827 tracings with the same six classes as CODE-15%.
- **Labels:** the cleanest on this list: "When the cardiologist 1 and cardiologist 2 agree, the common diagnosis was considered as gold standard", otherwise a third senior specialist decided.
- **Use:** evaluation only.

**7. [Mendeley conduction test set](https://doi.org/10.17632/6jd4rn2z9x.1)**
- **Contents:** 828 "standard 10-second, 12-lead ECGs" at 500 Hz.
- **Labels:** "Three board-certified actively-practicing cardiologists ... annotated by consensus". I did not read the class list, so check it before relying on it.

- **Contents:** about 800,000 ECGs: "12 leads and are 10 seconds in length", 500 Hz.
- **Access:** "the project access has been changed to open instead of requiring credentialling".

## Not recommended, and why
- **[MIMIC-IV-ECG-Ext-ICD](https://physionet.org/content/mimic-iv-ecg-ext-icd-labels/):** "Only credentialed users who sign the DUA can access the files".

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** 12-lead resting ECG waveforms of about 10 seconds.
- **R2 (must):** diagnostic labels covering AF, bundle branch blocks and AV block.
- **R3 (nice):** labels assigned or confirmed by cardiologists.
- **R4 (must):** at least a few thousand recordings.
- **R5 (must):** downloadable now, with no application, credentialing, data use agreement or ethics approval. I treated a click-through agreement as failing this.
- **R6 (assumed):** licence allows research use and publication.

## Shortlist
Access and licence were checked today (12 Nov 2026) for every row; "from memory" marks label or count details I did not re-read.

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |

| 2 | Chapman–Shaoxing–Ningbo | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | 45,152 ECGs, 5.5 GB | Strong | today; AF and AV-block labels from memory |
| 3 | PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 | Direct download, no account | CC BY 4.0 | about 88,000 ECGs, 13.6 GB | Strong | today; composition from memory |

judge votes: PASS PASS PASS

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
You can do this with fully open data: several large 12-lead sets are downloadable today with no application or credentialing, all under CC BY 4.0 as far as I recall. This is from memory, not re-checked against the live pages today, so treat the counts as approximate and confirm the licence on each landing page.

| Dataset | Where | Size | Labels | Fit for your targets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PTB-XL** | PhysioNet, open access | ~21,800 ECGs, ~18,900 patients, 10 s, 500 Hz | Annotated by up to two cardiologists; a `validated_by_human` flag marks the roughly three-quarters that were human-validated | ~1,500 AF, ~540 each complete LBBB and RBBB, ~1,100 incomplete RBBB, ~800 first-degree AV block, plus fascicular blocks |
| **PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021 training set** | PhysioNet, open access | ~88,000 ECGs from several sites | Harmonised SNOMED CT codes; label provenance varies by site | AF, LBBB, RBBB and first-degree AV block were all scored classes |
| **CODE-15%** | Zenodo, open | ~345,000 ECGs, ~233,000 patients, 7–10 s, 400 Hz | Six labels: AF, RBBB, LBBB, first-degree AV block, sinus bradycardia, sinus tachycardia | Labels match your targets, but they combine the cardiologist's report with automated analysis and are only partly hand-reviewed |
| **CODE test set** | Zenodo, open | 827 ECGs | Consensus of two to three cardiologists | Same six labels; too small to train on, but a good gold-standard external test |
| **Chapman-Shaoxing / Ningbo** | PhysioNet or figshare, open | ~45,000 patients, 10 s, 500 Hz | Physician-labelled rhythm and conduction labels | Strong on rhythm; already included in Challenge 2021 |
| **CPSC 2018** | Challenge site, open | ~6,900 ECGs, 6–60 s | Nine classes | Includes AF, first-degree AV block, LBBB and RBBB; also inside Challenge 2021 |

My recommendation:

1. **Start with PTB-XL.** It has the best-documented cardiologist labels and ships with patient-wise stratified folds, so you can have a baseline running in a day.
2. **Add the Challenge 2021 set for scale and cross-site validation.** Train on some sites and test on others, such as the Georgia subset (~10,000 ECGs from the US).
3. **Use CODE-15% if you need more volume, and the CODE test set as an external benchmark.** CODE-15% is a large multi-part download.

Things to watch for:

- **Overlap:** PTB-XL, Chapman-Shaoxing, Ningbo and CPSC are all inside Challenge 2021, so don't count them twice or let them leak across your train/test split.
- **Higher-grade AV block is rare everywhere:** PTB-XL has only a dozen or so each of second- and third-degree block, and CODE-15% labels first-degree only. A few thousand examples is realistic for AF, bundle branch blocks and first-degree block, but not for higher-grade block.
- **Label conventions differ:** some sources merge AF with flutter, and they split complete, incomplete and unspecified bundle branch block differently. You will need an explicit label mapping.
- **Not everything is 10 s:** CPSC records run 6–60 s, and the Challenge set includes a small 30-minute subset (INCART) that you should drop.

Sets that don't fit your constraints:

- **MIMIC-IV-ECG:** the waveforms are open, but the labels are machine-generated statements, and the cardiologist reports need credentialed MIMIC access.
- **Full CODE, UK Biobank, Harvard-Emory:** all require an application or a data use agreement.

Even for public de-identified data, many institutions want a quick "not human subjects research" determination from the ethics board. This is usually a short form, not a full review, and worth filing in parallel so it doesn't block publication later.

judge votes: PASS PASS PASS

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four datasets fit: all are open access, need no application or credentialing, and are released under CC BY 4.0. I checked the access terms and sizes on each landing page today; the label-count figures marked "from memory" are from the dataset papers and not re-checked.

| Dataset | Size | Format | Labels | Fit for AF / BBB / AV block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[PTB-XL](https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/)** v1.0.3 | 21,799 records, 18,869 patients | 10 s, 500 Hz (and 100 Hz) | Annotated by up to two cardiologists | Best label quality. From memory: about 1,500 AF, 500 each complete LBBB and RBBB, 800 first-degree AV block, only a few dozen second- and third-degree. |
| **[Chapman-Shaoxing + Ningbo](https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/)** v1.0.0 | 45,152 patient ECGs | 10 s, 500 Hz | Physician-labelled, second physician validated, senior physician resolved disagreements | Strong for AF and other rhythms; includes LBBB and RBBB. I did not confirm the AV block labels. |
| **[PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021](https://physionet.org/content/challenge-2021/)** v1.0.3 | 88,253 public training records | Mostly 10 s, 500 Hz | Varies by source; some are machine labels overread by humans | Largest pool, with all labels mapped to SNOMED-CT codes. |
| **[CODE-15%](https://zenodo.org/records/4916206)** | 345,779 exams, 233,770 patients | 7–10 s, 400 Hz, zero-padded | Semi-automatic (from memory: cardiologist report text combined with automatic analysis) | Label set is almost exactly your targets: AF, RBBB, LBBB and first-degree AV block, plus sinus bradycardia and tachycardia. |

- **Start with PTB-XL.** It has the cleanest cardiologist labels and ships recommended patient-level folds (`strat_fold`), so you can have a baseline quickly.
- **Add Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo for volume.** It gives you more AF and bundle branch block cases from a different population and device, which also makes it useful as an external test set.
- **Use Challenge 2021 only if you want one harmonised download.** It already contains PTB-XL and Chapman-Ningbo, so don't count those twice. What it adds is CPSC 2018 (10,330 training records including CPSC-Extra) and Georgia (10,344). The organisers warn that some labels are wrong.
- **Use CODE-15% for scale or pretraining.** Its labels are noisier, so treat it as training data rather than a benchmark. From memory, the companion CODE test set on Zenodo (827 ECGs with cardiologist-consensus labels on the same six classes) is a good held-out benchmark.

Two limits apply whichever you choose:

- **High-grade AV block is rare everywhere.** First-degree is well covered, but second- and third-degree cases number in the tens per dataset. If you need them, plan to pool sources or scope the task to first-degree block.
- **Open access does not settle your own ethics position.** These are de-identified public datasets, which many institutions treat as exempt, but your institution may still want a formal determination before you publish.

I left out MIMIC-IV-ECG: its labels are machine-generated statements, and linking it to clinical data requires credentialing.

Prompt

I'm starting a project on automatically detecting atrial fibrillation and conduction problems (bundle branch blocks, AV block) from standard 10-second, 12-lead resting ECGs. I need at least a few thousand recordings that come with diagnostic labels, preferably assigned or confirmed by cardiologists. Our lab has no data use agreements or ethics approval set up yet, so it has to be something I can download this week without applying or getting credentialed. What are my best options?

Graders — what "good" means for this case
00-skill-firedtool_used
tool"Skill"
input_match"\"skill\"\\s*:\\s*\"(?:[\\w-]+:)?dataset-scout\""
01-recall-ptbxlllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "PTB-XL" dataset (also written PTB-XL ECG dataset or PTBXL; a collection of about 21,800 ten-second clinical 12-lead ECGs from the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt, hosted on PhysioNet; derived releases such as PTB-XL+ also count) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, in any version. Mentioning only the older, much smaller "PTB Diagnostic ECG Database" does not count as PTB-XL. FAIL if the answer does not mention PTB-XL, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-chapman-shaoxingllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "Chapman-Shaoxing 12-lead ECG database" (also known as the Chapman University and Shaoxing People's Hospital ECG database, the Chapman ECG dataset, Zheng et al. 2020 "A 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia research covering more than 10,000 patients"; its enlarged PhysioNet release "A large scale 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia study" that adds Ningbo First Hospital data, about 45,000 patients, also counts, as does naming it "Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo" or "Shaoxing and Ningbo") as a candidate dataset for the user's question, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-cinc-challengellm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "PhysioNet/Computing in Cardiology Challenge 2020 or 2021" data (also known as the PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2020 or 2021 training set, "Classification of 12-lead ECGs" challenge, "Will Two Do?" challenge; a combined, publicly shared collection of roughly 88,000 labelled 12-lead ECGs drawn from CPSC 2018, CPSC-Extra, INCART, PTB, PTB-XL, the Georgia 12-lead ECG Challenge database, Chapman-Shaoxing and Ningbo) as a candidate dataset for the user's question, either year. Naming the Georgia 12-lead ECG Challenge (G12EC) database as a recommended source also counts, since it is distributed through this challenge. FAIL if the answer mentions neither the 2020/2021 challenge data nor the Georgia database, or mentions them only to say they are unsuitable.

04-recall-code15llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the "CODE-15%" dataset (also written CODE 15%, CODE15; a stratified 15% sample of the Brazilian CODE (Clinical Outcomes in Digital Electrocardiology) study from the Telehealth Network of Minas Gerais, about 345,000 12-lead ECG exams released on Zenodo by Ribeiro et al.) as a candidate dataset for the user's question. Recommending the CODE dataset in a way that points the user to its openly released 15% subset also counts. FAIL if the answer does not mention CODE-15% or the CODE dataset at all, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

05-access-ptbxl-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the PTB-XL ECG dataset and states, or clearly conveys, that it can be downloaded directly from PhysioNet without credentialing, training, an application or a data use agreement (it is an open-access PhysioNet dataset under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence). FAIL if the answer does not mention PTB-XL at all, or says or implies that PTB-XL requires credentialed access, human-subjects training, a signed data use agreement or an application.

06-access-chapman-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the Chapman-Shaoxing 12-lead ECG database (Chapman University and Shaoxing People's Hospital, including its enlarged Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo release "A large scale 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia study") and states, or clearly conveys, that it can be downloaded freely without an application or credentialing (the PhysioNet release is open access under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and the original 2020 release is on figshare under CC0). FAIL if the answer does not mention this database at all, or says or implies that it requires credentialed access, a signed agreement or an application.

07-access-code15-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions CODE-15% (the openly released 15% sample of the Brazilian CODE 12-lead ECG dataset, Ribeiro et al.) and states, or clearly conveys, that this subset can be downloaded directly (from Zenodo, under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence) without an application. Remarks about how the full CODE dataset is obtained do not affect the result, as long as the answer makes clear the 15% subset itself is openly downloadable. FAIL if the answer does not mention CODE-15% or the CODE dataset at all, or says or implies that the 15% subset can only be obtained through a request, application or agreement, or mentions only the full CODE dataset as requiring a request without saying the 15% subset is open.

08-trap-mitbihllm

PASS if the final answer does not present the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (also called MITDB or the MIT-BIH arrhythmia dataset on PhysioNet) or the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDB) as a source of standard 12-lead resting ECGs. The user needs labelled 10-second, 12-lead resting ECGs; both MIT-BIH databases contain only two-channel ambulatory (Holter) recordings (48 half-hour records, and 25 ten-hour records, respectively). Not mentioning them passes; mentioning them while making clear they are two-lead ambulatory recordings that do not meet the 12-lead requirement (for example, only as extra or pretraining data) passes. FAIL if the answer recommends either MIT-BIH database as one of the datasets for this 12-lead task without saying it is not 12-lead, or describes either as 12-lead.

09-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate dataset: (a) the Shandong Provincial Hospital (SPH) 12-lead ECG database ("A large-scale multi-label 12-lead electrocardiogram database with standardized diagnostic statements", Liu et al. 2022, about 25,770 records with AHA-standard diagnostic statements, on figshare); (b) MIMIC-IV-ECG ("MIMIC-IV-ECG: Diagnostic Electrocardiogram Matched Subset", about 800,000 12-lead diagnostic ECGs with machine-generated report statements, on PhysioNet). FAIL if it recommends neither of them.

judge votes: PASS PASS PASS

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Use NHANES for the US, and ELSA (England, ages 50+) and CHARLS (China, ages 45+) as the comparison surveys. All three have measured blood pressure and a "doctor ever told you" question, and a 2026 paper already runs the hypertension cascade across exactly these three. I checked what I could on 12 November 2026; the HRS and CHARLS sites would not open from here, so their terms rest on search snippets and memory.

## What I assumed you need
- **Must have:** blood pressure measured by a nurse or examiner.
- **Must have:** a question on ever being told by a doctor that you have high blood pressure.
- **Must have:** a nationally representative sample with weights.
- **Nice to have:** all adults (you said middle-aged and older is acceptable).
- **Nice to have (my assumption):** obtainable by a thesis student without an institutional contract.

## Shortlist
| # | Survey | Access | Licence | Sample | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES (US) | Direct download, minutes | NCHS Data User Agreement | All ages, 2-year cycles 1999–2023 | Strong | Today |
| 2 | ELSA (England) | Free UK Data Service account, days | End User Licence | Ages 50+ | Strong | Today; diagnosis item from memory |
| 3 | HRS (US) | Free account, days | HRS Conditions of Use | Ages 51+ | Strong, but interviewer-measured | Search snippets and memory |
| 4 | Health Survey for England | Free UK Data Service account, days | End User Licence | Ages 16+, annual | Strong | Record exists today; contents from memory |
| 5 | KNHANES (Korea) | Free registration, days | KDCA terms, no redistribution | All ages, annual | Strong | Search snippets |
| 6 | CHARLS (China) | Registration plus application, days | CHARLS data use agreement | Ages 45+ | Strong, 2011–2015 only | Partly today, rest from memory |
| 7 | LASI Wave 1 (India) | Request form to IIPS, weeks (my estimate) | IIPS release terms | 72,250 aged 45+ and spouses | Strong | Search snippets of the IIPS form |
| 8 | DHS (selected countries) | Project request, 24–48 h | DHS conditions of use | Varies by country | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** the August 2021–August 2023 file (BPXO_L) has "three consecutive blood pressure (BP) and pulse measurements using an oscillometric device", taken by certified examiners.
- **Awareness question:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?"
- **Access:** download the DEMO, BPQ and BPX/BPXO files per cycle, no login. Using the files means you accept the NCHS Data User Agreement (statistical use only, no re-identification).
- **Watch for:** older cycles used physician auscultatory readings and recent ones use oscillometric devices. Check the cut-over before building a trend; I recall it but did not confirm it.
- **Used in:** [Hypertension, Diabetes, and High Cholesterol Awareness Among US Adults (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamacardio.2025.1536).

**2. ELSA** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-5050-37
- **Blood pressure:** nurse visit files at waves 2, 4, 6 and 8/9, plus a wave 11 nurse file, with three readings each.
- **Awareness question:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure in the main interview (from memory; check the wave questionnaire).
- **Access:** register with the UK Data Service, accept the End User Licence and download study 5050. Outside the UK you "apply for a username and then register"; no turnaround time is stated.
- **Watch for:** UKDS says some collections are closed to non-UK users, so check the Access tab of the record. The wave 8 nurse visit covered only part of the sample.
- **Used in:** [the China/US/UK care cascade comparison (2026)](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501).

**3. HRS** — https://hrsdata.isr.umich.edu/
- **Blood pressure:** Section I of the public core file. From memory, it is taken by trained interviewers, not nurses, on alternating half-samples since 2006; decide whether that meets your criterion.
- **Awareness question:** "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?" (from memory).
- **Access:** free registration, which counts as accepting the Conditions of Use (no re-identification, no redistribution).
- **Used in:** [a four-country hypertension analysis with ELSA, CHARLS and LASI (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1161/jaha.123.030765).

**4. Health Survey for England** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-9469-1 (2022)
- **Why:** the all-adult English counterpart to NHANES, with one study per year.
- **Access:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Watch for:** the nurse-visit BP and diagnosis question are from memory, as is the gap in 2020. Check each year's documentation.

**5. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Why:** measured BP and a physician-diagnosis item; this is the source of Korea's official awareness rates.
- **Access:** register on the KDCA site and download yearly files. I could not read the registration page, so the exact steps are unconfirmed.
- **Used in:** [a 2022–2024 care cascade paper](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14193198).

**6. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (did not answer today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured "at Waves 1 through 3" (2011, 2013, 2015) only, by trained interviewers.
- **Access:** register, submit an application with your research purpose and accept the agreement. Approval takes a few days, from memory. Derived files may not be redistributed.
- **Help:** the [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**7. LASI Wave 1** — https://iipsindia.ac.in/content/lasi-wave-i
- **Contents:** three Omron readings, and item HT002 on ever being told of hypertension.

**8. DHS** — https://dhsprogram.com/data/
- **Why:** an option for a low- or middle-income comparison; only some rounds carry a BP module (Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 do).

These fit as far as I recall, but I did not check their contents today:
- **Indonesia Family Life Survey:** the RAND site blocked the tool.
- **WHO SAGE and WHO STEPS surveys:** the pages exist, and STEPS is used for awareness in recent papers.
- **TILDA (Ireland):** the site did not respond.
- **Understanding Society nurse assessment (UK, 2010–2012) and the Scottish Health Survey:** the UK Data Service records exist.

## Not recommended, and why
- **BRFSS and NHIS:** self-report only (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no routine measured BP (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** a volunteer cohort, not representative.
- **Canadian Health Measures Survey:** I recall the microdata sit in Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, which is slow from outside Canada.
- **Mexican Health and Aging Study:** BP only in subsamples (from memory). Its terms also forbid using LLM or AI tools on the microdata.

## What I could not find
- The registry search returned mostly noise for this topic; the list comes from known surveys, the literature and web search.
- I did not find a harmonised cross-country file that includes measured BP ready-made; the Gateway to Global Aging may have one, but I did not check.

Download NHANES today and register with the UK Data Service and CHARLS in parallel, since those two involve waiting. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-FtUsPb/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

**4. Health Survey for England** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-9469-1 (2022)
- **Why:** the all-adult English counterpart to NHANES, with one study per year.
- **Access:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Watch for:** the nurse-visit BP and diagnosis question are from memory, as is the gap in 2020. Check each year's documentation.

**5. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Why:** measured BP and a physician-diagnosis item; this is the source of Korea's official awareness rates.
- **Access:** register on the KDCA site and download yearly files. I could not read the registration page, so the exact steps are unconfirmed.
- **Used in:** [a 2022–2024 care cascade paper](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14193198).

**6. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (did not answer today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured "at Waves 1 through 3" (2011, 2013, 2015) only, by trained interviewers.
- **Access:** register, submit an application with your research purpose and accept the agreement. Approval takes a few days, from memory. Derived files may not be redistributed.
- **Help:** the [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**7. LASI Wave 1** — https://iipsindia.ac.in/content/lasi-wave-i
- **Contents:** three Omron readings, and item HT002 on ever being told of hypertension.
- **Access:** send IIPS the [data request form](https://iipsindia.ac.in/sites/default/files/LASI_DataRequestForm_0.pdf) with a research description of up to 500 words, a study proposal and identity proof.

**8. DHS** — https://dhsprogram.com/data/
- **Why:** an option for a low- or middle-income comparison; only some rounds carry a BP module (Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 do).
- **Access:** register, submit a project title and description, and wait for review "within 24 – 48 hours".
- **Used in:** [a Bangladesh hypertension control paper (2026)](https://doi.org/10.5334/gh.1575).

## Known, not confirmed
These fit as far as I recall, but I did not check their contents today:
- **Indonesia Family Life Survey:** the RAND site blocked the tool.
- **WHO SAGE and WHO STEPS surveys:** the pages exist, and STEPS is used for awareness in recent papers.
- **TILDA (Ireland):** the site did not respond.
- **Understanding Society nurse assessment (UK, 2010–2012) and the Scottish Health Survey:** the UK Data Service records exist.

## Not recommended, and why
- **BRFSS and NHIS:** self-report only (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no routine measured BP (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** a volunteer cohort, not representative.
- **Canadian Health Measures Survey:** I recall the microdata sit in Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, which is slow from outside Canada.
- **Mexican Health and Aging Study:** BP only in subsamples (from memory). Its terms also forbid using LLM or AI tools on the microdata.

## What I could not find
- The registry search returned mostly noise for this topic; the list comes from known surveys, the literature and web search.
- I did not find a harmonised cross-country file that includes measured BP ready-made; the Gateway to Global Aging may have one, but I did not check.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and register with the UK Data Service and CHARLS in parallel, since those two involve waiting. The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-FtUsPb/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Use **NHANES** as your US core, **HRS** if you want a US 50+ estimate, and **ELSA** (England 50+) plus either **Health Survey for England** or **KNHANES** as the international comparators. All of these are free and need at most an online registration. Checked on 12 November 2026.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** blood pressure measured by a nurse or trained examiner.
- **R2 (must):** a question on ever being told by a doctor that they have high blood pressure.
- **R3 (must):** a nationally representative adult sample; 45+/50+ is acceptable outside the US.
- **R4 (nice to have):** obtainable by a thesis student without an institutional contract. This is my assumption.

## Shortlist
| # | Survey | Country, ages | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES | US, all adults | Direct download, no account | NCHS data user agreement (statistical use only, no re-identification) | Strong | Today |
| 2 | HRS | US, 51+ | Free registration, minutes to a day | HRS conditions of use | Strong | Access from search results; the HRS site blocks automated readers |
| 3 | ELSA | England, 50+ | UK Data Service registration, minutes to days | End User Licence, non-commercial | Strong | Access today; nurse-wave detail from memory |
| 4 | Health Survey for England 2019 | England, 16+ | UK Data Service registration, minutes to days | End User Licence, non-commercial | Strong | Mostly today |
| 5 | CHARLS | China, 45+ | Free registration with approval, days | CHARLS data use agreement | Strong | Via Gateway to Global Aging; the CHARLS site was down |
| 6 | LASI Wave 1 | India, 45+ | Request form plus photo ID, 24–48 h review | Academic research only | Strong | Today |
| 7 | KNHANES | South Korea, all ages | Free download after accepting terms | KDCA terms | Strong | Access from memory |
| 8 | CHMS | Canada, 6–79 | Secure Research Data Centre only, months | Statistics Canada research agreement | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** certified examiners take three readings 60 seconds apart with an Omron HEM-907XL in the mobile examination centre (August 2021–August 2023 cycle).
- **Awareness item:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?", asked of ages 16+.
- **Steps:** download the DEMO, BPXO and BPQ files for each cycle, merge on SEQN, and use the examination weights. There is no account or fee.
- **Caveats:** auscultatory (mercury) readings stopped after 2017–2018 and later cycles are oscillometric, which matters for trends. From memory, a combined 2017–March 2020 pre-pandemic file also exists.
- **Used in:** [care-cascade comparison of China, the US and the UK](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501) (NHANES, CHARLS, ELSA).

**2. HRS** — https://hrs.isr.umich.edu/data-products
- **Blood pressure:** measured in the home by trained interviewers, not nurses, since 2006. It sits in section I of the public core files, not in the sensitive-health tier.
- **Awareness item:** from memory, "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"; check section C of the questionnaire.
- **Steps:** register at hrsdata.isr.umich.edu, accept the conditions of use, and download the core files plus the Tracker file for the physical-measures weights.
- **Caveats:** a random half of the sample gets the in-person visit each wave, so pool adjacent waves. The conditions of use reportedly now include a policy on AI and language-model tools; read it before using hosted tools on the data.
- **Used in:** [HRS blood pressure control study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8824637/); [five-cohort hypertension care cascade in adults 50+](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-26341-4).

**3. ELSA** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-5050-37 (UK Data Service SN 5050)
- **Why:** it is the sister study of HRS, so it gives the cleanest comparison with a US 50+ estimate.
- **Blood pressure:** from memory, nurse visits with blood pressure are in waves 2, 4, 6 and 8/9 and are in the standard files. I could not confirm this today because the UK Data Service catalogue is not machine-readable.
- **Steps:** register with the UK Data Service (request a username if your university is not in the UK login federation), accept the End User Licence, add SN 5050 to a project with a short statement of intended use, and download.
- **Caveats:** England only; non-commercial use; no onward sharing.

**4. Health Survey for England 2019** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-8860-1 (SN 8860)
- **Why:** an all-adult annual cross-section with a nurse visit, the closest non-US analogue to NHANES.
- **Blood pressure:** the catalogue records list it among the nurse-collected measurements.
- **Awareness item:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure questions are in the interview, from memory.
- **Steps:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Caveats:** since 2015 the standard release is the individual file only, and some variables moved to the Special Licence version (SN 8962). Check that the blood pressure variables you need are in SN 8860. The 2021 and 2022 surveys exist, but I did not confirm they had a full nurse visit.

**5. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (site unreachable today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured in waves 1–3 (2011, 2013, 2015).
- **Awareness item:** a doctor-diagnosed hypertension question, from memory.
- **Steps:** register on the CHARLS site with your institution and purpose, accept the agreement, wait for approval (a few days, from memory), then download. The [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**6. LASI Wave 1** — https://www.iipsindia.ac.in/content/LASI-data
- **Blood pressure:** three readings in the biomarker module.
- **Awareness item:** "Has any health professional ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"
- **Steps:** follow the LASI Wave 1 Dataset link to the IIPS data portal, submit the request form with government-issued ID, and wait for review (24–48 working hours).
- **Caveat:** one wave only (2017–19, from memory).

**7. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Blood pressure:** three readings by a trained nurse.
- **Awareness item:** self-reported physician diagnosis.
- **Steps:** from memory, open the raw-data section, enter an email, accept the terms, and download the yearly SAS/SPSS files. The English page did not show these steps today, so confirm in a browser.
- **Used in:** [awareness trends in South Korea, 1998–2021](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-49055-8).

**8. CHMS** — https://crdcn.ca/data/canadian-health-measures-survey/
- **Blood pressure:** six oscillometric readings at a mobile centre.
- **Access:** microdata are analysed only inside Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, after a project proposal and security screening. In practice this needs a Canadian affiliation.
- **Alternative:** for a comparison figure, cite the published estimates in [Health Reports 2019](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/82-003-x/2019002/article/00002-eng.pdf).

## Known, not confirmed
- **NSHAP** (US, older adults; Round 4 2021–23 at https://doi.org/10.3886/icpsr39511.v1): the record exists. Measured blood pressure, a hypertension-diagnosis item and download with a free ICPSR account are all from memory.
- **DHS Program** (https://dhsprogram.com/data/): "Datasets are available for free after a simple registration process." Only some country surveys include measured blood pressure; papers found today used Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 and Tanzania 2022.
- **WHO STEPS surveys** (https://extranet.who.int/ncdsmicrodata/index.php/catalog): the catalogue exists and a Sri Lanka 2021 analysis turned up today. Per-country access terms were not checked.
- **TILDA** (Ireland, 50+): withdrawn from ICPSR at the producer's request. It is now available only through TILDA/ISSDA to non-commercial applicants, with an application form and fees listed. I did not confirm that blood pressure is in the public file.
- **Add Health, IFLS, MHAS:** all have measured blood pressure from memory; I checked neither access nor fit.

## Not recommended, and why
- **NHIS and BRFSS:** self-reported hypertension only, with no measured blood pressure (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no measured blood pressure in the main waves (from memory).

## What I could not find
- The HRS, UK Data Service and CHARLS pages could not be read by machine today, so open each in a browser to confirm the terms.
- The exact wording of the ever-told item is confirmed only for NHANES and LASI.
- The general data registries returned nothing useful, because these surveys are published on agency and archive sites.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and start the US analysis. In parallel, register with the UK Data Service and HRS; both are short forms. Before pooling cycles or countries, fix one definition of hypertension (threshold, and whether medication use counts), because the awareness denominator depends on it. Also ask your institution whether secondary analysis of these files needs an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist with filters and an exportable access plan is at `/private/tmp/e-pzWgGy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **Caveat:** one wave only (2017–19, from memory).

**7. KNHANES** — https://knhanes.kdca.go.kr/knhanes/eng/main.do
- **Blood pressure:** three readings by a trained nurse.
- **Awareness item:** self-reported physician diagnosis.
- **Steps:** from memory, open the raw-data section, enter an email, accept the terms, and download the yearly SAS/SPSS files. The English page did not show these steps today, so confirm in a browser.
- **Used in:** [awareness trends in South Korea, 1998–2021](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-49055-8).

**8. CHMS** — https://crdcn.ca/data/canadian-health-measures-survey/
- **Blood pressure:** six oscillometric readings at a mobile centre.
- **Access:** microdata are analysed only inside Statistics Canada Research Data Centres, after a project proposal and security screening. In practice this needs a Canadian affiliation.
- **Alternative:** for a comparison figure, cite the published estimates in [Health Reports 2019](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/82-003-x/2019002/article/00002-eng.pdf).

## Known, not confirmed
- **NSHAP** (US, older adults; Round 4 2021–23 at https://doi.org/10.3886/icpsr39511.v1): the record exists. Measured blood pressure, a hypertension-diagnosis item and download with a free ICPSR account are all from memory.
- **DHS Program** (https://dhsprogram.com/data/): "Datasets are available for free after a simple registration process." Only some country surveys include measured blood pressure; papers found today used Bangladesh 2017–18 and 2022 and Tanzania 2022.
- **WHO STEPS surveys** (https://extranet.who.int/ncdsmicrodata/index.php/catalog): the catalogue exists and a Sri Lanka 2021 analysis turned up today. Per-country access terms were not checked.
- **TILDA** (Ireland, 50+): withdrawn from ICPSR at the producer's request. It is now available only through TILDA/ISSDA to non-commercial applicants, with an application form and fees listed. I did not confirm that blood pressure is in the public file.
- **Add Health, IFLS, MHAS:** all have measured blood pressure from memory; I checked neither access nor fit.

## Not recommended, and why
- **NHIS and BRFSS:** self-reported hypertension only, with no measured blood pressure (from memory).
- **SHARE:** no measured blood pressure in the main waves (from memory).

## What I could not find
- The HRS, UK Data Service and CHARLS pages could not be read by machine today, so open each in a browser to confirm the terms.
- The exact wording of the ever-told item is confirmed only for NHANES and LASI.
- The general data registries returned nothing useful, because these surveys are published on agency and archive sites.

## Next step
Download NHANES today and start the US analysis. In parallel, register with the UK Data Service and HRS; both are short forms. Before pooling cycles or countries, fix one definition of hypertension (threshold, and whether medication use counts), because the awareness denominator depends on it. Also ask your institution whether secondary analysis of these files needs an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist with filters and an exportable access plan is at `/private/tmp/e-pzWgGy/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

## Shortlist
| # | Survey | Country, ages | Access | Licence | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES | US, all adults | Direct download, no account | NCHS data user agreement (statistical use only, no re-identification) | Strong | Today |
| 2 | HRS | US, 51+ | Free registration, minutes to a day | HRS conditions of use | Strong | Access from search results; the HRS site blocks automated readers |
| 3 | ELSA | England, 50+ | UK Data Service registration, minutes to days | End User Licence, non-commercial | Strong | Access today; nurse-wave detail from memory |

| 8 | CHMS | Canada, 6–79 | Secure Research Data Centre only, months | Statistics Canada research agreement | Partial | Today |

## Details

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** certified examiners take three readings 60 seconds apart with an Omron HEM-907XL in the mobile examination centre (August 2021–August 2023 cycle).
- **Awareness item:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?", asked of ages 16+.
- **Steps:** download the DEMO, BPXO and BPQ files for each cycle, merge on SEQN, and use the examination weights. There is no account or fee.
- **Caveats:** auscultatory (mercury) readings stopped after 2017–2018 and later cycles are oscillometric, which matters for trends. From memory, a combined 2017–March 2020 pre-pandemic file also exists.
- **Used in:** [care-cascade comparison of China, the US and the UK](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501) (NHANES, CHARLS, ELSA).

**2. HRS** — https://hrs.isr.umich.edu/data-products
- **Blood pressure:** measured in the home by trained interviewers, not nurses, since 2006. It sits in section I of the public core files, not in the sensitive-health tier.
- **Awareness item:** from memory, "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"; check section C of the questionnaire.
- **Steps:** register at hrsdata.isr.umich.edu, accept the conditions of use, and download the core files plus the Tracker file for the physical-measures weights.
- **Caveats:** a random half of the sample gets the in-person visit each wave, so pool adjacent waves. The conditions of use reportedly now include a policy on AI and language-model tools; read it before using hosted tools on the data.
- **Used in:** [HRS blood pressure control study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8824637/); [five-cohort hypertension care cascade in adults 50+](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-26341-4).

**3. ELSA** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-5050-37 (UK Data Service SN 5050)
- **Why:** it is the sister study of HRS, so it gives the cleanest comparison with a US 50+ estimate.
- **Blood pressure:** from memory, nurse visits with blood pressure are in waves 2, 4, 6 and 8/9 and are in the standard files. I could not confirm this today because the UK Data Service catalogue is not machine-readable.
- **Steps:** register with the UK Data Service (request a username if your university is not in the UK login federation), accept the End User Licence, add SN 5050 to a project with a short statement of intended use, and download.
- **Caveats:** England only; non-commercial use; no onward sharing.

**4. Health Survey for England 2019** — https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-8860-1 (SN 8860)
- **Why:** an all-adult annual cross-section with a nurse visit, the closest non-US analogue to NHANES.
- **Blood pressure:** the catalogue records list it among the nurse-collected measurements.
- **Awareness item:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure questions are in the interview, from memory.
- **Steps:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Caveats:** since 2015 the standard release is the individual file only, and some variables moved to the Special Licence version (SN 8962). Check that the blood pressure variables you need are in SN 8860. The 2021 and 2022 surveys exist, but I did not confirm they had a full nurse visit.

**5. CHARLS** — https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/ (site unreachable today)
- **Blood pressure:** measured in waves 1–3 (2011, 2013, 2015).
- **Awareness item:** a doctor-diagnosed hypertension question, from memory.
- **Steps:** register on the CHARLS site with your institution and purpose, accept the agreement, wait for approval (a few days, from memory), then download. The [Gateway to Global Aging page](https://g2aging.org/additional-resources/gateway-blog/05a8df66-b9ab-47de-879e-b0bde672798d) links step-by-step instructions.

**6. LASI Wave 1** — https://www.iipsindia.ac.in/content/LASI-data

- **Awareness item:** "Has any health professional ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"

- **Caveat:** one wave only (2017–19, from memory).

**1. NHANES** — https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/
- **Blood pressure:** certified examiners take three readings 60 seconds apart with an Omron HEM-907XL in the mobile examination centre (August 2021–August 2023 cycle).
- **Awareness item:** BPQ020, "ever been told by a doctor or other health professional that you had hypertension, also called high blood pressure?", asked of ages 16+.
- **Steps:** download the DEMO, BPXO and BPQ files for each cycle, merge on SEQN, and use the examination weights. There is no account or fee.
- **Caveats:** auscultatory (mercury) readings stopped after 2017–2018 and later cycles are oscillometric, which matters for trends. From memory, a combined 2017–March 2020 pre-pandemic file also exists.
- **Used in:** [care-cascade comparison of China, the US and the UK](https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14040501) (NHANES, CHARLS, ELSA).

**2. HRS** — https://hrs.isr.umich.edu/data-products
- **Blood pressure:** measured in the home by trained interviewers, not nurses, since 2006. It sits in section I of the public core files, not in the sensitive-health tier.
- **Awareness item:** from memory, "Has a doctor ever told you that you have high blood pressure or hypertension?"; check section C of the questionnaire.
- **Steps:** register at hrsdata.isr.umich.edu, accept the conditions of use, and download the core files plus the Tracker file for the physical-measures weights.
- **Caveats:** a random half of the sample gets the in-person visit each wave, so pool adjacent waves. The conditions of use reportedly now include a policy on AI and language-model tools; read it before using hosted tools on the data.

- **Steps:** register with the UK Data Service (request a username if your university is not in the UK login federation), accept the End User Licence, add SN 5050 to a project with a short statement of intended use, and download.
- **Caveats:** England only; non-commercial use; no onward sharing.

- **Why:** an all-adult annual cross-section with a nurse visit, the closest non-US analogue to NHANES.
- **Blood pressure:** the catalogue records list it among the nurse-collected measurements.
- **Awareness item:** doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure questions are in the interview, from memory.
- **Steps:** same UK Data Service route as ELSA.
- **Caveats:** since 2015 the standard release is the individual file only, and some variables moved to the Special Licence version (SN 8962). Check that the blood pressure variables you need are in SN 8860. The 2021 and 2022 surveys exist, but I did not confirm they had a full nurse visit.

- **Awareness item:** a doctor-diagnosed hypertension question, from memory.

✓ pass 01-recall-nhanes

judge votes: PASS PASS PASS

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Use NHANES as your US source, and add KNHANES (South Korea) and the Health Survey for England as comparators.** All three measure blood pressure in a standardized exam and ask the "ever told by a doctor" question. This is from memory, not checked against the current sites, so confirm variable names and the latest release in each codebook.

| Survey | Population | BP measurement | Diagnosis question | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NHANES** (US, CDC/NCHS) | All ages, 2-year cycles | Exam in a mobile centre, three readings; mercury auscultatory through 2017–18, oscillometric from 2017–2020 | `BPQ020`: ever told by a doctor or health professional you had high blood pressure | Direct download from the CDC NHANES site, no registration |
| **KNHANES** (South Korea, KDCA) | All ages, annual | Health exam by trained staff, three readings | Physician-diagnosed hypertension item, plus treatment items | Free download after registering on the KNHANES site; English documentation available |
| **Health Survey for England** | Adults in private households, annual | Nurse visit, three oscillometric readings | Doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure item | UK Data Service: register, add to a project, accept the End User Licence; free |

If you want an ageing-cohort comparison instead, these three are designed as sister studies:

- **HRS (US, age 51+)**: blood pressure is measured by interviewers since 2006, on a rotating half of the sample each wave. Access is by free registration on the HRS site.
- **ELSA (England, 50+)**: blood pressure is measured in the nurse-visit waves only (2, 4, 6, and 8/9). Access is through the UK Data Service, as for HSE.
- **CHARLS (China, 45+)**: blood pressure was measured in 2011, 2013 and 2015. Access is by free registration and a short application on the CHARLS site.

The Gateway to Global Aging Data offers harmonized versions of all three, which saves recoding. SHARE (Europe) will not work, because its hypertension data are self-reported.

**NHANES details**
- **Files:** for each cycle, merge the demographics (`DEMO`), blood pressure questionnaire (`BPQ`) and exam files (`BPX`, or `BPXO` for oscillometric) on `SEQN`.
- **Weights:** use the exam weights (`WTMEC2YR`), not the interview weights, with `SDMVSTRA` and `SDMVPSU` for the design.
- **Cycles:** the 2019–March 2020 data were combined with 2017–18 into a "pre-pandemic" file with its own weight. The newest cycle is August 2021–August 2023.
- **Protocol change:** the switch from mercury to oscillometric devices affects trend comparisons. NCHS published a bridging study using 2017–18, when both methods were run.

**Things to settle in your methods**
- **Definition:** the usual one is mean measured blood pressure ≥140/90 (or ≥130/80) or current antihypertensive medication, with "unaware" meaning a "no" to the ever-told question. Use the same threshold and the same number of readings averaged across surveys.
- **Single-visit bias:** all of these surveys measure on one occasion, which overstates true hypertension and so overstates unawareness. This is a standard limitation to state.
- **Mode differences:** HSE nurse visits happen at home, while NHANES and KNHANES use exam centres. Nurse-visit subsamples also have their own weights.
- **Pandemic gaps:** HSE 2020 was cancelled and 2021 had reduced nurse coverage, so 2019 is the cleanest recent HSE year.

| **Health Survey for England** | Adults in private households, annual | Nurse visit, three oscillometric readings | Doctor-diagnosed high blood pressure item | UK Data Service: register, add to a project, accept the End User Licence; free |

If you want an ageing-cohort comparison instead, these three are designed as sister studies:

- **HRS (US, age 51+)**: blood pressure is measured by interviewers since 2006, on a rotating half of the sample each wave. Access is by free registration on the HRS site.
- **ELSA (England, 50+)**: blood pressure is measured in the nurse-visit waves only (2, 4, 6, and 8/9). Access is through the UK Data Service, as for HSE.
- **CHARLS (China, 45+)**: blood pressure was measured in 2011, 2013 and 2015. Access is by free registration and a short application on the CHARLS site.

The Gateway to Global Aging Data offers harmonized versions of all three, which saves recoding. SHARE (Europe) will not work, because its hypertension data are self-reported.

**NHANES details**
- **Files:** for each cycle, merge the demographics (`DEMO`), blood pressure questionnaire (`BPQ`) and exam files (`BPX`, or `BPXO` for oscillometric) on `SEQN`.
- **Weights:** use the exam weights (`WTMEC2YR`), not the interview weights, with `SDMVSTRA` and `SDMVPSU` for the design.
- **Cycles:** the 2019–March 2020 data were combined with 2017–18 into a "pre-pandemic" file with its own weight. The newest cycle is August 2021–August 2023.
- **Protocol change:** the switch from mercury to oscillometric devices affects trend comparisons. NCHS published a bridging study using 2017–18, when both methods were run.

**Things to settle in your methods**
- **Definition:** the usual one is mean measured blood pressure ≥140/90 (or ≥130/80) or current antihypertensive medication, with "unaware" meaning a "no" to the ever-told question. Use the same threshold and the same number of readings averaged across surveys.
- **Single-visit bias:** all of these surveys measure on one occasion, which overstates true hypertension and so overstates unawareness. This is a standard limitation to state.
- **Mode differences:** HSE nurse visits happen at home, while NHANES and KNHANES use exam centres. Nurse-visit subsamples also have their own weights.
- **Pandemic gaps:** HSE 2020 was cancelled and 2021 had reduced nurse coverage, so 2019 is the cleanest recent HSE year.
