Six datasets fit, but the best-known one, UK Biobank, appears to have paused new applications since April 2026, so NHANES (open today) and All of Us (days, if your university has an agreement in place) are where to start. I could not open the official UK Biobank, All of Us, Whitehall II or NSRR pages directly (they block automated readers), so their access terms below come from search results and memory, as marked.

## What I assumed you need

- **Wrist placement (must):** a research accelerometer or consumer tracker worn on the wrist.
- **Wear time (must):** free-living wear for several days to a week or longer.
- **Size (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **Outcomes (must):** linked deaths, hospital records or diagnoses after the wear period.
- **Access (must):** obtainable from a US university; applications are fine.
- **Activity and sleep (nice to have):** 24-hour wear with minute-level or raw data, so both can be derived.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public linked mortality files | Open download, minutes | No formal licence; NCHS data-use terms | 14,693 wearers of all ages; about 7,100 adults in a 2026 mortality paper | Strong, but deaths only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us Fitbit + health records | Institutional agreement, then individual registration and training; days if the agreement exists; cloud-only analysis | Data User Code of Conduct | More than 59,000 with wearable data | Strong, but consumer device with no raw signal | Search results today; official site not read |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer sub-study | Application, institutional agreement and fee; new applications reported paused; months | Material Transfer Agreement | About 100,000 | Strongest on content | Search results today; official site not read |
| 4 | Whitehall II accelerometer sub-study | Application to the study's data sharing committee plus signed agreement; months | Study access agreement | About 4,000 | Strong | Search results today; official site not read |
| 5 | MrOS and SOF wrist actigraphy | Free account plus click-through data use agreement; days | Data Use Agreement | About 3,000 men and 3,000 women | Partial | Today (home pages) |
| 6 | MESA Sleep actigraphy | NSRR request plus a separate BioLINCC application for outcomes; weeks | Per-dataset agreements | 2,237 | Partial | Search results and memory |

## Details

**1. NHANES 2011–2014** ([accelerometer documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))
- **Contents:** ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven 24-hour days, in a US national sample. Minute-level and raw 80 Hz files are public, with an algorithm-predicted wake/sleep/non-wear flag.
- **Outcomes:** deaths only, through 31 December 2019. The public mortality files replace follow-up time or cause of death with synthetic values for some records; vital status is unaltered.
- **What is missing:** no public hospital or diagnosis linkage. Unaltered mortality data need an approved project at the NCHS Research Data Center; Medicare and Medicaid linkage sits there too (from memory).
- **Steps:** download the accelerometer files for both cycles, download the mortality files, merge on the participant ID.
- **Shortcut:** an open [PhysioNet release](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) (CC0) provides minute-level step counts already derived from the raw data.
- **Used by:** [activity fragmentation and cause-specific mortality, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-29778-9).

**2. All of Us** ([CDR v8 release notes](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/30294451486356-Curated-Data-Repository-CDR-version-8-Release-Notes), [NIH research page](https://www.nih.gov/allofus/research))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate, activity and sleep stages, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Wearable data are in the Registered Tier.
- **What is missing:** no raw acceleration, and metrics come from Fitbit's proprietary algorithms. Device model is recorded for about 90% of donors, so filter to wrist models. Death capture is incomplete (from memory).
- **Steps:**
  1. Confirm your university has signed the Data Use and Registration Agreement.
  2. Register with identity verification.
  3. Complete the responsible conduct training and sign the code of conduct.
  4. Create a workspace with a public project description.
- **Conditions:** analysis happens only inside the cloud Workbench, with no participant-level downloads. Compute is billed after initial credits (from memory).
- **Used by:** [sleep patterns and chronic disease](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03155-8), [11 million days of Fitbit data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78529-2), [activity and chronic disease risk](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-025-01372-x).

**3. UK Biobank** ([apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2013–2015, with raw data, linked to hospital records and to cancer and death registries. This is the cohort most wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results say the analysis platform was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New project applications were still paused as of late October, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. Confirm this on the official page before planning.
- **Steps when open:** register in the Access Management System, submit a project application, have your institution sign the transfer agreement, and pay the fee.
- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.
- **Timing:** about 15 weeks was quoted for normal times. Analysis is on the cloud platform only.
- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.
- **Used by:** [the methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649), [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253), [step counts and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1249/mss.0000000000003478).

**4. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/our-research/mental-health-older-people/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, with 4,008 valid recordings in adults aged 60–83. Deaths come from the NHS register (633 deaths, followed to November 2023 in a 2025 paper), and diagnoses from hospital records.
- **What is missing:** it is an occupational cohort that is about three-quarters men. I could not confirm whether raw accelerometer files and linked hospital data are released to external applicants on the same terms as the core data.
- **Steps:** apply directly to the study team or through the Dementias Platform UK portal. The platform triages, the Whitehall II committee decides, and you sign the access agreement.
- **Used by:** [Whitehall II and UK Biobank mortality comparison](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30237-5), which is a ready template for cross-cohort comparability, and [activity and successful ageing](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep45772).

**5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** wrist actigraphy in older US men (about 5 days, 2003–2005) and older women, with long study-adjudicated follow-up for death, fractures and cardiovascular events.
- **What is missing:** these are count-based actigraphs from the early 2000s, so intensity metrics will not map onto modern raw-acceleration measures. I could not confirm whether epoch-level files are downloadable or what actigraphy SOF Online holds.
- **Steps:** register on each site and accept the data use agreement. Both home pages state: "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://doi.org/10.3109/07420520903419157), [incident diabetes](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc20-0557), [SOF and MrOS combined](https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igy023.363).

**6. MESA Sleep** ([NSRR page](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for seven days in 2010–2013, in a multi-ethnic US cohort; 2,159 people have epoch files.
- **What is missing:** cardiovascular events and deaths are not on NSRR. They need a separate BioLINCC application with an ethics determination and an institution-signed agreement (from memory).
- **Steps:** request the actigraphy from NSRR, apply to BioLINCC for the events data, and merge on the BioLINCC participant ID.

Check the [data access page](https://www.ckbiobank.org/data-access) for the release schedule; collaboration with the study team may be the only route.

- **German National Cohort (NAKO):** hip-worn, and applications were described as limited to researchers in EU countries.

- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** wrist actigraphy for a week, but only 1,887 people in the public epoch files and I found no outcome linkage.
- **CAPTURE-24 and similar activity-recognition sets:** open raw wrist data, but about 150 people and no outcomes.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Six datasets fit, but the best-known one, UK Biobank, appears to have paused new applications since April 2026, so NHANES (open today) and All of Us (days, if your university has an agreement in place) are where to start. I could not open the official UK Biobank, All of Us, Whitehall II or NSRR pages directly (they block automated readers), so their access terms below come from search results and memory, as marked.

## What I assumed you need

- **Wrist placement (must):** a research accelerometer or consumer tracker worn on the wrist.
- **Wear time (must):** free-living wear for several days to a week or longer.
- **Size (must):** at least a few thousand adults.
- **Outcomes (must):** linked deaths, hospital records or diagnoses after the wear period.
- **Access (must):** obtainable from a US university; applications are fine.
- **Activity and sleep (nice to have):** 24-hour wear with minute-level or raw data, so both can be derived.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NHANES 2011–2014 wrist accelerometry + public linked mortality files | Open download, minutes | No formal licence; NCHS data-use terms | 14,693 wearers of all ages; about 7,100 adults in a 2026 mortality paper | Strong, but deaths only | Today |
| 2 | All of Us Fitbit + health records | Institutional agreement, then individual registration and training; days if the agreement exists; cloud-only analysis | Data User Code of Conduct | More than 59,000 with wearable data | Strong, but consumer device with no raw signal | Search results today; official site not read |
| 3 | UK Biobank accelerometer sub-study | Application, institutional agreement and fee; new applications reported paused; months | Material Transfer Agreement | About 100,000 | Strongest on content | Search results today; official site not read |
| 4 | Whitehall II accelerometer sub-study | Application to the study's data sharing committee plus signed agreement; months | Study access agreement | About 4,000 | Strong | Search results today; official site not read |
| 5 | MrOS and SOF wrist actigraphy | Free account plus click-through data use agreement; days | Data Use Agreement | About 3,000 men and 3,000 women | Partial | Today (home pages) |
| 6 | MESA Sleep actigraphy | NSRR request plus a separate BioLINCC application for outcomes; weeks | Per-dataset agreements | 2,237 | Partial | Search results and memory |

## Details

**1. NHANES 2011–2014** ([accelerometer documentation](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2011/DataFiles/PAXMIN_G.htm), [linked mortality files](https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/linked-data/mortality-files/))
- **Contents:** ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven 24-hour days, in a US national sample. Minute-level and raw 80 Hz files are public, with an algorithm-predicted wake/sleep/non-wear flag.
- **Outcomes:** deaths only, through 31 December 2019. The public mortality files replace follow-up time or cause of death with synthetic values for some records; vital status is unaltered.
- **What is missing:** no public hospital or diagnosis linkage. Unaltered mortality data need an approved project at the NCHS Research Data Center; Medicare and Medicaid linkage sits there too (from memory).
- **Steps:** download the accelerometer files for both cycles, download the mortality files, merge on the participant ID.
- **Shortcut:** an open [PhysioNet release](https://physionet.org/content/minute-level-step-count-nhanes/1.0.2/) (CC0) provides minute-level step counts already derived from the raw data.
- **Used by:** [activity fragmentation and cause-specific mortality, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-29778-9).

**2. All of Us** ([CDR v8 release notes](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/30294451486356-Curated-Data-Repository-CDR-version-8-Release-Notes), [NIH research page](https://www.nih.gov/allofus/research))
- **Contents:** Fitbit steps, heart rate, activity and sleep stages, often over months or years, linked to health record diagnoses. Wearable data are in the Registered Tier.
- **What is missing:** no raw acceleration, and metrics come from Fitbit's proprietary algorithms. Device model is recorded for about 90% of donors, so filter to wrist models. Death capture is incomplete (from memory).
- **Steps:**
  1. Confirm your university has signed the Data Use and Registration Agreement.
  2. Register with identity verification.
  3. Complete the responsible conduct training and sign the code of conduct.
  4. Create a workspace with a public project description.
- **Conditions:** analysis happens only inside the cloud Workbench, with no participant-level downloads. Compute is billed after initial credits (from memory).
- **Used by:** [sleep patterns and chronic disease](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-03155-8), [11 million days of Fitbit data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78529-2), [activity and chronic disease risk](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43856-025-01372-x).

**3. UK Biobank** ([apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/))
- **Contents:** Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2013–2015, with raw data, linked to hospital records and to cancer and death registries. This is the cohort most wrist studies compare against.
- **Current status:** search results say the analysis platform was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data were found for sale. New project applications were still paused as of late October, with a "late 2026" target and no confirmed date. Confirm this on the official page before planning.
- **Steps when open:** register in the Access Management System, submit a project application, have your institution sign the transfer agreement, and pay the fee.
- **Fees:** search results cite £3,000 to £9,000 plus VAT for three years depending on tier, with a reduced student rate. I did not confirm which tier covers accelerometry.
- **Timing:** about 15 weeks was quoted for normal times. Analysis is on the cloud platform only.
- **Interim route:** ask whether a colleague already holds an approved project you could join. I could not confirm that additions are being processed during the pause.
- **Used by:** [the methods paper](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0169649), [sleep regularity and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1093/sleep/zsad253), [step counts and mortality](https://doi.org/10.1249/mss.0000000000003478).

**4. Whitehall II** ([data sharing page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/brain-sciences/psychiatry/our-research/mental-health-older-people/whitehall-ii/data-sharing))
- **Contents:** GENEActiv on the non-dominant wrist for nine days in 2012–2013, with 4,008 valid recordings in adults aged 60–83. Deaths come from the NHS register (633 deaths, followed to November 2023 in a 2025 paper), and diagnoses from hospital records.
- **What is missing:** it is an occupational cohort that is about three-quarters men. I could not confirm whether raw accelerometer files and linked hospital data are released to external applicants on the same terms as the core data.
- **Steps:** apply directly to the study team or through the Dementias Platform UK portal. The platform triages, the Whitehall II committee decides, and you sign the access agreement.
- **Used by:** [Whitehall II and UK Biobank mortality comparison](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30237-5), which is a ready template for cross-cohort comparability, and [activity and successful ageing](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep45772).

**5. MrOS and SOF** ([MrOS Online](https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/), [SOF Online](https://sofonline.ucsf.edu/))
- **Contents:** wrist actigraphy in older US men (about 5 days, 2003–2005) and older women, with long study-adjudicated follow-up for death, fractures and cardiovascular events.
- **What is missing:** these are count-based actigraphs from the early 2000s, so intensity metrics will not map onto modern raw-acceleration measures. I could not confirm whether epoch-level files are downloadable or what actigraphy SOF Online holds.
- **Steps:** register on each site and accept the data use agreement. Both home pages state: "You must have an account and accept the terms of a Data Use Agreement before you can download or explore clinical data."
- **Used by:** [rest-activity rhythms and mortality in MrOS](https://doi.org/10.3109/07420520903419157), [incident diabetes](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc20-0557), [SOF and MrOS combined](https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igy023.363).

**6. MESA Sleep** ([NSRR page](https://sleepdata.org/datasets/mesa))
- **Contents:** Actiwatch Spectrum on the wrist for seven days in 2010–2013, in a multi-ethnic US cohort; 2,159 people have epoch files.
- **What is missing:** cardiovascular events and deaths are not on NSRR. They need a separate BioLINCC application with an ethics determination and an institution-signed agreement (from memory).
- **Steps:** request the actigraphy from NSRR, apply to BioLINCC for the events data, and merge on the BioLINCC participant ID.

## Known, not confirmed

- **China Kadoorie Biobank, third resurvey:** about 20,000 adults wore an Axivity AX3 on the wrist for seven days in 2020–2021 ([description paper](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12966-023-01537-8)). The open-access policy I found covers baseline, the first two resurveys and disease follow-up, not this resurvey. Check the [data access page](https://www.ckbiobank.org/data-access) for the release schedule; collaboration with the study team may be the only route.
- **Rotterdam Study:** wrist actigraphy with mortality follow-up in 1,734 people ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwu245)). From memory, data go by request to the study's management team and export is restricted. I did not confirm the procedure or any later, larger wave.
- **CoLaus|PsyCoLaus (Lausanne):** from memory, about 2,900 adults with 14 days of wrist GENEActiv. It was used as the external validation cohort for a Whitehall II mortality model. Access is by request to the study's committee, not confirmed.

## Not recommended, and why

- **NHANES 2003–2006:** open with long mortality follow-up, but the device was hip-worn.
- **German National Cohort (NAKO):** hip-worn, and applications were described as limited to researchers in EU countries.
- **WHI OPACH, Women's Health Study, REGARDS:** large US cohorts with outcomes, but hip-worn (from memory).
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** wrist actigraphy for a week, but only 1,887 people in the public epoch files and I found no outcome linkage.
- **CAPTURE-24 and similar activity-recognition sets:** open raw wrist data, but about 150 people and no outcomes.

## What I could not find

- No dataset accessible now pairs raw wrist accelerometry with hospital-record linkage at UK Biobank scale. NHANES has deaths only in its public files; All of Us has diagnoses but no raw signal.
- Registry searches returned almost only paper supplements and unrelated datasets; everything above came from the literature and study portals.

## Next step

Download NHANES today and build your pipeline on it. In parallel, ask your research office whether the All of Us agreement is signed, and send the Whitehall II application, since it is the slowest. Check the UK Biobank application page for a reopening date, and ask your institution early whether these secondary analyses need an ethics exemption.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-JDr6IM/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`. Checked 12 November 2026.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
For your design, three datasets do most of the work: NHANES 2011–2014 (usable today), UK Biobank (the field's reference dataset, but access is suspended right now), and All of Us (the only large tracker-based option). I checked access terms on the web today; items marked "from memory" I did not re-verify.

## Main options

| Dataset | Wrist device and wear | Size | Linked outcomes | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NHANES 2011–2014** | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, 7 days, 24 h | About 7,600 adults with valid wear | Deaths via National Death Index through 31 Dec 2019 | Public download, no application |
| **UK Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2013–15) | About 100,000 adults (from memory) | Hospital records, cancer and death registries | Paid application; currently on hold |
| **All of Us** | Participants' Fitbits, often months to years | About 59,000 with Fitbit data; roughly 22,000–29,000 also have health records | Electronic health records; deaths only from those records | Institutional agreement, free |
| **Whitehall II** | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days (2012–13) | About 4,200, aged 60–83 | NHS mortality register through 2024; hospital records | Application to UCL |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2020–21) | About 20,000–21,000 | Death and hospitalisation records (from memory) | Application; release status unconfirmed |

## What access involves

- **NHANES:** Download the minute-level files (PAXMIN) and the public-use linked mortality file from CDC.
  - The public mortality file has perturbed follow-up values for some records and limited cause-of-death detail.
  - Full mortality detail and Medicare/Medicaid linkage need a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center, with fees and on-site or remote enclave analysis (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** Normally you register, submit a project application, have your institution sign a Material Transfer Agreement, and pay.
  - Fees are £3,000 for three years at Tier 1, plus VAT and cloud compute; analysis runs only on their cloud platform. I could not confirm which tier covers the accelerometer data.
  - Access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data appeared for sale. New applications are on hold, with "late 2026" targeted for reopening and no firm date.
  - Approval took about 15 weeks on average before the suspension.
- **All of Us:** Your university signs a Data Use and Registration Agreement (many US universities already have one). You then verify your identity, complete training, and work in the Researcher Workbench.
  - Access is free, with $300 in initial compute credits.
  - Fitbit owners are a self-selected group, the measures are consumer-device outputs rather than raw acceleration, and deaths are under-counted.
- **Whitehall II:** Submit a data-sharing application to the UCL study team. I did not confirm whether linked hospital records are released to external applicants.
- **China Kadoorie Biobank:** Apply through the CKB Data Access System. I could not confirm that the accelerometer data are released yet, and follow-up since 2020–21 is short.

## Smaller or narrower cohorts

- **MrOS and SOF:** About 3,000 older men and about 3,000 older women (SOF from memory) with wrist actigraphy. MrOS wear was only 3–5 days. Deaths and events come from cohort follow-up rather than records, and data are free through MrOS Online and SOF Online after registration and a data use agreement.
- **Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966:** About 5,500 people wore a wrist Polar Active for two weeks at age 46, linked to Finnish national registers. Access is by request to the University of Oulu with a Data Transfer Agreement. The cohort is still young, so events are few.
- **MESA Sleep and CoLaus:** Each has roughly 2,000–3,000 participants with wrist devices and adjudicated events (from memory). MESA goes through NSRR and BioLINCC; CoLaus is by collaboration request.

Many well-known accelerometer cohorts used hip or thigh devices and don't fit your requirement, including NHANES 2003–2006, the Women's Health Study, REGARDS and HUNT4.

## Recommendation

Start on NHANES now, since it needs no approval and uses a research-grade wrist device. Prepare a UK Biobank application to submit when applications reopen, because most published wrist-based outcome studies use it. Add All of Us if you want long-duration tracker data and can live with the weaker death ascertainment.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NHANES 2011–2014** | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, 7 days, 24 h | About 7,600 adults with valid wear | Deaths via National Death Index through 31 Dec 2019 | Public download, no application |
| **UK Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2013–15) | About 100,000 adults (from memory) | Hospital records, cancer and death registries | Paid application; currently on hold |
| **All of Us** | Participants' Fitbits, often months to years | About 59,000 with Fitbit data; roughly 22,000–29,000 also have health records | Electronic health records; deaths only from those records | Institutional agreement, free |
| **Whitehall II** | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days (2012–13) | About 4,200, aged 60–83 | NHS mortality register through 2024; hospital records | Application to UCL |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days (2020–21) | About 20,000–21,000 | Death and hospitalisation records (from memory) | Application; release status unconfirmed |

## What access involves

- **NHANES:** Download the minute-level files (PAXMIN) and the public-use linked mortality file from CDC.
  - The public mortality file has perturbed follow-up values for some records and limited cause-of-death detail.
  - Full mortality detail and Medicare/Medicaid linkage need a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center, with fees and on-site or remote enclave analysis (from memory).
- **UK Biobank:** Normally you register, submit a project application, have your institution sign a Material Transfer Agreement, and pay.
  - Fees are £3,000 for three years at Tier 1, plus VAT and cloud compute; analysis runs only on their cloud platform. I could not confirm which tier covers the accelerometer data.
  - Access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported data appeared for sale. New applications are on hold, with "late 2026" targeted for reopening and no firm date.
  - Approval took about 15 weeks on average before the suspension.
- **All of Us:** Your university signs a Data Use and Registration Agreement (many US universities already have one). You then verify your identity, complete training, and work in the Researcher Workbench.
  - Access is free, with $300 in initial compute credits.
  - Fitbit owners are a self-selected group, the measures are consumer-device outputs rather than raw acceleration, and deaths are under-counted.
- **Whitehall II:** Submit a data-sharing application to the UCL study team. I did not confirm whether linked hospital records are released to external applicants.
- **China Kadoorie Biobank:** Apply through the CKB Data Access System. I could not confirm that the accelerometer data are released yet, and follow-up since 2020–21 is short.

## Smaller or narrower cohorts

- **MrOS and SOF:** About 3,000 older men and about 3,000 older women (SOF from memory) with wrist actigraphy. MrOS wear was only 3–5 days. Deaths and events come from cohort follow-up rather than records, and data are free through MrOS Online and SOF Online after registration and a data use agreement.
- **Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966:** About 5,500 people wore a wrist Polar Active for two weeks at age 46, linked to Finnish national registers. Access is by request to the University of Oulu with a Data Transfer Agreement. The cohort is still young, so events are few.
- **MESA Sleep and CoLaus:** Each has roughly 2,000–3,000 participants with wrist devices and adjudicated events (from memory). MESA goes through NSRR and BioLINCC; CoLaus is by collaboration request.

Many well-known accelerometer cohorts used hip or thigh devices and don't fit your requirement, including NHANES 2003–2006, the Women's Health Study, REGARDS and HUNT4.

## Recommendation

Start on NHANES now, since it needs no approval and uses a research-grade wrist device. Prepare a UK Biobank application to submit when applications reopen, because most published wrist-based outcome studies use it. Add All of Us if you want long-duration tracker data and can live with the weaker death ascertainment.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four datasets fit your criteria well, and the most obvious one, UK Biobank, is not taking new applications right now. NHANES and All of Us are the ones you can start on today.

| Dataset | Wrist device and wear | Size | Linked outcomes | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UK Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days | ~100,000 (from memory) | Hospital, cancer and death registries | New applications paused |
| **NHANES 2011–2014** (US) | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, up to 7 full days | 13,603 with minute-level data (includes children) | Deaths only, via the National Death Index | Open download |
| **All of Us** (US) | Participants' own Fitbits, long-running records | 68,000+ in the 2026 release | Electronic health records | Registration, no project review |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days | 20,370 | Death and hospital records | Application; accelerometer release unconfirmed |
| **Whitehall II** (UK) | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days | 4,204 | Hospital records and deaths | Application via Dementias Platform UK |

**UK Biobank**
- **Status:** Researcher access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported participant data were found for sale online. New applications were targeted to reopen in "late 2026", and I found no confirmation that they have.
- **Cost:** The tier that covers linked health records is £3,000 for three years, plus cloud compute. I could not confirm which tier the accelerometer data sit in.
- **Process:** Analysis is only on its cloud platform, and about 15 weeks typically pass from application to data. Expect tighter export rules on reopening.
- **Caveat:** I could not open the official pages directly, so the status comes from search summaries of them; check the Apply for access page.

**NHANES 2011–2014**
- **Access:** Both the accelerometer files (raw 80 Hz and minute-level summaries) and the public mortality file are free downloads with no application.
- **Follow-up:** Public mortality follow-up runs to 31 December 2019, for adults only.
- **Limits:** The public file perturbs some follow-up times and causes of death. The unaltered files require a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center. There is no disease incidence linkage.

**All of Us**
- **Access:** Your university signs a data use agreement (many already have), then you verify your identity and complete training. Analysis is in its cloud workbench, and you pay for compute.
- **Limits:** Fitbit owners are self-selected, device data are processed by Fitbit's proprietary algorithms, and death capture is incomplete. This makes it the least comparable to research-grade wrist studies.

**China Kadoorie Biobank**
- **Access:** You apply to the Oxford team, and your institution contracts with the University of Oxford. The fee is £2,500 per approved request for researchers outside mainland China and Hong Kong.
- **Limits:** The accelerometer data come from the 2020–2021 resurvey, and I could not confirm they are released to external researchers yet. Email ckbaccess@ndph.ox.ac.uk before planning around it. Follow-up after wear is still short.

**Whitehall II**
- **Access:** Requests are triaged by Dementias Platform UK and then reviewed by the study's data sharing committee.
- **Follow-up:** A recent analysis followed participants to August 2024.
- **Limits:** Participants were aged 60–83 at wear and are all civil servants. I could not confirm fees, timelines, or whether raw files are available.

**Smaller sleep-focused options**
- **MESA Sleep:** 2,237 adults with a week of wrist actigraphy. The actigraphy is at the National Sleep Research Resource, and cardiovascular events need a separate request to NHLBI's BioLINCC repository.
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** About a week of wrist actigraphy in US Hispanic/Latino adults (roughly 2,200, from memory), through the same two repositories.
- **MrOS Sleep:** 3,135 older men, but only 3–5 days of wear, and the actigraphy requires an analysis proposal to the coordinating center.

I left out cohorts that used hip or thigh devices (for example Women's Health Study, REGARDS, HUNT4), since they would break your comparability requirement.

My recommendation: start with NHANES for mortality now, register for All of Us in parallel, and prepare a UK Biobank application to submit when the pause lifts, since it is the main comparator for wrist-based outcome studies.

- [UK Biobank apply for access](https://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/use-our-data/apply-for-access/)

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Four datasets fit your criteria well, and the most obvious one, UK Biobank, is not taking new applications right now. NHANES and All of Us are the ones you can start on today.

| Dataset | Wrist device and wear | Size | Linked outcomes | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UK Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days | ~100,000 (from memory) | Hospital, cancer and death registries | New applications paused |
| **NHANES 2011–2014** (US) | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, up to 7 full days | 13,603 with minute-level data (includes children) | Deaths only, via the National Death Index | Open download |
| **All of Us** (US) | Participants' own Fitbits, long-running records | 68,000+ in the 2026 release | Electronic health records | Registration, no project review |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days | 20,370 | Death and hospital records | Application; accelerometer release unconfirmed |
| **Whitehall II** (UK) | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days | 4,204 | Hospital records and deaths | Application via Dementias Platform UK |

**UK Biobank**
- **Status:** Researcher access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported participant data were found for sale online. New applications were targeted to reopen in "late 2026", and I found no confirmation that they have.
- **Cost:** The tier that covers linked health records is £3,000 for three years, plus cloud compute. I could not confirm which tier the accelerometer data sit in.
- **Process:** Analysis is only on its cloud platform, and about 15 weeks typically pass from application to data. Expect tighter export rules on reopening.
- **Caveat:** I could not open the official pages directly, so the status comes from search summaries of them; check the Apply for access page.

**NHANES 2011–2014**
- **Access:** Both the accelerometer files (raw 80 Hz and minute-level summaries) and the public mortality file are free downloads with no application.
- **Follow-up:** Public mortality follow-up runs to 31 December 2019, for adults only.
- **Limits:** The public file perturbs some follow-up times and causes of death. The unaltered files require a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center. There is no disease incidence linkage.

**All of Us**
- **Access:** Your university signs a data use agreement (many already have), then you verify your identity and complete training. Analysis is in its cloud workbench, and you pay for compute.
- **Limits:** Fitbit owners are self-selected, device data are processed by Fitbit's proprietary algorithms, and death capture is incomplete. This makes it the least comparable to research-grade wrist studies.

**China Kadoorie Biobank**
- **Access:** You apply to the Oxford team, and your institution contracts with the University of Oxford. The fee is £2,500 per approved request for researchers outside mainland China and Hong Kong.
- **Limits:** The accelerometer data come from the 2020–2021 resurvey, and I could not confirm they are released to external researchers yet. Email ckbaccess@ndph.ox.ac.uk before planning around it. Follow-up after wear is still short.

**Whitehall II**
- **Access:** Requests are triaged by Dementias Platform UK and then reviewed by the study's data sharing committee.
- **Follow-up:** A recent analysis followed participants to August 2024.
- **Limits:** Participants were aged 60–83 at wear and are all civil servants. I could not confirm fees, timelines, or whether raw files are available.

**Smaller sleep-focused options**
- **MESA Sleep:** 2,237 adults with a week of wrist actigraphy. The actigraphy is at the National Sleep Research Resource, and cardiovascular events need a separate request to NHLBI's BioLINCC repository.
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** About a week of wrist actigraphy in US Hispanic/Latino adults (roughly 2,200, from memory), through the same two repositories.
- **MrOS Sleep:** 3,135 older men, but only 3–5 days of wear, and the actigraphy requires an analysis proposal to the coordinating center.

I left out cohorts that used hip or thigh devices (for example Women's Health Study, REGARDS, HUNT4), since they would break your comparability requirement.

My recommendation: start with NHANES for mortality now, register for All of Us in parallel, and prepare a UK Biobank application to submit when the pause lifts, since it is the main comparator for wrist-based outcome studies.

| **NHANES 2011–2014** (US) | ActiGraph GT3X+, non-dominant wrist, up to 7 full days | 13,603 with minute-level data (includes children) | Deaths only, via the National Death Index | Open download |
| **All of Us** (US) | Participants' own Fitbits, long-running records | 68,000+ in the 2026 release | Electronic health records | Registration, no project review |
| **China Kadoorie Biobank** | Axivity AX3, 7 days | 20,370 | Death and hospital records | Application; accelerometer release unconfirmed |
| **Whitehall II** (UK) | GENEActiv, non-dominant wrist, 9 days | 4,204 | Hospital records and deaths | Application via Dementias Platform UK |

**UK Biobank**
- **Status:** Researcher access was suspended on 23 April 2026 after exported participant data were found for sale online. New applications were targeted to reopen in "late 2026", and I found no confirmation that they have.
- **Cost:** The tier that covers linked health records is £3,000 for three years, plus cloud compute. I could not confirm which tier the accelerometer data sit in.
- **Process:** Analysis is only on its cloud platform, and about 15 weeks typically pass from application to data. Expect tighter export rules on reopening.
- **Caveat:** I could not open the official pages directly, so the status comes from search summaries of them; check the Apply for access page.

**NHANES 2011–2014**
- **Access:** Both the accelerometer files (raw 80 Hz and minute-level summaries) and the public mortality file are free downloads with no application.
- **Follow-up:** Public mortality follow-up runs to 31 December 2019, for adults only.
- **Limits:** The public file perturbs some follow-up times and causes of death. The unaltered files require a proposal to the NCHS Research Data Center. There is no disease incidence linkage.

**All of Us**
- **Access:** Your university signs a data use agreement (many already have), then you verify your identity and complete training. Analysis is in its cloud workbench, and you pay for compute.
- **Limits:** Fitbit owners are self-selected, device data are processed by Fitbit's proprietary algorithms, and death capture is incomplete. This makes it the least comparable to research-grade wrist studies.

**China Kadoorie Biobank**
- **Access:** You apply to the Oxford team, and your institution contracts with the University of Oxford. The fee is £2,500 per approved request for researchers outside mainland China and Hong Kong.
- **Limits:** The accelerometer data come from the 2020–2021 resurvey, and I could not confirm they are released to external researchers yet. Email ckbaccess@ndph.ox.ac.uk before planning around it. Follow-up after wear is still short.

**Whitehall II**
- **Access:** Requests are triaged by Dementias Platform UK and then reviewed by the study's data sharing committee.
- **Follow-up:** A recent analysis followed participants to August 2024.
- **Limits:** Participants were aged 60–83 at wear and are all civil servants. I could not confirm fees, timelines, or whether raw files are available.

**Smaller sleep-focused options**
- **MESA Sleep:** 2,237 adults with a week of wrist actigraphy. The actigraphy is at the National Sleep Research Resource, and cardiovascular events need a separate request to NHLBI's BioLINCC repository.
- **HCHS/SOL Sueño:** About a week of wrist actigraphy in US Hispanic/Latino adults (roughly 2,200, from memory), through the same two repositories.
- **MrOS Sleep:** 3,135 older men, but only 3–5 days of wear, and the actigraphy requires an analysis proposal to the coordinating center.

I left out cohorts that used hip or thigh devices (for example Women's Health Study, REGARDS, HUNT4), since they would break your comparability requirement.

My recommendation: start with NHANES for mortality now, register for All of Us in parallel, and prepare a UK Biobank application to submit when the pause lifts, since it is the main comparator for wrist-based outcome studies.

Prompt

I want to study whether physical activity and sleep patterns measured in daily life by wrist-worn accelerometers or activity trackers predict later disease and death. I need data from at least a few thousand adults who wore the device on the wrist for several days to a week or longer, linked to follow-up outcomes such as hospital records, diagnoses or death registrations. Wrist placement matters to me because I want my results to be comparable with other wrist-based studies. I'm at a US university and happy to go through applications. Which datasets should I consider, and what does getting access involve for each?

Recommending "NHANES accelerometry" without naming the cycle also counts, unless the answer points only to the 2003-2006 cycles. 03-recall-allofus-fitbitllm

04-access-ukbiobank-applicationllm

Mentioning the approved application is enough; the analysis platform and any fees are optional details. 05-access-allofus-durallm

Wording such as "your institution must have an agreement with All of Us" passes. FAIL if the answer does not mention All of Us at all, or says or implies that the data can be downloaded freely, or describes access without any indication that an institutional agreement is required.

06-access-nhanes-downloadllm

07-trap-nhanes-hipllm

PASS if the final answer does not present the NHANES 2003-2004 and 2005-2006 accelerometer data as wrist-worn data. The user needs wrist-worn devices; in those NHANES cycles the ActiGraph monitor was worn on an elasticized belt on the right hip, whereas only the 2011-2014 cycles used wrist-worn monitors. Not mentioning the 2003-2006 cycles passes; mentioning them while making clear they were hip-worn (or are not wrist data) passes; recommending NHANES accelerometry in general or the 2011-2014 cycles passes. FAIL if the answer states or implies that the 2003-2006 NHANES accelerometers were worn on the wrist, or recommends the 2003-2006 accelerometer data as meeting the wrist requirement without noting the hip placement.

08-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends at least one of the following as a candidate dataset: (a) the MrOS Sleep Study actigraphy data (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study; wrist actigraphy in about 3,000 older men with mortality follow-up); (b) the Study of Osteoporotic Fractures (SOF) actigraphy data (wrist actigraphy in about 3,000 older women with adjudicated mortality follow-up). FAIL if it recommends neither of them.

Nothing I found is a ready-made open file that fully fits, but two options are close to immediate: the Veneto Workers Histories (a signed form, likely days) and Chile's public unemployment-insurance samples (public release, though I could not open the download page today). Everything else takes an institution-signed application and weeks to months. All access facts below were checked on 12 November 2026 unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need

- **R1 (must):** a worker identifier plus an employer identifier shared across workers.
- **R2 (must):** workers followed across employers for 10+ years.
- **R3 (must):** earnings per job and period.
- **R4 (important for your question):** all or most coworkers observed in each firm. A within/between-firm variance split needs firm-level wage distributions, and files that sample *workers* (Spain, Chile, France, UK) show only one or two people in most firms.
- **R5 (nice to have):** reachable by a PhD student without residence or a co-author in the country.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence / terms | Size and span | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Veneto Workers Histories (Italy) | Signed form e-mailed to the foundation; likely days | Citation requirement; form terms not read | All private-sector firms and workers in the covered area, 1975–2001 | Strong, but ends 2001 | Today |
| 2 | SIEED (Germany, IAB) | Institutional agreement, on-site then remote execution; 1–3 months | Data use agreement | 1% of establishments, all their workers, 1975–2023 | Strong | Today |
| 3 | MCVL (Spain) | Application by your institution; weeks (from memory) | Non-commercial research, credit and send outputs | About 4% of individuals (from memory), full histories | Partial (worker sample) | Today |
| 4 | Seguro de Cesantía samples (Chile) | Public download per the regulator's press releases; minutes if the page works | None stated | 3%, 5% or 12% of affiliates, 2002 onward | Partial (worker sample) | Partly: download page failed |
| 5 | Quadros de Pessoal via BPLIM (Portugal) | Application plus confidentiality agreement; may need a Banco de Portugal co-author; months | Scientific use only, no fee | Universe of firms and employees, mid-1980s onward (from memory) | Strong | Access today, content from memory |
| 6 | Panel tous salariés (France, CASD) | Committee approval, institutional contract, paid secure terminal; months | Contract with CASD | 1/24 of workers to 2001, 1976–2022 | Partial (worker sample) | Today |
| 7 | LEHD (US Census) | Proposal, background check, secure data centre; 6–12 months | Title 13/26 confidentiality | Near-universe of US jobs | Strong | Today, timeline from search |
| 8 | RAIS identificada (Brazil) | Cooperation agreement between an institution and the ministry; months | Confidentiality term per user | Universe of formal jobs | Strong | Today (via search) |
| 9 | LIAB longitudinal (Germany, IAB) | As SIEED | Data use agreement | 1975–2024 | Partial | Today |
| 10 | Admin3 (Hungary, KRTK) | Only with a KRTK co-author or supervisor | Server access only | Population sample, 2003–2017 | Partial | Today (via search) |
| 11 | ASHE (UK) | Accredited researcher, secure lab; months | Secure access | 1% of employees, 1997–2025 | Partial (worker sample) | Search only; checker could not read the catalogue |

## Details

**1. [Veneto Workers Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**
- **Contents:** three Stata files (workers, firms, yearly contribution records) from Italian social-security archives, 1975–2001.
- **Access:** the page says "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". [Arellano-Bover's user notes](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources) say a copy "can easily be obtained" this way.
- **Gaps:** it ends in 2001, so it covers a historical rise in inequality only. The foundation's page says the provinces of Treviso and Vicenza, while papers describe the whole Veneto region; ask which extract you get. The page does not list earnings variables (from memory: annual earnings and days or weeks paid per job).
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494) for bias-corrected AKM variance decompositions, and [Card, Devicienti and Maida](https://davidcard.berkeley.edu/papers/RESTUD-2014.pdf).

**2. [SIEED 7523](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/the-sample-of-integrated-employer-employee-data-sieed-sieed-7523-version-1/)**
- **Why it fits:** it holds "the entire employment biographies of all people ever employed in the sampled establishments", so whole workforces are visible.
- **Access** ([on-site use page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/)): a request form, a check that "could take up to one month", then a use agreement signed by your institution. For thesis work "the supervising chair must submit the application".
- **Where you work:** on site at a guest location (Germany, USA, Canada, UK), then by submitting code remotely. Remote desktop is limited to institutions in Germany. No fee is mentioned.
- **Gaps:** wages are top-coded at the social-security ceiling and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Used by:** [Card, Heining and Kline (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjt006), which is the template for your question on the same underlying data.

**3. [MCVL](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)**
- **Contents:** anonymised Spanish social-security histories, with each spell tied to an employer's contribution account code and monthly contribution bases.
- **Access:** open to "instituciones públicas y privadas que lo soliciten" for non-commercial research. Your university submits the form and researcher sheet, and the social-security directorate approves.
- **Gaps:** contribution bases are capped unless you take the tax-data version (from memory). Whether non-Spanish universities qualify is not stated on the page; from memory, foreign universities have obtained it.
- **Also there:** the same portal lists a firm–worker panel (PET) that I did not check and that may suit R4 better.

**4. [Chile Seguro de Cesantía samples](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-7521.html)**
- **Contents:** monthly contribution histories for sampled affiliates, with workers and employers under consistent anonymous numbers. The regulator's 2024 public account says the samples were refreshed that year.
- **Access:** the regulator says the samples are "a disposición del público" on its website. The download link in its press releases returned a 404 to my client, so open spensiones.cl in a browser and look under statistics and databases.
- **Gaps:** earnings are capped at the contribution ceiling, and early years cover only contracts started after 2002 (both from memory). Confirm the employer identifier in the variable dictionary before building on it.

**5. [Quadros de Pessoal via BPLIM](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)**
- **Access:** application form, project description, CV and a confidentiality agreement that your supervisor also signs. You work remotely on perturbed data and staff run the final code.
- **Catch:** a 2018 version of the lab's guide says this dataset is limited to Banco de Portugal researchers and their co-authors. Check the current Guide for Researchers before investing time.

**6. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- **Access:** apply through the confidential data access portal, get the producer's agreement and the Statistical Secrecy Committee's approval ([procedure](https://www.casd.eu/en/your-project/procedures-dhabilitation/)). Your institution's legal representative then signs a contract and pays for the secure terminal ([price list](https://www.casd.eu/en/tarifs-2/)).
- **Gaps:** I did not capture the fee amounts.

**7. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html)**
- **Access:** "researchers must have an approved project" and all work happens in a Federal Statistical Research Data Center.
- **Conditions (from data-centre slide decks found by search, 2018–2025):** advisor as co-principal investigator, about 4–6 months to approval and longer with tax-agency review, and US residency for 3 of the last 5 years.

**8. [RAIS identificada](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)**
- **Access:** requires a cooperation agreement between an institution and the labour ministry, plus a confidentiality term per user. The realistic route is a Brazilian co-author or host whose institution already has one.

**9–11.**
- **[LIAB](https://doi.org/10.5164/iab.liablm7524.de.en.v1):** same procedure as SIEED. Its page says full biographies of all employees are provided only "for establishments with up to 49 employees", so prefer SIEED unless you need the establishment survey.
- **[Admin3](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/):** open only to KRTK staff, their co-authors and students they supervise.
- **[ASHE](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689):** needs UK accredited-researcher status and an approved project; from memory, access is from within the UK only.

## Known, not confirmed

- **LoSaI (Italy, national social-security worker sample, 1985 onward):** a labour-ministry [research proposal form](https://www.lavoro.gov.it/documenti-e-norme/studi-e-statistiche/Documents/Microdati%20per%20la%20ricerca/ALLEGATO3-microdati.pdf) exists, signed by the lead researcher and a recognised research body. I could not confirm that it carries a firm identifier; check the record layout.
- **VisitINPS (Italy, full social-security archives):** competitive programme with on-site work in Rome (from memory).
- **Austria (social-security database), Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Netherlands, Canada:** all have full-population linked registers (from memory). Access generally needs an affiliation or co-author at an approved institution in the country, often with fees. I did not check any of their pages today.
- **Cross-country overview:** [Boza and Pető (2025)](https://kti.krtk.hu/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/KRTKKTIWP202502.pdf) review linked employer-employee panels in 33 countries, with an appendix table on access for the European ones. I found it but did not read it.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Public RAIS files (Brazil):** open, but identifiers are removed, so workers cannot be followed.
- **[GRAPH-EE](https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-858769) (UK, 2007–2023):** open worker–firm panel built from web profiles; its description mentions no wage data.
- **[Synthetic Workplace and Employee Survey](https://doi.org/10.5683/sp3/abotie) (Canada):** open but synthetic, and each worker is followed for two years only (from memory).
- **US tax-record studies (Song et al.; [Lamadon, Mogstad and Setzler](https://doi.org/10.3886/e146661v1)):** the replication package is public, but from memory it has code and no microdata, and outsiders cannot request the records.
- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP:** no employer identifier shared across respondents (from memory).
- **EU Structure of Earnings Survey:** repeated cross-sections, no worker panel (from memory).

## What I could not find

- No open file combines worker and firm identifiers, uncapped earnings, whole firm workforces and recent years.
- The Chilean download page and variable dictionary could not be opened.
- Registry searches (DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo, Hugging Face) returned almost nothing relevant beyond the German records, so most of this comes from the data owners' own pages.

## Next step

1. **This week:** send the Veneto form to info@frdb.org and try the Chilean download in a browser.
2. **Meanwhile:** build and test your AKM pipeline on simulated panels with [BipartitePandas / PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway), and on the free SIEED test data. The test data are random, so they are for code only.
3. **In parallel:** ask your advisor to start the German application for SIEED, since it is the best fit for a modern within/between-firm decomposition and the paperwork must come from the supervising chair.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-1FMVJG/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **Gaps:** contribution bases are capped unless you take the tax-data version (from memory). Whether non-Spanish universities qualify is not stated on the page; from memory, foreign universities have obtained it.
- **Also there:** the same portal lists a firm–worker panel (PET) that I did not check and that may suit R4 better.

**4. [Chile Seguro de Cesantía samples](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-7521.html)**
- **Contents:** monthly contribution histories for sampled affiliates, with workers and employers under consistent anonymous numbers. The regulator's 2024 public account says the samples were refreshed that year.
- **Access:** the regulator says the samples are "a disposición del público" on its website. The download link in its press releases returned a 404 to my client, so open spensiones.cl in a browser and look under statistics and databases.
- **Gaps:** earnings are capped at the contribution ceiling, and early years cover only contracts started after 2002 (both from memory). Confirm the employer identifier in the variable dictionary before building on it.

**5. [Quadros de Pessoal via BPLIM](https://bplim.bportugal.pt/content/access-0)**
- **Access:** application form, project description, CV and a confidentiality agreement that your supervisor also signs. You work remotely on perturbed data and staff run the final code.
- **Catch:** a 2018 version of the lab's guide says this dataset is limited to Banco de Portugal researchers and their co-authors. Check the current Guide for Researchers before investing time.

**6. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- **Access:** apply through the confidential data access portal, get the producer's agreement and the Statistical Secrecy Committee's approval ([procedure](https://www.casd.eu/en/your-project/procedures-dhabilitation/)). Your institution's legal representative then signs a contract and pays for the secure terminal ([price list](https://www.casd.eu/en/tarifs-2/)).
- **Gaps:** I did not capture the fee amounts.

**7. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html)**
- **Access:** "researchers must have an approved project" and all work happens in a Federal Statistical Research Data Center.
- **Conditions (from data-centre slide decks found by search, 2018–2025):** advisor as co-principal investigator, about 4–6 months to approval and longer with tax-agency review, and US residency for 3 of the last 5 years.

**8. [RAIS identificada](https://www.gov.br/pt-br/servicos/solicitar-acesso-aos-dados-identificados-rais-e-caged)**
- **Access:** requires a cooperation agreement between an institution and the labour ministry, plus a confidentiality term per user. The realistic route is a Brazilian co-author or host whose institution already has one.

**9–11.**
- **[LIAB](https://doi.org/10.5164/iab.liablm7524.de.en.v1):** same procedure as SIEED. Its page says full biographies of all employees are provided only "for establishments with up to 49 employees", so prefer SIEED unless you need the establishment survey.
- **[Admin3](https://adatbank.krtk.mta.hu/en/2020/02/):** open only to KRTK staff, their co-authors and students they supervise.
- **[ASHE](https://datacatalogue.ukdataservice.ac.uk/studies/study/6689):** needs UK accredited-researcher status and an approved project; from memory, access is from within the UK only.

## Known, not confirmed

- **LoSaI (Italy, national social-security worker sample, 1985 onward):** a labour-ministry [research proposal form](https://www.lavoro.gov.it/documenti-e-norme/studi-e-statistiche/Documents/Microdati%20per%20la%20ricerca/ALLEGATO3-microdati.pdf) exists, signed by the lead researcher and a recognised research body. I could not confirm that it carries a firm identifier; check the record layout.
- **VisitINPS (Italy, full social-security archives):** competitive programme with on-site work in Rome (from memory).
- **Austria (social-security database), Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Netherlands, Canada:** all have full-population linked registers (from memory). Access generally needs an affiliation or co-author at an approved institution in the country, often with fees. I did not check any of their pages today.
- **Cross-country overview:** [Boza and Pető (2025)](https://kti.krtk.hu/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/KRTKKTIWP202502.pdf) review linked employer-employee panels in 33 countries, with an appendix table on access for the European ones. I found it but did not read it.

## Not recommended, and why

- **Public RAIS files (Brazil):** open, but identifiers are removed, so workers cannot be followed.
- **[GRAPH-EE](https://doi.org/10.5255/ukda-sn-858769) (UK, 2007–2023):** open worker–firm panel built from web profiles; its description mentions no wage data.
- **[Synthetic Workplace and Employee Survey](https://doi.org/10.5683/sp3/abotie) (Canada):** open but synthetic, and each worker is followed for two years only (from memory).
- **US tax-record studies (Song et al.; [Lamadon, Mogstad and Setzler](https://doi.org/10.3886/e146661v1)):** the replication package is public, but from memory it has code and no microdata, and outsiders cannot request the records.
- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP:** no employer identifier shared across respondents (from memory).
- **EU Structure of Earnings Survey:** repeated cross-sections, no worker panel (from memory).

## What I could not find

- No open file combines worker and firm identifiers, uncapped earnings, whole firm workforces and recent years.
- The Chilean download page and variable dictionary could not be opened.
- Registry searches (DataCite, OpenAIRE, Zenodo, Hugging Face) returned almost nothing relevant beyond the German records, so most of this comes from the data owners' own pages.

## Next step

1. **This week:** send the Veneto form to info@frdb.org and try the Chilean download in a browser.
2. **Meanwhile:** build and test your AKM pipeline on simulated panels with [BipartitePandas / PyTwoWay](https://github.com/tlamadon/pytwoway), and on the free SIEED test data. The test data are random, so they are for code only.
3. **In parallel:** ask your advisor to start the German application for SIEED, since it is the best fit for a modern within/between-firm decomposition and the paperwork must come from the supervising chair.

The interactive shortlist, with filters and an exportable access plan, is at `/private/tmp/e-1FMVJG/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP:** no employer identifier shared across respondents (from memory).
- **EU Structure of Earnings Survey:** repeated cross-sections, no worker panel (from memory).

- No open file combines worker and firm identifiers, uncapped earnings, whole firm workforces and recent years.

3. **In parallel:** ask your advisor to start the German application for SIEED, since it is the best fit for a modern within/between-firm decomposition and the paperwork must come from the supervising chair.

**1. [Veneto Workers Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**

- **Gaps:** it ends in 2001, so it covers a historical rise in inequality only. The foundation's page says the provinces of Treviso and Vicenza, while papers describe the whole Veneto region; ask which extract you get. The page does not list earnings variables (from memory: annual earnings and days or weeks paid per job).
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.01494) for bias-corrected AKM variance decompositions, and [Card, Devicienti and Maida](https://davidcard.berkeley.edu/papers/RESTUD-2014.pdf).

- **Where you work:** on site at a guest location (Germany, USA, Canada, UK), then by submitting code remotely. Remote desktop is limited to institutions in Germany. No fee is mentioned.
- **Gaps:** wages are top-coded at the social-security ceiling and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Used by:** [Card, Heining and Kline (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjt006), which is the template for your question on the same underlying data.

- **Contents:** anonymised Spanish social-security histories, with each spell tied to an employer's contribution account code and monthly contribution bases.
- **Access:** open to "instituciones públicas y privadas que lo soliciten" for non-commercial research. Your university submits the form and researcher sheet, and the social-security directorate approves.
- **Gaps:** contribution bases are capped unless you take the tax-data version (from memory). Whether non-Spanish universities qualify is not stated on the page; from memory, foreign universities have obtained it.

**4. [Chile Seguro de Cesantía samples](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-7521.html)**
- **Contents:** monthly contribution histories for sampled affiliates, with workers and employers under consistent anonymous numbers. The regulator's 2024 public account says the samples were refreshed that year.
- **Access:** the regulator says the samples are "a disposición del público" on its website. The download link in its press releases returned a 404 to my client, so open spensiones.cl in a browser and look under statistics and databases.

- **Catch:** a 2018 version of the lab's guide says this dataset is limited to Banco de Portugal researchers and their co-authors. Check the current Guide for Researchers before investing time.

**6. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- **Access:** apply through the confidential data access portal, get the producer's agreement and the Statistical Secrecy Committee's approval ([procedure](https://www.casd.eu/en/your-project/procedures-dhabilitation/)). Your institution's legal representative then signs a contract and pays for the secure terminal ([price list](https://www.casd.eu/en/tarifs-2/)).
- **Gaps:** I did not capture the fee amounts.

**7. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/ces/data/restricted-use-data/lehd-data.html)**
- **Access:** "researchers must have an approved project" and all work happens in a Federal Statistical Research Data Center.
- **Conditions (from data-centre slide decks found by search, 2018–2025):** advisor as co-principal investigator, about 4–6 months to approval and longer with tax-agency review, and US residency for 3 of the last 5 years.

- **Access:** requires a cooperation agreement between an institution and the labour ministry, plus a confidentiality term per user. The realistic route is a Brazilian co-author or host whose institution already has one.

**9–11.**

Nothing real is downloadable today with a confirmed employer identifier. The fastest real option is the Veneto Worker Histories file (Italy, 1975–2001), released on a signed form by email; the best current data is Germany's SIEED, which takes months and an application from your advisor's chair. ## What I assumed you need

- **R1–R3 (must):** persistent worker ID, persistent employer ID, individual earnings.
- **R4 (must):** at least ten years.
- **R5 (must, my addition):** all or most co-workers observed at each employer. A within/between-firm split needs this, and small worker samples (2–4%) also give badly biased firm effects. This rules out several otherwise "easy" datasets.
- **R6 (nice):** obtainable by a PhD student, ideally soon.

## Details

**1. [Veneto Worker Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**
- **Contents:** three linkable Stata files (workers, firms, contracts) with an anonymous worker ID and a firm ID; firms are not anonymised.
- **Coverage:** the distributor's page says Treviso and Vicenza only, but [a user's notes page](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources) says it covers all of Veneto and follows workers who leave the region.
- **Access:** the page says "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". No fee is stated. I could not read the form's terms or turnaround.
- **Limits:** it ends in 2001, covers one region, and users drop the years before 1984–85 because of missing data. That leaves about 17 usable years, but none recent.
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten (2020)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.3982/ECTA16410) for an AKM variance decomposition.

**2. [SIEED 7523](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/the-sample-of-integrated-employer-employee-data-sieed-sieed-7523-version-1/)**
- **Contents:** every worker ever employed at a 1% sample of German establishments, with full biographies. Wages are top-coded and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Access:** there is no off-site file. Per the [access page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/), the agreement is between your institution and the data centre, and for thesis work the supervising chair must apply and name you. The legal check "could take up to one month".
- **Working mode:** you then submit Stata scripts remotely and receive disclosure-checked output, or work on-site. Sites in the US, Canada and UK are only for stays of nine months or more and use extra-anonymised data. Remote desktop is only for institutions in Germany.
- **Available now:** test data with the real file structure can be downloaded, but it is "random and therefore not eligible for analysis".

**3. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/topics/research/guidance/restricted-use-microdata/standard-application-process.html)**
- **Eligibility:** US residence for 36 of the past 60 months and a US institution; your advisor should be co-PI.
- **Timeline:** 1–2 months to write the proposal, several months of review, then at least 3–4 months for the background check. Budget a year.
- **Caveat:** the page I verified is the general Census application page, not one specific to LEHD.

**4. [LIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-cross-sectional-model-1993-2023-version-1/)**
- It adds establishment survey variables (bargaining coverage, works councils) to the worker records, through the same application as SIEED.
- The page I verified is the cross-sectional model; the longitudinal model is the one for AKM (from memory).

**5. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- It is long (from 1976) but a worker sample, so it cannot give within-firm variance.
- The exhaustive annual files in the same secure centre can be chained across years instead (from memory).
- Approval goes through the Comité du secret statistique. Whether non-French institutions are eligible, and the price, were not confirmed.

**6. [MCVL](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)**
- The portal says public and private institutions may request it for non-commercial scientific research. It is free, and employment spells carry the employer's contribution account code.
- It is good for mobility and earnings dynamics but not for firm effects. Whether institutions outside Spain qualify was not confirmed.

**7. [PyTwoWay](https://tlamadon.github.io/pytwoway/)**
- It simulates a worker-firm panel with known worker and firm effects, and includes AKM plus the standard bias corrections.
- It cannot answer your question, but it lets you build and test the whole pipeline now. The [2026 JEP guide to AKM](https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.20231372) covers estimation practice.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Chile, unemployment insurance samples:** this is the lead most worth an hour of your time. The regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples, monthly since 2002, and published papers describe downloading them directly. A separate public sample of the employer database also exists. The download address those papers cite returned 404 today, and I could not confirm an employer identifier in the public files. Even with one, the worker samples would fail R5; check whether the employer sample includes all workers at sampled firms. Start from the [regulator's announcement](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-12931.html).
- **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal:** the classic AKM dataset. Access appears to run through a researcher accreditation platform and a contract with the statistics office; the conditions for foreign institutions were not found.
- **Brazil, RAIS (identified version):** requires an application to the Brazilian ministry, per the [Engbom–Moser replication package](https://github.com/economoser/EM2022), which also ships AKM code.
- **Italy, full social security archives:** on-site in Rome through the VisitINPS programme, which is competitive. A separate 6.5% worker sample (LoSaI) is released by the Ministry of Labour on a research proposal; I could not confirm a firm identifier.
- **Not checked at all (from memory, all secure-environment access through a national statistics office):** Nordic registers, the Netherlands, Austria, UK (ASHE), Hungary, Canada. Most are much easier with a local co-author.

## Not recommended, and why

- **SIAB (Germany), including its Scientific Use File:** a 2% worker sample, so co-workers are almost never observed. It is the easiest IAB file to hold off-site but the wrong design for this question.
- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP, SOEP:** they follow workers across jobs but do not link co-workers to a common employer ID (from memory).
- **European Structure of Earnings Survey:** allows a within/between-workplace split, but workers are not followed, so no AKM.
- **Public LEHD tabulations and public RAIS extracts:** aggregates, or no person IDs (from memory).

## What I could not find

- No real linked panel with a confirmed employer ID that downloads without an application.
- The text of the Veneto access form, the Spanish request forms and the French secure-centre prices.
- Whether the test data in the [Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten code repository](https://github.com/rsaggio87/LeaveOutTwoWay) is real or simulated.

Dataset registries hold almost nothing for this kind of data, so most facts come from the owners' pages and web search.

1. **Today:** install PyTwoWay and build the pipeline on simulated data.
2. **This week:** send the Veneto form, and ask your advisor whether the chair will submit the SIEED application. That request is the long pole, and you can code against the test data while it runs.
3. **If you need a US result:** start the LEHD conversation with your nearest research data center now, in parallel.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-M9mN91/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

## What I assumed you need

- **R6 (nice):** obtainable by a PhD student, ideally soon.

## Shortlist

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
