| 3 | LEHD (US Census) | Proposal plus security clearance, secure lab only; 6–12+ months | Federal confidentiality law | Near-universe, 1990s onward | Strong | Process today via secondary sources; contents from memory |
| 4 | LIAB (Germany, IAB) | Same route as SIEED; months | Custom use agreement | Surveyed establishments and their workers, 1993–2023 | Partial | Today; longitudinal variant from memory |
| 5 | Panel tous salariés (France, CASD) | Committee approval plus paid secure access; months | Custom | 1/24 worker sample (1/12 from 2002), from 1976 | Partial (fails R5) | Catalogue today; procedure and fee from memory |
| 6 | MCVL (Spain) | Institution applies to Social Security, free; weeks (from memory) | Non-commercial research terms | 4% of individuals (from memory) | Partial (fails R5) | Eligibility today; sample size from memory |
| 7 | PyTwoWay / BipartitePandas simulated data | `pip install`; minutes | Not checked | Any size you simulate | Pipeline only | Today |

## Details

**1. [Veneto Worker Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**
- **Contents:** three linkable Stata files (workers, firms, contracts) with an anonymous worker ID and a firm ID; firms are not anonymised.
- **Coverage:** the distributor's page says Treviso and Vicenza only, but [a user's notes page](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources) says it covers all of Veneto and follows workers who leave the region.
- **Access:** the page says "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". No fee is stated. I could not read the form's terms or turnaround.
- **Limits:** it ends in 2001, covers one region, and users drop the years before 1984–85 because of missing data. That leaves about 17 usable years, but none recent.
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten (2020)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.3982/ECTA16410) for an AKM variance decomposition.

**2. [SIEED 7523](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/the-sample-of-integrated-employer-employee-data-sieed-sieed-7523-version-1/)**
- **Contents:** every worker ever employed at a 1% sample of German establishments, with full biographies. Wages are top-coded and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Access:** there is no off-site file. Per the [access page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/), the agreement is between your institution and the data centre, and for thesis work the supervising chair must apply and name you. The legal check "could take up to one month".
- **Working mode:** you then submit Stata scripts remotely and receive disclosure-checked output, or work on-site. Sites in the US, Canada and UK are only for stays of nine months or more and use extra-anonymised data. Remote desktop is only for institutions in Germany.
- **Available now:** test data with the real file structure can be downloaded, but it is "random and therefore not eligible for analysis".

**3. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/topics/research/guidance/restricted-use-microdata/standard-application-process.html)**
- **Eligibility:** US residence for 36 of the past 60 months and a US institution; your advisor should be co-PI.
- **Timeline:** 1–2 months to write the proposal, several months of review, then at least 3–4 months for the background check. Budget a year.
- **Caveat:** the page I verified is the general Census application page, not one specific to LEHD.

**4. [LIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-cross-sectional-model-1993-2023-version-1/)**
- It adds establishment survey variables (bargaining coverage, works councils) to the worker records, through the same application as SIEED.
- The page I verified is the cross-sectional model; the longitudinal model is the one for AKM (from memory).

**5. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- It is long (from 1976) but a worker sample, so it cannot give within-firm variance.
- The exhaustive annual files in the same secure centre can be chained across years instead (from memory).
- Approval goes through the Comité du secret statistique. Whether non-French institutions are eligible, and the price, were not confirmed.

**6. [MCVL](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)**
- The portal says public and private institutions may request it for non-commercial scientific research. It is free, and employment spells carry the employer's contribution account code.
- It is good for mobility and earnings dynamics but not for firm effects. Whether institutions outside Spain qualify was not confirmed.

**7. [PyTwoWay](https://tlamadon.github.io/pytwoway/)**
- It simulates a worker-firm panel with known worker and firm effects, and includes AKM plus the standard bias corrections.
- It cannot answer your question, but it lets you build and test the whole pipeline now. The [2026 JEP guide to AKM](https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.20231372) covers estimation practice.

## Known, not confirmed

The regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples, monthly since 2002, and published papers describe downloading them directly. A separate public sample of the employer database also exists. The download address those papers cite returned 404 today, and I could not confirm an employer identifier in the public files. Even with one, the worker samples would fail R5; check whether the employer sample includes all workers at sampled firms. Start from the [regulator's announcement](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-12931.html).

- **R6 (nice):** obtainable by a PhD student, ideally soon.

## Shortlist

| 6 | MCVL (Spain) | Institution applies to Social Security, free; weeks (from memory) | Non-commercial research terms | 4% of individuals (from memory) | Partial (fails R5) | Eligibility today; sample size from memory |
| 7 | PyTwoWay / BipartitePandas simulated data | `pip install`; minutes | Not checked | Any size you simulate | Pipeline only | Today |

## Details

**1. [Veneto Worker Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**
- **Contents:** three linkable Stata files (workers, firms, contracts) with an anonymous worker ID and a firm ID; firms are not anonymised.
- **Coverage:** the distributor's page says Treviso and Vicenza only, but [a user's notes page](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources) says it covers all of Veneto and follows workers who leave the region.
- **Access:** the page says "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". No fee is stated. I could not read the form's terms or turnaround.
- **Limits:** it ends in 2001, covers one region, and users drop the years before 1984–85 because of missing data. That leaves about 17 usable years, but none recent.
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten (2020)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.3982/ECTA16410) for an AKM variance decomposition.

**2. [SIEED 7523](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/the-sample-of-integrated-employer-employee-data-sieed-sieed-7523-version-1/)**
- **Contents:** every worker ever employed at a 1% sample of German establishments, with full biographies. Wages are top-coded and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Access:** there is no off-site file. Per the [access page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/), the agreement is between your institution and the data centre, and for thesis work the supervising chair must apply and name you. The legal check "could take up to one month".
- **Working mode:** you then submit Stata scripts remotely and receive disclosure-checked output, or work on-site. Sites in the US, Canada and UK are only for stays of nine months or more and use extra-anonymised data. Remote desktop is only for institutions in Germany.
- **Available now:** test data with the real file structure can be downloaded, but it is "random and therefore not eligible for analysis".

**3. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/topics/research/guidance/restricted-use-microdata/standard-application-process.html)**
- **Eligibility:** US residence for 36 of the past 60 months and a US institution; your advisor should be co-PI.
- **Timeline:** 1–2 months to write the proposal, several months of review, then at least 3–4 months for the background check. Budget a year.
- **Caveat:** the page I verified is the general Census application page, not one specific to LEHD.

**4. [LIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-cross-sectional-model-1993-2023-version-1/)**
- It adds establishment survey variables (bargaining coverage, works councils) to the worker records, through the same application as SIEED.
- The page I verified is the cross-sectional model; the longitudinal model is the one for AKM (from memory).

**5. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- It is long (from 1976) but a worker sample, so it cannot give within-firm variance.
- The exhaustive annual files in the same secure centre can be chained across years instead (from memory).
- Approval goes through the Comité du secret statistique. Whether non-French institutions are eligible, and the price, were not confirmed.

**6. [MCVL](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)**
- The portal says public and private institutions may request it for non-commercial scientific research. It is free, and employment spells carry the employer's contribution account code.
- It is good for mobility and earnings dynamics but not for firm effects. Whether institutions outside Spain qualify was not confirmed.

**7. [PyTwoWay](https://tlamadon.github.io/pytwoway/)**
- It simulates a worker-firm panel with known worker and firm effects, and includes AKM plus the standard bias corrections.
- It cannot answer your question, but it lets you build and test the whole pipeline now. The [2026 JEP guide to AKM](https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.20231372) covers estimation practice.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Chile, unemployment insurance samples:** this is the lead most worth an hour of your time. The regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples, monthly since 2002, and published papers describe downloading them directly. A separate public sample of the employer database also exists. The download address those papers cite returned 404 today, and I could not confirm an employer identifier in the public files. Even with one, the worker samples would fail R5; check whether the employer sample includes all workers at sampled firms. Start from the [regulator's announcement](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-12931.html).
- **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal:** the classic AKM dataset. Access appears to run through a researcher accreditation platform and a contract with the statistics office; the conditions for foreign institutions were not found.
- **Brazil, RAIS (identified version):** requires an application to the Brazilian ministry, per the [Engbom–Moser replication package](https://github.com/economoser/EM2022), which also ships AKM code.
- **Italy, full social security archives:** on-site in Rome through the VisitINPS programme, which is competitive. A separate 6.5% worker sample (LoSaI) is released by the Ministry of Labour on a research proposal; I could not confirm a firm identifier.
- **Not checked at all (from memory, all secure-environment access through a national statistics office):** Nordic registers, the Netherlands, Austria, UK (ASHE), Hungary, Canada. Most are much easier with a local co-author.

## Not recommended, and why

- **SIAB (Germany), including its Scientific Use File:** a 2% worker sample, so co-workers are almost never observed. It is the easiest IAB file to hold off-site but the wrong design for this question.
- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP, SOEP:** they follow workers across jobs but do not link co-workers to a common employer ID (from memory).
- **European Structure of Earnings Survey:** allows a within/between-workplace split, but workers are not followed, so no AKM.
- **Public LEHD tabulations and public RAIS extracts:** aggregates, or no person IDs (from memory).

## What I could not find

- No real linked panel with a confirmed employer ID that downloads without an application.
- The text of the Veneto access form, the Spanish request forms and the French secure-centre prices.
- Whether the test data in the [Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten code repository](https://github.com/rsaggio87/LeaveOutTwoWay) is real or simulated.

Dataset registries hold almost nothing for this kind of data, so most facts come from the owners' pages and web search.

3. **If you need a US result:** start the LEHD conversation with your nearest research data center now, in parallel.

All checks were made on 12 November 2026; anything marked "from memory" was not confirmed.

## What I assumed you need

- **R1–R3 (must):** persistent worker ID, persistent employer ID, individual earnings.
- **R4 (must):** at least ten years.
- **R5 (must, my addition):** all or most co-workers observed at each employer. A within/between-firm split needs this, and small worker samples (2–4%) also give badly biased firm effects. This rules out several otherwise "easy" datasets.
- **R6 (nice):** obtainable by a PhD student, ideally soon.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Veneto Worker Histories (Italy) | Signed form emailed to the distributor; weeks (my estimate) | Signed form; required credit line | All private-sector workers and firms in Veneto, 1975–2001 | Strong | Today; earnings variables from memory |
| 2 | SIEED (Germany, IAB) | Institutional agreement, then remote execution or on-site; months | Custom use agreement | 1% of establishments, all their workers, 1975–2023 | Strong | Today; top-coding from memory |
| 3 | LEHD (US Census) | Proposal plus security clearance, secure lab only; 6–12+ months | Federal confidentiality law | Near-universe, 1990s onward | Strong | Process today via secondary sources; contents from memory |
| 4 | LIAB (Germany, IAB) | Same route as SIEED; months | Custom use agreement | Surveyed establishments and their workers, 1993–2023 | Partial | Today; longitudinal variant from memory |
| 5 | Panel tous salariés (France, CASD) | Committee approval plus paid secure access; months | Custom | 1/24 worker sample (1/12 from 2002), from 1976 | Partial (fails R5) | Catalogue today; procedure and fee from memory |
| 6 | MCVL (Spain) | Institution applies to Social Security, free; weeks (from memory) | Non-commercial research terms | 4% of individuals (from memory) | Partial (fails R5) | Eligibility today; sample size from memory |
| 7 | PyTwoWay / BipartitePandas simulated data | `pip install`; minutes | Not checked | Any size you simulate | Pipeline only | Today |

## Details

**1. [Veneto Worker Histories](https://www.frdb.org/en/dati/dati-inps-carriere-lavorative-in-veneto/)**
- **Contents:** three linkable Stata files (workers, firms, contracts) with an anonymous worker ID and a firm ID; firms are not anonymised.
- **Coverage:** the distributor's page says Treviso and Vicenza only, but [a user's notes page](https://www.jarellanobover.com/veneto-workers-histories-dataset-additional-resources) says it covers all of Veneto and follows workers who leave the region.
- **Access:** the page says "fill and sign the attached form and send it to info@frdb.org". No fee is stated. I could not read the form's terms or turnaround.
- **Limits:** it ends in 2001, covers one region, and users drop the years before 1984–85 because of missing data. That leaves about 17 usable years, but none recent.
- **Used by:** [Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten (2020)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.3982/ECTA16410) for an AKM variance decomposition.

**2. [SIEED 7523](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/the-sample-of-integrated-employer-employee-data-sieed-sieed-7523-version-1/)**
- **Contents:** every worker ever employed at a 1% sample of German establishments, with full biographies. Wages are top-coded and there are no hours (from memory).
- **Access:** there is no off-site file. Per the [access page](https://fdz.iab.de/en/data-access/on-site-use/), the agreement is between your institution and the data centre, and for thesis work the supervising chair must apply and name you. The legal check "could take up to one month".
- **Working mode:** you then submit Stata scripts remotely and receive disclosure-checked output, or work on-site. Sites in the US, Canada and UK are only for stays of nine months or more and use extra-anonymised data. Remote desktop is only for institutions in Germany.
- **Available now:** test data with the real file structure can be downloaded, but it is "random and therefore not eligible for analysis".

**3. [LEHD](https://www.census.gov/topics/research/guidance/restricted-use-microdata/standard-application-process.html)**
- **Eligibility:** US residence for 36 of the past 60 months and a US institution; your advisor should be co-PI.
- **Timeline:** 1–2 months to write the proposal, several months of review, then at least 3–4 months for the background check. Budget a year.
- **Caveat:** the page I verified is the general Census application page, not one specific to LEHD.

**4. [LIAB](https://fdz.iab.de/en/int_bd_pd/linked-employer-employee-data-of-the-iab-liab-liab-cross-sectional-model-1993-2023-version-1/)**
- It adds establishment survey variables (bargaining coverage, works councils) to the worker records, through the same application as SIEED.
- The page I verified is the cross-sectional model; the longitudinal model is the one for AKM (from memory).

**5. [Panel tous salariés](https://www.casd.eu/en/source/all-employee-panel/)**
- It is long (from 1976) but a worker sample, so it cannot give within-firm variance.
- The exhaustive annual files in the same secure centre can be chained across years instead (from memory).
- Approval goes through the Comité du secret statistique. Whether non-French institutions are eligible, and the price, were not confirmed.

**6. [MCVL](https://portaldatos.seg-social.gob.es/mcvl)**
- The portal says public and private institutions may request it for non-commercial scientific research. It is free, and employment spells carry the employer's contribution account code.
- It is good for mobility and earnings dynamics but not for firm effects. Whether institutions outside Spain qualify was not confirmed.

**7. [PyTwoWay](https://tlamadon.github.io/pytwoway/)**
- It simulates a worker-firm panel with known worker and firm effects, and includes AKM plus the standard bias corrections.
- It cannot answer your question, but it lets you build and test the whole pipeline now. The [2026 JEP guide to AKM](https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.20231372) covers estimation practice.

## Known, not confirmed

- **Chile, unemployment insurance samples:** this is the lead most worth an hour of your time. The regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples, monthly since 2002, and published papers describe downloading them directly. A separate public sample of the employer database also exists. The download address those papers cite returned 404 today, and I could not confirm an employer identifier in the public files. Even with one, the worker samples would fail R5; check whether the employer sample includes all workers at sampled firms. Start from the [regulator's announcement](https://www.spensiones.cl/portal/institucional/594/w3-article-12931.html).
- **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal:** the classic AKM dataset. Access appears to run through a researcher accreditation platform and a contract with the statistics office; the conditions for foreign institutions were not found.
- **Brazil, RAIS (identified version):** requires an application to the Brazilian ministry, per the [Engbom–Moser replication package](https://github.com/economoser/EM2022), which also ships AKM code.
- **Italy, full social security archives:** on-site in Rome through the VisitINPS programme, which is competitive. A separate 6.5% worker sample (LoSaI) is released by the Ministry of Labour on a research proposal; I could not confirm a firm identifier.
- **Not checked at all (from memory, all secure-environment access through a national statistics office):** Nordic registers, the Netherlands, Austria, UK (ASHE), Hungary, Canada. Most are much easier with a local co-author.

## Not recommended, and why

- **SIAB (Germany), including its Scientific Use File:** a 2% worker sample, so co-workers are almost never observed. It is the easiest IAB file to hold off-site but the wrong design for this question.
- **PSID, NLSY, SIPP, SOEP:** they follow workers across jobs but do not link co-workers to a common employer ID (from memory).
- **European Structure of Earnings Survey:** allows a within/between-workplace split, but workers are not followed, so no AKM.
- **Public LEHD tabulations and public RAIS extracts:** aggregates, or no person IDs (from memory).

## What I could not find

- No real linked panel with a confirmed employer ID that downloads without an application.
- The text of the Veneto access form, the Spanish request forms and the French secure-centre prices.
- Whether the test data in the [Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten code repository](https://github.com/rsaggio87/LeaveOutTwoWay) is real or simulated.

Dataset registries hold almost nothing for this kind of data, so most facts come from the owners' pages and web search.

## Next step

1. **Today:** install PyTwoWay and build the pipeline on simulated data.
2. **This week:** send the Veneto form, and ask your advisor whether the chair will submit the SIEED application. That request is the long pole, and you can code against the test data while it runs.
3. **If you need a US result:** start the LEHD conversation with your nearest research data center now, in parallel.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-M9mN91/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

**Nothing fully adequate is downloadable today, but two datasets are within weeks of a signed form, and one of them (Veneto) is the standard AKM testbed.** I checked the access pages where I could; items I could not confirm are marked.

## Start now

- **Veneto Worker Histories (Italy, 1975–2001).** It has worker and firm IDs and all workers in covered firms, and was used by Card–Devicienti–Maida (2014) and Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten (2020). You email a signed form to Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti; the page lists no fee or eligibility rules. Its page describes coverage as Treviso and Vicenza provinces, while the papers describe all of Veneto, so ask which version you get. It ends in 2001 and is one region.
- **Chile unemployment insurance samples.** The pensions regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples with monthly records per employment relationship and sequential firm IDs. The download link I found returned a 404, and I could not confirm the firm ID tracks across employers, so check the codebook first.
- **IAB test data (Germany).** Fake-content files with the real structure are freely downloadable for SIEED and LIAB. They are useless for results, but you can write and debug your whole pipeline while an application is pending.

## Options requiring an application

| Data | What it takes | Fit for your question |
|---|---|---|
| **Germany, IAB SIEED / LIAB** (1975–2023) | Free; your institution signs the contract; document check takes up to a month. A guest stay comes first, then remote job submission. US, Canadian and UK sites require a nine-month minimum stay. A third-party source says students cannot apply alone, so expect your advisor to be the applicant. | Best realistic option. SIEED samples establishments and keeps all their workers. Pre-estimated AKM effects can be added on request. Wages are top-coded. |
| **Spain, MCVL** (2004 onward, with retrospective histories) | Free; institutional application for a defined scientific project; forms in Spanish. I could not confirm rules for foreign institutions. | 4% worker sample, so few coworkers per firm. |
| **US, LEHD** | Census proposal with your advisor as co-PI, showing a benefit to Census. Clearance alone adds 3–4 months after approval. Non-citizens need three of the last five years in the US. Work is done in a secure data centre. | Excellent data, but plan on a year or more before first results. |
| **Brazil, identified RAIS** | Formal cooperation agreement with the Ministry of Labor, or joining one your institution already holds. | The public RAIS files lack worker identifiers, so they cannot be used. |
| **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal** | Through Banco de Portugal's microdata lab, apparently restricted to Bank researchers and their collaborators (2018 guide, possibly outdated). | Realistically needs a Portuguese co-author. |
| **Italy, LoSaI** | Research proposal to the Ministry of Labour. | Roughly 7% worker sample; I could not confirm it carries a usable firm identifier. |

From memory, not checked this session: the Nordic registers, the Netherlands, France and Austria generally require a local affiliation or accredited institution, usually with fees. Ask your advisor before ruling them out.

## Design constraint

Worker-based samples (MCVL, LoSaI, Chile) are weak for your decomposition. With only a few sampled workers per firm, firm mean wages are noisy and the between-firm share is overstated. Firm effects are also identified off few movers, which inflates their variance. Prefer data with all workers in a firm (Veneto, SIEED, LEHD), and plan on a bias-corrected estimator such as the Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten leave-out method either way.

## Recommendation

1. Send the Veneto form this week and build the full AKM and decomposition pipeline on it.
2. Ask your advisor and department whether anyone already holds an IAB, LEHD or RAIS agreement you can join. This is the fastest route to the big datasets.
3. Start the IAB SIEED application in parallel as the dataset for the actual paper, since it covers the period when German inequality rose.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Nothing fully adequate is downloadable today, but two datasets are within weeks of a signed form, and one of them (Veneto) is the standard AKM testbed.** I checked the access pages where I could; items I could not confirm are marked.

## Start now

- **Veneto Worker Histories (Italy, 1975–2001).** It has worker and firm IDs and all workers in covered firms, and was used by Card–Devicienti–Maida (2014) and Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten (2020). You email a signed form to Fondazione Rodolfo Debenedetti; the page lists no fee or eligibility rules. Its page describes coverage as Treviso and Vicenza provinces, while the papers describe all of Veneto, so ask which version you get. It ends in 2001 and is one region.
- **Chile unemployment insurance samples.** The pensions regulator publishes anonymised 3%, 5% and 12% worker samples with monthly records per employment relationship and sequential firm IDs. The download link I found returned a 404, and I could not confirm the firm ID tracks across employers, so check the codebook first.
- **IAB test data (Germany).** Fake-content files with the real structure are freely downloadable for SIEED and LIAB. They are useless for results, but you can write and debug your whole pipeline while an application is pending.

## Options requiring an application

| Data | What it takes | Fit for your question |
|---|---|---|
| **Germany, IAB SIEED / LIAB** (1975–2023) | Free; your institution signs the contract; document check takes up to a month. A guest stay comes first, then remote job submission. US, Canadian and UK sites require a nine-month minimum stay. A third-party source says students cannot apply alone, so expect your advisor to be the applicant. | Best realistic option. SIEED samples establishments and keeps all their workers. Pre-estimated AKM effects can be added on request. Wages are top-coded. |
| **Spain, MCVL** (2004 onward, with retrospective histories) | Free; institutional application for a defined scientific project; forms in Spanish. I could not confirm rules for foreign institutions. | 4% worker sample, so few coworkers per firm. |
| **US, LEHD** | Census proposal with your advisor as co-PI, showing a benefit to Census. Clearance alone adds 3–4 months after approval. Non-citizens need three of the last five years in the US. Work is done in a secure data centre. | Excellent data, but plan on a year or more before first results. |
| **Brazil, identified RAIS** | Formal cooperation agreement with the Ministry of Labor, or joining one your institution already holds. | The public RAIS files lack worker identifiers, so they cannot be used. |
| **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal** | Through Banco de Portugal's microdata lab, apparently restricted to Bank researchers and their collaborators (2018 guide, possibly outdated). | Realistically needs a Portuguese co-author. |
| **Italy, LoSaI** | Research proposal to the Ministry of Labour. | Roughly 7% worker sample; I could not confirm it carries a usable firm identifier. |

From memory, not checked this session: the Nordic registers, the Netherlands, France and Austria generally require a local affiliation or accredited institution, usually with fees. Ask your advisor before ruling them out.

## Design constraint

Worker-based samples (MCVL, LoSaI, Chile) are weak for your decomposition. With only a few sampled workers per firm, firm mean wages are noisy and the between-firm share is overstated. Firm effects are also identified off few movers, which inflates their variance. Prefer data with all workers in a firm (Veneto, SIEED, LEHD), and plan on a bias-corrected estimator such as the Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten leave-out method either way.

## Recommendation

1. Send the Veneto form this week and build the full AKM and decomposition pipeline on it.
2. Ask your advisor and department whether anyone already holds an IAB, LEHD or RAIS agreement you can join. This is the fastest route to the big datasets.
3. Start the IAB SIEED application in parallel as the dataset for the actual paper, since it covers the period when German inequality rose.

- **IAB test data (Germany).** Fake-content files with the real structure are freely downloadable for SIEED and LIAB. They are useless for results, but you can write and debug your whole pipeline while an application is pending.

## Options requiring an application

| Data | What it takes | Fit for your question |
|---|---|---|
| **Germany, IAB SIEED / LIAB** (1975–2023) | Free; your institution signs the contract; document check takes up to a month. A guest stay comes first, then remote job submission. US, Canadian and UK sites require a nine-month minimum stay. A third-party source says students cannot apply alone, so expect your advisor to be the applicant. | Best realistic option. SIEED samples establishments and keeps all their workers. Pre-estimated AKM effects can be added on request. Wages are top-coded. |
| **Spain, MCVL** (2004 onward, with retrospective histories) | Free; institutional application for a defined scientific project; forms in Spanish. I could not confirm rules for foreign institutions. | 4% worker sample, so few coworkers per firm. |
| **US, LEHD** | Census proposal with your advisor as co-PI, showing a benefit to Census. Clearance alone adds 3–4 months after approval. Non-citizens need three of the last five years in the US. Work is done in a secure data centre. | Excellent data, but plan on a year or more before first results. |
| **Brazil, identified RAIS** | Formal cooperation agreement with the Ministry of Labor, or joining one your institution already holds. | The public RAIS files lack worker identifiers, so they cannot be used. |
| **Portugal, Quadros de Pessoal** | Through Banco de Portugal's microdata lab, apparently restricted to Bank researchers and their collaborators (2018 guide, possibly outdated). | Realistically needs a Portuguese co-author. |
| **Italy, LoSaI** | Research proposal to the Ministry of Labour. | Roughly 7% worker sample; I could not confirm it carries a usable firm identifier. |

From memory, not checked this session: the Nordic registers, the Netherlands, France and Austria generally require a local affiliation or accredited institution, usually with fees. Ask your advisor before ruling them out.

## Design constraint

Worker-based samples (MCVL, LoSaI, Chile) are weak for your decomposition. With only a few sampled workers per firm, firm mean wages are noisy and the between-firm share is overstated. Firm effects are also identified off few movers, which inflates their variance. Prefer data with all workers in a firm (Veneto, SIEED, LEHD), and plan on a bias-corrected estimator such as the Kline–Saggio–Sølvsten leave-out method either way.

## Recommendation

1. Send the Veneto form this week and build the full AKM and decomposition pipeline on it.
2. Ask your advisor and department whether anyone already holds an IAB, LEHD or RAIS agreement you can join. This is the fastest route to the big datasets.
3. Start the IAB SIEED application in parallel as the dataset for the actual paper, since it covers the period when German inequality rose.

**Nothing fully suitable is a same-day download, but one real dataset is close.** The Veneto Workers Histories (Italy) needs only a signed form emailed to a foundation, and it is a full-population panel you run on your own laptop. I checked the access pages for the first four options below today; the rest is from memory and flagged as such.

## Ranked by how fast you can realistically start

| Data | What it is | What access takes | Fit for AKM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Veneto Workers Histories (VWH)** | All private-sector workers and firms in the Veneto region, 1975–2001, with worker and firm IDs | Fill in and sign a form, email it to info@frdb.org. The page states no fee, eligibility rule or turnaround time. | Good. It ends in 2001 and has missing-data issues before the mid-1980s, so 1984–2001 is the usable window. |
| **Spain MCVL** | 4% random sample of people in Social Security records, with firm and establishment IDs and full work histories | Free application to Spain's Social Security directorate (about 11 forms in an older guide); approved users work on their own computers. | Feasible but thin. A 4% worker sample means few movers per firm, so limited-mobility bias is severe. |
| **Germany IAB (SIAB, LIAB)** | SIAB is a 2% worker sample; LIAB links establishments to their workers | Free. Request form, up to a month for document checks, then an institutional use agreement. Analysis is by remote job submission or on-site visits. For a dissertation, your faculty must submit the request. | Very good. IAB also supplies pre-estimated AKM worker and establishment effects (1985–2023) to merge in. |
| **US LEHD** | Near-universe quarterly earnings records | Proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center, plus background clearance and state sign-offs. Centres quote 6–12 months or more, and your advisor is expected to be co-PI. | Excellent data, but only realistic if your university has a centre and your advisor is on board. |
| **France (panel via CASD)** | Long worker panel from 1976, a sample of workers | Statistical confidentiality committee approval plus a paid secure-access box. I could not confirm current fees or rules for foreign institutions. | Good, but months and money. |
| **Brazil RAIS (identified)** | Universe of formal jobs | Requires a formal cooperation agreement between your institution and the Ministry of Labour. | Excellent data, but hard without a Brazilian co-author or institution. |

From memory, not checked today:
- **Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), Denmark, Sweden, Norway:** these generally require affiliation with a domestic institution or a local co-author.
- **Austria and the Netherlands:** open to foreign institutions, for a fee.
- **Italy LoSaI:** a roughly 7% worker sample available from the Ministry of Labour on a project application. I could not confirm that it carries a firm identifier.

## Traps to avoid

- **Public RAIS microdata** downloads freely but is de-identified, so you cannot follow workers. It is useless for AKM.
- **The German Scientific Use File** is the downloadable version of SIAB, but the pre-estimated AKM effects appear restricted to on-site or remote-execution use.
- **PSID, NLSY and SIPP** follow workers but do not link coworkers at the same firm, so firm effects are not identified.

## What I would do

1. **This week:** send the VWH form, and start the German application through your advisor in parallel, since it has the longest paperwork chain of the realistic options.
2. **While waiting:** build the full pipeline on simulated data: connected set, AKM estimation, variance decomposition, and a limited-mobility bias correction (leave-out, as in Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten). The `pytwoway` Python package includes a simulator for this, as I recall. Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten ran their correction on VWH, so their published numbers give you a benchmark.
3. **Ask your advisor** whether anyone in the department has an existing LEHD or IAB project you could join. That is the usual shortcut around the longest queues.

One caveat on VWH: Italian inequality over 1984–2001 has been studied on this exact dataset, so it is better as a training ground and first chapter than as a novel contribution on its own.

| Data | What it is | What access takes | Fit for AKM |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Veneto Workers Histories (VWH)** | All private-sector workers and firms in the Veneto region, 1975–2001, with worker and firm IDs | Fill in and sign a form, email it to info@frdb.org. The page states no fee, eligibility rule or turnaround time. | Good. It ends in 2001 and has missing-data issues before the mid-1980s, so 1984–2001 is the usable window. |
| **Spain MCVL** | 4% random sample of people in Social Security records, with firm and establishment IDs and full work histories | Free application to Spain's Social Security directorate (about 11 forms in an older guide); approved users work on their own computers. | Feasible but thin. A 4% worker sample means few movers per firm, so limited-mobility bias is severe. |
| **Germany IAB (SIAB, LIAB)** | SIAB is a 2% worker sample; LIAB links establishments to their workers | Free. Request form, up to a month for document checks, then an institutional use agreement. Analysis is by remote job submission or on-site visits. For a dissertation, your faculty must submit the request. | Very good. IAB also supplies pre-estimated AKM worker and establishment effects (1985–2023) to merge in. |
| **US LEHD** | Near-universe quarterly earnings records | Proposal through a Federal Statistical Research Data Center, plus background clearance and state sign-offs. Centres quote 6–12 months or more, and your advisor is expected to be co-PI. | Excellent data, but only realistic if your university has a centre and your advisor is on board. |
| **France (panel via CASD)** | Long worker panel from 1976, a sample of workers | Statistical confidentiality committee approval plus a paid secure-access box. I could not confirm current fees or rules for foreign institutions. | Good, but months and money. |
| **Brazil RAIS (identified)** | Universe of formal jobs | Requires a formal cooperation agreement between your institution and the Ministry of Labour. | Excellent data, but hard without a Brazilian co-author or institution. |

From memory, not checked today:
- **Portugal (Quadros de Pessoal), Denmark, Sweden, Norway:** these generally require affiliation with a domestic institution or a local co-author.
- **Austria and the Netherlands:** open to foreign institutions, for a fee.
- **Italy LoSaI:** a roughly 7% worker sample available from the Ministry of Labour on a project application. I could not confirm that it carries a firm identifier.

## Traps to avoid

- **Public RAIS microdata** downloads freely but is de-identified, so you cannot follow workers. It is useless for AKM.
- **The German Scientific Use File** is the downloadable version of SIAB, but the pre-estimated AKM effects appear restricted to on-site or remote-execution use.
- **PSID, NLSY and SIPP** follow workers but do not link coworkers at the same firm, so firm effects are not identified.

## What I would do

1. **This week:** send the VWH form, and start the German application through your advisor in parallel, since it has the longest paperwork chain of the realistic options.
2. **While waiting:** build the full pipeline on simulated data: connected set, AKM estimation, variance decomposition, and a limited-mobility bias correction (leave-out, as in Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten). The `pytwoway` Python package includes a simulator for this, as I recall. Kline, Saggio and Sølvsten ran their correction on VWH, so their published numbers give you a benchmark.
3. **Ask your advisor** whether anyone in the department has an existing LEHD or IAB project you could join. That is the usual shortcut around the longest queues.

One caveat on VWH: Italian inequality over 1984–2001 has been studied on this exact dataset, so it is better as a training ground and first chapter than as a novel contribution on its own.

Prompt

I'm a second-year PhD student in labor economics. I want to decompose the rise in wage inequality into within-firm and between-firm parts with an AKM-style model (worker and firm fixed effects), so I need linked employer-employee microdata where I can follow individual workers as they move between employers over at least ten years. Any country is fine. I already know most data like this is restricted, so please be honest about what it would actually take to get access to each option, and tell me if there is anything I could start working with right away.

Graders — what "good" means for this case
00-skill-firedtool_used
tool"Skill"
input_match"\"skill\"\\s*:\\s*\"(?:[\\w-]+:)?dataset-scout\""
01-recall-german-iabllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists German linked employer-employee data from the Institute for Employment Research (IAB) and its Research Data Centre (FDZ der BA im IAB) as a candidate, in any version: for example the Linked Employer-Employee Data of the IAB (LIAB, including the LIAB longitudinal model), the Sample of Integrated Labour Market Biographies (SIAB) linked to establishment data, the Integrated Employment Biographies (IEB), the Employment History (BeH) or the Establishment History Panel (BHP) combined with worker records. FAIL if the answer does not mention any German IAB/FDZ worker-establishment data, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-us-lehdllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the confidential microdata of the US Census Bureau's Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program (LEHD, also called the LEHD microdata, LEHD infrastructure files or LEHD Snapshot, built from state unemployment-insurance wage records) as a candidate source of linked employer-employee data. FAIL if the answer does not mention LEHD microdata, mentions only the public LEHD tabulations (QWI, LODES, J2J or OnTheMap) without the restricted worker-level microdata, or mentions LEHD only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-brazil-raisllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists Brazil's RAIS (Relação Anual de Informações Sociais, the Annual Social Information Report administered by the Brazilian Ministry of Labour and Employment) as a candidate source of linked employer-employee data, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention RAIS, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-german-fdz-applicationllm

PASS if the final answer mentions German IAB linked employer-employee data (LIAB, SIAB, IEB or other IAB/FDZ data) and states that getting it requires applying to the IAB Research Data Centre (FDZ) with a research project and concluding a use agreement or contract, or states that the data can be analysed only through on-site use at an FDZ location, remote desktop access or remote execution (submitting code) rather than being downloaded freely. FAIL if the answer does not mention the German IAB/FDZ data, gives no information about how it is accessed, or states that it can be downloaded freely without an application or contract.

05-access-us-fsrdc-projectllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the US Census Bureau's LEHD microdata and states that access requires an approved research project or proposal and takes place inside a secure Federal Statistical Research Data Center (FSRDC, also called a Census Research Data Center or RDC), for example also mentioning Special Sworn Status or additional IRS/SSA approval. Stating either the approved-project requirement or the FSRDC-only access is enough. FAIL if the answer does not mention LEHD microdata, gives no information about how they are accessed, or states that the worker-level LEHD microdata can be downloaded publicly.

06-access-brazil-ministry-agreementllm

PASS if the final answer mentions Brazil's RAIS and states that the identified version (with the worker and firm identifiers needed to follow individuals across employers) is restricted and is obtained through a formal request to, and agreement with, the Brazilian Ministry of Labour and Employment (for example a technical cooperation agreement, data-use agreement or similar approval), as opposed to the de-identified public files. FAIL if the answer does not mention RAIS, gives no information about how identified RAIS is accessed, or states that RAIS with worker identifiers can be freely downloaded without any agreement or approval.

07-trap-lehd-public-tablesllm

PASS if the final answer does not present the public LEHD data products (LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, LODES; Quarterly Workforce Indicators, QWI; Job-to-Job Flows, J2J; Post-Secondary Employment Outcomes, PSEO; or the OnTheMap tool) as worker-level linked employer-employee microdata in which individual workers can be followed across employers or used to estimate worker and firm fixed effects. Not mentioning them passes; mentioning them while noting that they are aggregated public tabulations (for example at census-block, county or industry level) and not individual-level microdata also passes. FAIL if the answer recommends any of these public tables as a dataset that lets the user track individual workers across firms or estimate an AKM model.

08-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists at least one of these less known linked employer-employee datasets as a candidate: (a) the Canadian Employer-Employee Dynamics Database (CEEDD) of Statistics Canada; (b) the Finnish Longitudinal Employer-Employee Data (FLEED) of Statistics Finland; (c) the Austrian Social Security Database (ASSD). FAIL if the answer mentions none of them as a candidate.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Start with **AMI**, **NOTSOFAR-1** and **ICSI**: all three are real English meetings with speaker-attributed transcripts and distant-microphone audio, and all three are released under CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution. Together they give you roughly 200 hours you can download today. Nothing I found offers hundreds of hours of genuine corporate meetings with far-field audio under a commercial licence.

All facts below were checked on 2026-11-12 against the named pages unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need
- **Must:** real recorded multi-party conversation (no simulated mixtures), speaker-turn annotation, English, and a licence that allows commercial use (a fee is acceptable).
- **Nice to have:** business-style meetings, and far-field or microphone-array audio.
- **My assumption:** "commercial use" means training and evaluating models that ship in your product, not redistributing the audio.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AMI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 100 h | Strong | today |
| 2 | NOTSOFAR-1 recorded meetings | Free Hugging Face account and token | CC BY 4.0, with "for open research" wording | 237 meetings of about 6 min | Strong | today |
| 3 | ICSI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | about 72 h, 75 meetings | Strong | licence today; size from a search result |
| 4 | DiPCo | Direct download | CDLA-Permissive 1.0 | about 5 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party | today |
| 5 | CHiME-6 | Direct download | CC BY-SA 4.0 | about 40–50 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party, share-alike | today |
| 6 | Earnings-21 | Direct download | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 39 h | Partial: business, not far-field | today |
| 7 | LDC corpora via for-profit membership | Membership agreement and fee, weeks | LDC member agreement | varies | Partial | terms today; sizes and fee from memory |

## Details

**1. [AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)**
- **Contents:** 100 hours of recorded meetings with headset, lapel and microphone-array channels, plus manual transcripts with speaker and timing.
- **Limits:** most meetings are role-played ("participants play different roles in a fictitious design team"), so they are business-style but elicited. The recordings come from a small number of instrumented rooms in the mid-2000s (from memory).
- **Access:** pick meetings and signals on the [download page](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/download/) and fetch the 22 MB manual annotations file.
- **Licence:** "The AMI corpus and its annotations are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license."
- **Used in:** [Carletta 2007](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-007-9040-x) (corpus description) and [ECAPA-TDNN diarization, 2021](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2021-941).

**2. [NOTSOFAR-1](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)** (Microsoft)
- **Contents:** "237 meetings, each averaging 6 minutes, recorded across 30 conference rooms" with 35 speakers, captured on single-channel and multi-channel array devices, with ground-truth speaker-attributed transcripts. This is the closest match to real product acoustics.
- **Limits:** only about 24 hours of distinct meetings. Dev-set-2 is challenge-only and not in the open release.
- **Access:** create a Hugging Face token, set `HF_TOKEN`, and call `download_meeting_subset` from the repository.
- **Licence:** the README says CC BY 4.0 but also "The datasets are provided for open research", and the Hugging Face record has no licence tag. Have counsel read the data licence file or ask Microsoft before relying on it.
- **Used in:** [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge paper, 2024](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2024-1788).

**3. [ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)**
- **Contents:** naturally occurring research-group meetings with per-speaker headset channels, distant table microphones (not a geometric array, from memory) and speaker-attributed transcripts.
- **Limits:** academic rather than corporate meetings, recorded around 2000–2002 (from memory).
- **Access:** download from the Edinburgh site. The LDC copy (LDC2004S02) is under LDC terms, so avoid it.
- **Licence:** "The ICSI corpus and its annotations are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license."
- **Used in:** [Janin et al. 2003](https://doi.org/10.1109/icassp.2003.1198793).

**4. [DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)**
- **Contents:** real four-person dinner-party conversations on far-field array devices plus close-talk microphones (device layout from memory).
- **Use:** small, so best as far-field test or adaptation data.
- **Licence:** Community Data License Agreement Permissive 1.0, open download.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://openslr.org/150/)**
- **Contents:** home dinner parties recorded on multiple arrays; the training tarball is 97 GB.
- **Licence:** "Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0". Commercial use is allowed, but whether a trained model must carry the same licence is unsettled. Using it only as a test set avoids the question.
- **Used in:** [CHiME-7 DASR, 2023](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1), alongside DiPCo and Mixer 6.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets/tree/main/earnings21)** (Rev.com)
- **Contents:** 39 hours of real earnings calls with a speaker id on every reference token.
- **Fit:** good for business vocabulary and long-form multi-speaker evaluation, but it is phone and webcast audio.
- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0, with the same share-alike caveat as CHiME-6.

**7. LDC via for-profit membership** (for example [NIST Meeting Pilot, LDC2004S09](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09), [Mixer 6, LDC2013S03](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2013S03), Fisher)
- **Terms:** the [LDC licensing page](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing) says "For-profit organizations who are or were LDC members may conduct commercial technology development with LDC data". Nonmembers, including companies paying the non-member fee, "cannot use LDC data to develop or test products for commercialization".
- **Steps:** ask LDC for a for-profit quote, join, then license older corpora at the reduced member fee. Check each corpus-specific agreement.
- **Cost and time:** tens of thousands of US dollars a year (from memory), and weeks to complete.
- **Value:** mainly large telephone conversational sets and a few small meeting-room sets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Defined.ai "Meeting Recordings":** search snippets describe 99,500 hours of English meetings with audio, video and transcripts, and the vendor says its datasets are cleared for commercial use. The catalogue page would not load, so speaker labels, capture conditions and price are unknown. Ask whether transcripts carry timed speaker turns and whether the audio is far-field or online-meeting capture.
- **Nexdata and Magic Data:** they list English conversational sets of 172 to 1,178 hours with paid commercial licences. The snippets describe these as close-talk or speaker-separated dialogue, not far-field meetings.
- **Earnings-22:** 119 hours in the same Rev repository. I did not confirm its licence or whether it has speaker labels.
- **ELRA CHIL seminars and Fearless Steps (Apollo):** both may fit from memory. I did not check them today.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial.
- **VoxConverse:** released "for research purposes", and the audio is taken from YouTube videos the dataset does not own.
- **DIHARD II/III:** the LDC non-member agreement gives no commercial rights.
- **NOTSOFAR simulated training set, LibriCSS, LibriWASN:** simulated or replayed speech.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4:** Mandarin (from memory).

## What I could not find
- A large, far-field corpus of genuine corporate meetings in English under a commercial licence.
- A vendor listing that confirms both microphone-array capture and speaker-turn labels.
- Search coverage was incomplete: one Hugging Face registry query failed.

## Next step
Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1's eval set as your product-like benchmark. In parallel, send Defined.ai and Nexdata the two questions above. Because CC licences cover copyright but not participant consent or voice-data privacy, get a short legal review before shipping models trained on any of these.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-4TKw7J/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://openslr.org/150/)**
- **Contents:** home dinner parties recorded on multiple arrays; the training tarball is 97 GB.
- **Licence:** "Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0". Commercial use is allowed, but whether a trained model must carry the same licence is unsettled. Using it only as a test set avoids the question.
- **Used in:** [CHiME-7 DASR, 2023](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1), alongside DiPCo and Mixer 6.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets/tree/main/earnings21)** (Rev.com)
- **Contents:** 39 hours of real earnings calls with a speaker id on every reference token.
- **Fit:** good for business vocabulary and long-form multi-speaker evaluation, but it is phone and webcast audio.
- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0, with the same share-alike caveat as CHiME-6.

**7. LDC via for-profit membership** (for example [NIST Meeting Pilot, LDC2004S09](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09), [Mixer 6, LDC2013S03](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2013S03), Fisher)
- **Terms:** the [LDC licensing page](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing) says "For-profit organizations who are or were LDC members may conduct commercial technology development with LDC data". Nonmembers, including companies paying the non-member fee, "cannot use LDC data to develop or test products for commercialization".
- **Steps:** ask LDC for a for-profit quote, join, then license older corpora at the reduced member fee. Check each corpus-specific agreement.
- **Cost and time:** tens of thousands of US dollars a year (from memory), and weeks to complete.
- **Value:** mainly large telephone conversational sets and a few small meeting-room sets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Defined.ai "Meeting Recordings":** search snippets describe 99,500 hours of English meetings with audio, video and transcripts, and the vendor says its datasets are cleared for commercial use. The catalogue page would not load, so speaker labels, capture conditions and price are unknown. Ask whether transcripts carry timed speaker turns and whether the audio is far-field or online-meeting capture.
- **Nexdata and Magic Data:** they list English conversational sets of 172 to 1,178 hours with paid commercial licences. The snippets describe these as close-talk or speaker-separated dialogue, not far-field meetings.
- **Earnings-22:** 119 hours in the same Rev repository. I did not confirm its licence or whether it has speaker labels.
- **ELRA CHIL seminars and Fearless Steps (Apollo):** both may fit from memory. I did not check them today.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial.
- **VoxConverse:** released "for research purposes", and the audio is taken from YouTube videos the dataset does not own.
- **DIHARD II/III:** the LDC non-member agreement gives no commercial rights.
- **NOTSOFAR simulated training set, LibriCSS, LibriWASN:** simulated or replayed speech.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4:** Mandarin (from memory).

## What I could not find
- A large, far-field corpus of genuine corporate meetings in English under a commercial licence.
- A vendor listing that confirms both microphone-array capture and speaker-turn labels.
- Search coverage was incomplete: one Hugging Face registry query failed.

## Next step
Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1's eval set as your product-like benchmark. In parallel, send Defined.ai and Nexdata the two questions above. Because CC licences cover copyright but not participant consent or voice-data privacy, get a short legal review before shipping models trained on any of these.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-4TKw7J/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Start with **AMI**, **NOTSOFAR-1** and **ICSI**: all three are real English meetings with speaker-attributed transcripts and distant-microphone audio, and all three are released under CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution. Together they give you roughly 200 hours you can download today. Nothing I found offers hundreds of hours of genuine corporate meetings with far-field audio under a commercial licence.

All facts below were checked on 2026-11-12 against the named pages unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need
- **Must:** real recorded multi-party conversation (no simulated mixtures), speaker-turn annotation, English, and a licence that allows commercial use (a fee is acceptable).
- **Nice to have:** business-style meetings, and far-field or microphone-array audio.
- **My assumption:** "commercial use" means training and evaluating models that ship in your product, not redistributing the audio.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AMI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 100 h | Strong | today |
| 2 | NOTSOFAR-1 recorded meetings | Free Hugging Face account and token | CC BY 4.0, with "for open research" wording | 237 meetings of about 6 min | Strong | today |
| 3 | ICSI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | about 72 h, 75 meetings | Strong | licence today; size from a search result |
| 4 | DiPCo | Direct download | CDLA-Permissive 1.0 | about 5 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party | today |
| 5 | CHiME-6 | Direct download | CC BY-SA 4.0 | about 40–50 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party, share-alike | today |
| 6 | Earnings-21 | Direct download | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 39 h | Partial: business, not far-field | today |
| 7 | LDC corpora via for-profit membership | Membership agreement and fee, weeks | LDC member agreement | varies | Partial | terms today; sizes and fee from memory |

## Details

**1. [AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)**
- **Contents:** 100 hours of recorded meetings with headset, lapel and microphone-array channels, plus manual transcripts with speaker and timing.
- **Limits:** most meetings are role-played ("participants play different roles in a fictitious design team"), so they are business-style but elicited. The recordings come from a small number of instrumented rooms in the mid-2000s (from memory).
- **Access:** pick meetings and signals on the [download page](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/download/) and fetch the 22 MB manual annotations file.
- **Licence:** "The AMI corpus and its annotations are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license."
- **Used in:** [Carletta 2007](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-007-9040-x) (corpus description) and [ECAPA-TDNN diarization, 2021](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2021-941).

**2. [NOTSOFAR-1](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)** (Microsoft)
- **Contents:** "237 meetings, each averaging 6 minutes, recorded across 30 conference rooms" with 35 speakers, captured on single-channel and multi-channel array devices, with ground-truth speaker-attributed transcripts. This is the closest match to real product acoustics.
- **Limits:** only about 24 hours of distinct meetings. Dev-set-2 is challenge-only and not in the open release.
- **Access:** create a Hugging Face token, set `HF_TOKEN`, and call `download_meeting_subset` from the repository.
- **Licence:** the README says CC BY 4.0 but also "The datasets are provided for open research", and the Hugging Face record has no licence tag. Have counsel read the data licence file or ask Microsoft before relying on it.
- **Used in:** [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge paper, 2024](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2024-1788).

**3. [ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)**
- **Contents:** naturally occurring research-group meetings with per-speaker headset channels, distant table microphones (not a geometric array, from memory) and speaker-attributed transcripts.
- **Limits:** academic rather than corporate meetings, recorded around 2000–2002 (from memory).
- **Access:** download from the Edinburgh site. The LDC copy (LDC2004S02) is under LDC terms, so avoid it.
- **Licence:** "The ICSI corpus and its annotations are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license."
- **Used in:** [Janin et al. 2003](https://doi.org/10.1109/icassp.2003.1198793).

**4. [DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)**
- **Contents:** real four-person dinner-party conversations on far-field array devices plus close-talk microphones (device layout from memory).
- **Use:** small, so best as far-field test or adaptation data.
- **Licence:** Community Data License Agreement Permissive 1.0, open download.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://openslr.org/150/)**
- **Contents:** home dinner parties recorded on multiple arrays; the training tarball is 97 GB.
- **Licence:** "Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0". Commercial use is allowed, but whether a trained model must carry the same licence is unsettled. Using it only as a test set avoids the question.
- **Used in:** [CHiME-7 DASR, 2023](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1), alongside DiPCo and Mixer 6.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets/tree/main/earnings21)** (Rev.com)
- **Contents:** 39 hours of real earnings calls with a speaker id on every reference token.
- **Fit:** good for business vocabulary and long-form multi-speaker evaluation, but it is phone and webcast audio.
- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0, with the same share-alike caveat as CHiME-6.

**7. LDC via for-profit membership** (for example [NIST Meeting Pilot, LDC2004S09](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09), [Mixer 6, LDC2013S03](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2013S03), Fisher)
- **Terms:** the [LDC licensing page](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing) says "For-profit organizations who are or were LDC members may conduct commercial technology development with LDC data". Nonmembers, including companies paying the non-member fee, "cannot use LDC data to develop or test products for commercialization".
- **Steps:** ask LDC for a for-profit quote, join, then license older corpora at the reduced member fee. Check each corpus-specific agreement.
- **Cost and time:** tens of thousands of US dollars a year (from memory), and weeks to complete.
- **Value:** mainly large telephone conversational sets and a few small meeting-room sets.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Defined.ai "Meeting Recordings":** search snippets describe 99,500 hours of English meetings with audio, video and transcripts, and the vendor says its datasets are cleared for commercial use. The catalogue page would not load, so speaker labels, capture conditions and price are unknown. Ask whether transcripts carry timed speaker turns and whether the audio is far-field or online-meeting capture.
- **Nexdata and Magic Data:** they list English conversational sets of 172 to 1,178 hours with paid commercial licences. The snippets describe these as close-talk or speaker-separated dialogue, not far-field meetings.
- **Earnings-22:** 119 hours in the same Rev repository. I did not confirm its licence or whether it has speaker labels.
- **ELRA CHIL seminars and Fearless Steps (Apollo):** both may fit from memory. I did not check them today.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial.
- **VoxConverse:** released "for research purposes", and the audio is taken from YouTube videos the dataset does not own.
- **DIHARD II/III:** the LDC non-member agreement gives no commercial rights.
- **NOTSOFAR simulated training set, LibriCSS, LibriWASN:** simulated or replayed speech.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4:** Mandarin (from memory).

## What I could not find
- A large, far-field corpus of genuine corporate meetings in English under a commercial licence.
- A vendor listing that confirms both microphone-array capture and speaker-turn labels.
- Search coverage was incomplete: one Hugging Face registry query failed.

## Next step
Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1's eval set as your product-like benchmark. In parallel, send Defined.ai and Nexdata the two questions above. Because CC licences cover copyright but not participant consent or voice-data privacy, get a short legal review before shipping models trained on any of these.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-4TKw7J/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

## Details

**1. [AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)**
- **Contents:** about 100 hours with close-talking and far-field microphones; 8-microphone circular arrays (from memory).
- **Fit:** the standard meeting diarization benchmark, and the meetings are design-team project meetings.
- **Limits:** about two-thirds is role-played scenario; the rest is naturally occurring meetings. It was recorded in three rooms in the mid-2000s (from memory).
- **Licence:** the page says signals, transcription and "some of the annotations" are CC BY 4.0, so check the note on the annotation download.
- **Access:** follow the site's Download page, or use the [Hugging Face copy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/edinburghcstr/ami).
- **Paper:** [Unleashing the killer corpus](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-007-9040-x) (2007).

**2. [NOTSOFAR-1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/NOTSOFAR)**
- **Contents:** 315 meetings in 30 office conference rooms, 4–8 attendees, about 35 speakers. Far-field devices include 7-channel arrays, plus close-talk microphones.
- **Annotations:** speaker ID per utterance and word-level timings.
- **Fit:** the closest match to a modern product setting, but small. The separate 1000-hour training set is simulated, so leave it out.
- **Licence conflict:** the dataset card and the [DATA_LICENSE file](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge/blob/main/DATA_LICENSE) both say CC BY 4.0. The older [CHiME-8 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data) still says challenge-only, and one third-party comparison table lists it as non-commercial. I'd rely on the licence file, but save a dated copy.
- **Access:** clone the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge) and download with its script or AzCopy.
- **Papers:** [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2024-1788) (2024); [DiCoW](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csl.2025.101841) (2025).

**3. [ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)**
- **Contents:** about 70 hours of natural research-group meetings (not role-played, from memory).
- **Limits:** academic rather than business meetings. The page mentions only close-talking microphones; tabletop distant microphones exist in the corpus from memory, so check they are in the download.
- **Access:** follow the site's download page. Avoid the [LDC copy](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02), which carries a non-commercial non-member agreement for the same audio.

**4. [DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)**
- Four-person conversations recorded on five far-field 7-microphone arrays plus close-talk. Good far-field test data, but it is a dinner party.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://www.openslr.org/150/)**
- Dinner parties in homes with multiple arrays (from memory); the training archive alone is 97 GB.
- Share-alike applies to adapted material, and whether a trained model counts is unsettled, so ask counsel before training a shipped model on it.
- **Paper:** [CHiME-7 DASR](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1) (2023), which also uses DiPCo.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets)**
- 39 hours of earnings calls: real business vocabulary and long recordings, but call audio. Speaker labels are from memory. The same share-alike caveat applies.

**7. LDC: [ISL Meeting Speech](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S05), [NIST Meeting Pilot](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09)**
- Commercial use requires [for-profit membership](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing); a search result put it at about $24,000 a year, which I did not confirm.
- Poor value for these small, old corpora unless you want other LDC data too.

**8. [Nexdata 172 h](https://www.nexdata.ai/datasets/speechrecog/1770)**
- "Paid dataset licensed for commercial use" with timestamps and speaker IDs, but smartphone-recorded prompted dialogues. It adds speaker variety, not meeting acoustics.

## Known, not confirmed
- **CHIL evaluation packages (ELRA):** seminar and meeting recordings with arrays. Search snippets show a commercial licence at several thousand euros, but the [ELRA catalogue](https://catalogue.elra.info/en-us/repository/browse/ELRA-E0017/) timed out today, so content and price are unverified.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA, so non-commercial.
- **[MagicData English open sample](https://magichub.com/datasets/multi-stream-spontaneous-conversation-training-datasets_english/):** CC BY-NC-ND; the commercial version is by quote and is not far-field.
- **VoxConverse:** offered "for research purposes", built on YouTube audio, and not meetings.
- **LibriCSS:** read speech replayed in a room, not real conversation.
- **AliMeeting / AISHELL-4:** Mandarin.
- **DIHARD III / Mixer 6:** LDC terms, and not meetings.

## What I could not find
- No large commercially licensed corpus of real English far-field business meetings, either open or off the shelf.
- Searches of Defined.ai, Appen, Shaip and Nexdata showed no such product; they offer custom collection instead.

## Next step
1. Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1 as your most realistic test set.
2. If that is not enough, the realistic paid route is a custom collection from a vendor, or your own recordings with consent, in your target rooms and devices.
3. Ask counsel about speaker consent and voice-data privacy; a CC licence covers copyright only.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-0XYr2E/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

- **Access:** clone the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge) and download with its script or AzCopy.
- **Papers:** [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2024-1788) (2024); [DiCoW](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csl.2025.101841) (2025).

**3. [ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)**
- **Contents:** about 70 hours of natural research-group meetings (not role-played, from memory).
- **Limits:** academic rather than business meetings. The page mentions only close-talking microphones; tabletop distant microphones exist in the corpus from memory, so check they are in the download.
- **Access:** follow the site's download page. Avoid the [LDC copy](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02), which carries a non-commercial non-member agreement for the same audio.

**4. [DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)**
- Four-person conversations recorded on five far-field 7-microphone arrays plus close-talk. Good far-field test data, but it is a dinner party.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://www.openslr.org/150/)**
- Dinner parties in homes with multiple arrays (from memory); the training archive alone is 97 GB.
- Share-alike applies to adapted material, and whether a trained model counts is unsettled, so ask counsel before training a shipped model on it.
- **Paper:** [CHiME-7 DASR](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1) (2023), which also uses DiPCo.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets)**
- 39 hours of earnings calls: real business vocabulary and long recordings, but call audio. Speaker labels are from memory. The same share-alike caveat applies.

**7. LDC: [ISL Meeting Speech](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S05), [NIST Meeting Pilot](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09)**
- Commercial use requires [for-profit membership](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing); a search result put it at about $24,000 a year, which I did not confirm.
- Poor value for these small, old corpora unless you want other LDC data too.

**8. [Nexdata 172 h](https://www.nexdata.ai/datasets/speechrecog/1770)**
- "Paid dataset licensed for commercial use" with timestamps and speaker IDs, but smartphone-recorded prompted dialogues. It adds speaker variety, not meeting acoustics.

## Known, not confirmed
- **CHIL evaluation packages (ELRA):** seminar and meeting recordings with arrays. Search snippets show a commercial licence at several thousand euros, but the [ELRA catalogue](https://catalogue.elra.info/en-us/repository/browse/ELRA-E0017/) timed out today, so content and price are unverified.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA, so non-commercial.
- **[MagicData English open sample](https://magichub.com/datasets/multi-stream-spontaneous-conversation-training-datasets_english/):** CC BY-NC-ND; the commercial version is by quote and is not far-field.
- **VoxConverse:** offered "for research purposes", built on YouTube audio, and not meetings.
- **LibriCSS:** read speech replayed in a room, not real conversation.
- **AliMeeting / AISHELL-4:** Mandarin.
- **DIHARD III / Mixer 6:** LDC terms, and not meetings.

## What I could not find
- No large commercially licensed corpus of real English far-field business meetings, either open or off the shelf.
- Searches of Defined.ai, Appen, Shaip and Nexdata showed no such product; they offer custom collection instead.

## Next step
1. Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1 as your most realistic test set.
2. If that is not enough, the realistic paid route is a custom collection from a vendor, or your own recordings with consent, in your target rooms and devices.
3. Ask counsel about speaker consent and voice-data privacy; a CC licence covers copyright only.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-0XYr2E/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.
