- **Nice to have:** business-style meetings, far-field or microphone-array audio.
- **Assumption:** you want data for both training and evaluation.

## Shortlist

| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AMI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | ~100 h | Strong | today |
| 2 | NOTSOFAR-1 (Microsoft) | Direct download (AzCopy) | CC BY 4.0, with a conflict noted below | 315 meetings, ~6 min each | Strong | today |
| 3 | ICSI Meeting Corpus | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | ~70 h | Strong | today |
| 4 | DiPCo | Direct download | CDLA-Permissive 1.0 | ~5 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party | today |
| 5 | CHiME-6 | Direct download | CC BY-SA 4.0 | ~50 h (from memory) | Partial: dinner party, share-alike | today |
| 6 | Earnings-21 (Rev) | Direct download (Git LFS) | CC BY-SA 4.0 | 39 h | Partial: calls, not far-field | today |
| 7 | LDC meeting corpora (ISL, NIST Pilot) | For-profit membership fee, weeks | LDC agreement | ~10–15 h each (from memory) | Partial | terms via search |
| 8 | Nexdata 172 h US English dialogue | Paid, quote from vendor | Vendor commercial licence | 172 h | Weak: phone close-talk | today |

## Details

**1. [AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)**
- **Contents:** about 100 hours with close-talking and far-field microphones; 8-microphone circular arrays (from memory).
- **Fit:** the standard meeting diarization benchmark, and the meetings are design-team project meetings.
- **Limits:** about two-thirds is role-played scenario; the rest is naturally occurring meetings. It was recorded in three rooms in the mid-2000s (from memory).
- **Licence:** the page says signals, transcription and "some of the annotations" are CC BY 4.0, so check the note on the annotation download.
- **Access:** follow the site's Download page, or use the [Hugging Face copy](https://huggingface.co/datasets/edinburghcstr/ami).
- **Paper:** [Unleashing the killer corpus](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-007-9040-x) (2007).

**2. [NOTSOFAR-1](https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/NOTSOFAR)**
- **Contents:** 315 meetings in 30 office conference rooms, 4–8 attendees, about 35 speakers. Far-field devices include 7-channel arrays, plus close-talk microphones.
- **Annotations:** speaker ID per utterance and word-level timings.
- **Fit:** the closest match to a modern product setting, but small. The separate 1000-hour training set is simulated, so leave it out.
- **Licence conflict:** the dataset card and the [DATA_LICENSE file](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge/blob/main/DATA_LICENSE) both say CC BY 4.0. The older [CHiME-8 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data) still says challenge-only, and one third-party comparison table lists it as non-commercial. I'd rely on the licence file, but save a dated copy.
- **Access:** clone the [GitHub repo](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge) and download with its script or AzCopy.
- **Papers:** [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge](https://doi.org/10.21437/interspeech.2024-1788) (2024); [DiCoW](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csl.2025.101841) (2025).

**3. [ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)**
- **Contents:** about 70 hours of natural research-group meetings (not role-played, from memory).
- **Limits:** academic rather than business meetings. The page mentions only close-talking microphones; tabletop distant microphones exist in the corpus from memory, so check they are in the download.
- **Access:** follow the site's download page. Avoid the [LDC copy](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S02), which carries a non-commercial non-member agreement for the same audio.

**4. [DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)**
- Four-person conversations recorded on five far-field 7-microphone arrays plus close-talk. Good far-field test data, but it is a dinner party.

**5. [CHiME-6](https://www.openslr.org/150/)**
- Dinner parties in homes with multiple arrays (from memory); the training archive alone is 97 GB.
- Share-alike applies to adapted material, and whether a trained model counts is unsettled, so ask counsel before training a shipped model on it.
- **Paper:** [CHiME-7 DASR](https://doi.org/10.21437/chime.2023-1) (2023), which also uses DiPCo.

**6. [Earnings-21](https://github.com/revdotcom/speech-datasets)**
- 39 hours of earnings calls: real business vocabulary and long recordings, but call audio. Speaker labels are from memory. The same share-alike caveat applies.

**7. LDC: [ISL Meeting Speech](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S05), [NIST Meeting Pilot](https://catalog.ldc.upenn.edu/LDC2004S09)**
- Commercial use requires [for-profit membership](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing); a search result put it at about $24,000 a year, which I did not confirm.
- Poor value for these small, old corpora unless you want other LDC data too.

**8. [Nexdata 172 h](https://www.nexdata.ai/datasets/speechrecog/1770)**
- "Paid dataset licensed for commercial use" with timestamps and speaker IDs, but smartphone-recorded prompted dialogues. It adds speaker variety, not meeting acoustics.

## Known, not confirmed
- **CHIL evaluation packages (ELRA):** seminar and meeting recordings with arrays. Search snippets show a commercial licence at several thousand euros, but the [ELRA catalogue](https://catalogue.elra.info/en-us/repository/browse/ELRA-E0017/) timed out today, so content and price are unverified.

## Not recommended, and why
- **MeetingBank:** CC BY-NC-SA, so non-commercial.
- **[MagicData English open sample](https://magichub.com/datasets/multi-stream-spontaneous-conversation-training-datasets_english/):** CC BY-NC-ND; the commercial version is by quote and is not far-field.
- **VoxConverse:** offered "for research purposes", built on YouTube audio, and not meetings.
- **LibriCSS:** read speech replayed in a room, not real conversation.
- **AliMeeting / AISHELL-4:** Mandarin.
- **DIHARD III / Mixer 6:** LDC terms, and not meetings.

## What I could not find
- No large commercially licensed corpus of real English far-field business meetings, either open or off the shelf.
- Searches of Defined.ai, Appen, Shaip and Nexdata showed no such product; they offer custom collection instead.

## Next step
1. Download AMI, NOTSOFAR-1 and ICSI today, and hold out NOTSOFAR-1 as your most realistic test set.
2. If that is not enough, the realistic paid route is a custom collection from a vendor, or your own recordings with consent, in your target rooms and devices.
3. Ask counsel about speaker consent and voice-data privacy; a CC licence covers copyright only.

The interactive shortlist is at `/private/tmp/e-0XYr2E/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Start with AMI, ICSI and NOTSOFAR-1.** All three are real recorded English meetings with speaker-turn annotations, and all are CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution and no fee. I checked the licences on the official pages today, except where noted below.

| Corpus | What it is | Far-field / array | Licence | Caveats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)** | 100 h of meetings, with word-level transcripts and speaker segments | Yes: microphone arrays plus headset and lapel mics | CC BY 4.0 | About two-thirds are scenario meetings (role-played design-team projects, though genuinely recorded); many non-native speakers |
| **[ICSI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)** | About 70 h of naturally occurring research-group meetings | Partly: a few distant tabletop mics (from memory, not a proper array), plus close-talk | CC BY 4.0 | Technical/academic content; early-2000s recordings |
| **[NOTSOFAR-1](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)** (Microsoft) | Roughly 240–315 short meetings (about 6 min each), 4–8 attendees, about 30 conference rooms | Yes: commercial far-field array devices, plus close-talk references | CC BY 4.0 per the GitHub repo and [Hugging Face card](https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/NOTSOFAR) | Only about 35 unique speakers; one dev subset is flagged challenge-only |

NOTSOFAR-1 is the closest match to modern conference-room audio, but confirm its licence before you rely on it. The [CHiME-8 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data) still carries older challenge-only wording, and I did not open the licence file in the repo itself.

**Useful supplements, but not business meetings:**
- **[DiPCo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)** (Amazon): about 5 h across 10 dinner-party sessions of 4 speakers, with five 7-mic far-field arrays plus close-talk. It is CDLA-Permissive 1.0, so commercial use is fine, and it works well as a held-out far-field test set.
- **[CHiME-6](https://www.openslr.org/150/)**: real dinner parties recorded on multiple far-field arrays, with heavy overlap and noise. It is CC BY-SA 4.0, which allows commercial use, but have counsel look at the ShareAlike clause before training shipped models on it.

**If you need more or closer-matched data, these are the paid routes:**
- **LDC**: it holds the NIST meeting sets and conversational telephone corpora (Fisher, Switchboard, CALLHOME). Commercial rights generally require a for-profit membership, and terms vary by corpus, so check each agreement.
- **Commercial vendors** (Appen, Defined.ai, Datatang, Shaip and similar): they sell off-the-shelf or custom-collected meeting recordings with diarization labels. I have not checked their current catalogues or prices.

**What I'd avoid:**
- **VoxConverse** and other YouTube-derived sets: the annotations are openly licensed, but the underlying audio rights are not cleared.
- **LibriCSS**: it is replayed mixtures, not real conversations.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4**: both are Mandarin.

Public data alone won't cover your speaker and room diversity, since AMI and ICSI come from a handful of rooms and NOTSOFAR-1 has few speakers. I'd train on those three and build a small in-domain evaluation set from your own consented recordings as early as you can.

Sources:
- [AMI Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/)
- [ICSI Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/)
- [NOTSOFAR-1 GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)
- [NOTSOFAR on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/NOTSOFAR)
- [NOTSOFAR-1 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08887)
- [CHiME-8 Task 2 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data)
- [CHiME-6 on OpenSLR](https://www.openslr.org/150/)
- [DiPCo on Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/8122551)
- [DiPCo paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.13447)

Judge votes✓ ✓ ✓
Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Use the AMI Meeting Corpus as your core dataset, and add ICSI and NOTSOFAR-1.** All three are real recorded English meetings with speaker-turn annotations and far-field audio, and all are CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution and no fee.

I checked the licence pages for AMI, ICSI, NOTSOFAR-1 and CHiME-6 today. The DiPCo licence and the LDC terms come from search results, and the corpus sizes for AMI, DiPCo and CHiME-6 are from memory.

| Dataset | What it is | Far-field audio | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AMI** | About 100 h of 4-person meetings; roughly two-thirds are role-played design-team scenarios, the rest natural meetings | 8-mic circular arrays, plus headset and lapel mics | CC BY 4.0 |
| **ICSI Meeting Corpus** | About 72 h across 75 natural research-group meetings, 53 speakers | Tabletop distant mics plus headsets | CC BY 4.0 |
| **NOTSOFAR-1** (Microsoft) | 237 short meetings (about 6 min each), 4–8 attendees, 30 conference rooms | Multi-channel and single-channel commercial meeting devices | CC BY 4.0 |
| **DiPCo** (Amazon) | About 5 h of 4-person dinner-party conversation | Multiple 7-mic arrays plus close-talk | CDLA-Permissive 1.0 |
| **CHiME-6** | About 40 h of 4-person dinner parties in real homes | Multiple Kinect arrays | CC BY-SA 4.0 |

- **AMI:** this is the closest match to business meetings and the standard diarization benchmark. The scenario meetings are acted, but they are real people talking in a real room, not simulated mixtures. Many speakers are non-native English speakers.
- **ICSI:** these are fully natural meetings with heavy overlap, but they are academic discussions, not business ones. Get it from the Edinburgh site; the LDC copy comes under LDC's own terms.
- **NOTSOFAR-1:** this is the most product-like acoustically, since it was recorded on actual conference-room devices. Two cautions:
  - The README says the data is "provided for open research" alongside the CC BY 4.0 grant. The licence itself has no non-commercial clause, but have counsel confirm.
  - Dev-set-2 is approved for the challenge only, so do not use it.
- **DiPCo and CHiME-6:** these are not meetings, but they add far-field robustness. The ShareAlike clause on CHiME-6 applies to derivatives of the data; whether that reaches trained models is unsettled, so get a legal view before training on it.

**What to avoid**
- **VoxConverse:** the annotations are CC BY, but the audio is YouTube video you would have no rights to.
- **LibriCSS:** it is replayed mixtures, not real conversation.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4:** these are Mandarin.
- **LDC corpora (NIST RT sets, DIHARD, CALLHOME):** commercial use requires for-profit LDC membership at the time you obtain the data, and corpus-specific agreements can still override that. I'd only go this route if you need the NIST RT meeting sets for evaluation.

One thing the licences do not cover is privacy. CC BY settles copyright, but these are recordings of identifiable voices. If you operate in the EU or under biometric-privacy laws, check the consent basis for each corpus.

Sources:
- [AMI corpus licence](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/license.shtml)
- [ICSI corpus licence](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/license.shtml)
- [NOTSOFAR-1 Challenge repo](https://github.com/microsoft/NOTSOFAR1-Challenge)
- [CHiME-8 Task 2 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data)
- [CHiME-6 on OpenSLR (SLR150)](https://www.openslr.org/150/)
- [DiPCo paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.13447)
- [Amazon Science DiPCo announcement](https://www.amazon.science/blog/amazon-releases-new-public-data-set-to-help-address-cocktail-party-problem)
- [DiPCo on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huckiyang/DiPCo)
- [LDC licensing policy](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing)

**Use the AMI Meeting Corpus as your core dataset, and add ICSI and NOTSOFAR-1.** All three are real recorded English meetings with speaker-turn annotations and far-field audio, and all are CC BY 4.0, which allows commercial use with attribution and no fee.

I checked the licence pages for AMI, ICSI, NOTSOFAR-1 and CHiME-6 today. The DiPCo licence and the LDC terms come from search results, and the corpus sizes for AMI, DiPCo and CHiME-6 are from memory.

| Dataset | What it is | Far-field audio | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AMI** | About 100 h of 4-person meetings; roughly two-thirds are role-played design-team scenarios, the rest natural meetings | 8-mic circular arrays, plus headset and lapel mics | CC BY 4.0 |
| **ICSI Meeting Corpus** | About 72 h across 75 natural research-group meetings, 53 speakers | Tabletop distant mics plus headsets | CC BY 4.0 |
| **NOTSOFAR-1** (Microsoft) | 237 short meetings (about 6 min each), 4–8 attendees, 30 conference rooms | Multi-channel and single-channel commercial meeting devices | CC BY 4.0 |
| **DiPCo** (Amazon) | About 5 h of 4-person dinner-party conversation | Multiple 7-mic arrays plus close-talk | CDLA-Permissive 1.0 |
| **CHiME-6** | About 40 h of 4-person dinner parties in real homes | Multiple Kinect arrays | CC BY-SA 4.0 |

- **AMI:** this is the closest match to business meetings and the standard diarization benchmark. The scenario meetings are acted, but they are real people talking in a real room, not simulated mixtures. Many speakers are non-native English speakers.
- **ICSI:** these are fully natural meetings with heavy overlap, but they are academic discussions, not business ones. Get it from the Edinburgh site; the LDC copy comes under LDC's own terms.
- **NOTSOFAR-1:** this is the most product-like acoustically, since it was recorded on actual conference-room devices. Two cautions:
  - The README says the data is "provided for open research" alongside the CC BY 4.0 grant. The licence itself has no non-commercial clause, but have counsel confirm.
  - Dev-set-2 is approved for the challenge only, so do not use it.
- **DiPCo and CHiME-6:** these are not meetings, but they add far-field robustness. The ShareAlike clause on CHiME-6 applies to derivatives of the data; whether that reaches trained models is unsettled, so get a legal view before training on it.

**What to avoid**
- **VoxConverse:** the annotations are CC BY, but the audio is YouTube video you would have no rights to.
- **LibriCSS:** it is replayed mixtures, not real conversation.
- **AliMeeting and AISHELL-4:** these are Mandarin.
- **LDC corpora (NIST RT sets, DIHARD, CALLHOME):** commercial use requires for-profit LDC membership at the time you obtain the data, and corpus-specific agreements can still override that. I'd only go this route if you need the NIST RT meeting sets for evaluation.

One thing the licences do not cover is privacy. CC BY settles copyright, but these are recordings of identifiable voices. If you operate in the EU or under biometric-privacy laws, check the consent basis for each corpus.

- [ICSI corpus licence](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/icsi/license.shtml)

- [CHiME-8 Task 2 data page](https://www.chimechallenge.org/challenges/chime8/task2/data)
- [CHiME-6 on OpenSLR (SLR150)](https://www.openslr.org/150/)

- [DiPCo on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huckiyang/DiPCo)
- [LDC licensing policy](https://www.ldc.upenn.edu/data-management/using/licensing)

Prompt

We're a small startup building meeting transcription with speaker diarization. I'm looking for recordings of real multi-party conversations (not simulated mixtures), ideally business-style meetings, with speaker-turn annotations (who spoke when), preferably including far-field or microphone-array audio. English only. It's for a commercial product, so the licence has to allow commercial use. We can pay a reasonable licence fee if needed, but research-only or non-commercial data is out. What should we use?

Graders — what "good" means for this case
00-skill-firedtool_used
tool"Skill"
input_match"\"skill\"\\s*:\\s*\"(?:[\\w-]+:)?dataset-scout\""
01-recall-ami-meetingsllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the AMI Meeting Corpus (also called the AMI corpus or Augmented Multi-party Interaction corpus, about 100 hours of English meeting recordings from the University of Edinburgh / AMI consortium) as a candidate dataset for meeting diarization, in any version or subset. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-chime6-dinner-partyllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the CHiME-6 data (also known as the CHiME-5 dinner party corpus, the CHiME-5/CHiME-6 challenge recordings of home dinner parties with distant microphone arrays, OpenSLR resource SLR150, also reused in the CHiME-7/CHiME-8 DASR tasks) as a candidate dataset, in any version or distribution. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable or unavailable for commercial use.

03-recall-notsofar-meetingsllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists the NOTSOFAR-1 dataset (Natural Office Talkers in Settings of Far-field Audio Recordings, the Microsoft recorded-meeting dataset of the NOTSOFAR-1 / CHiME-8 Task 2 distant meeting transcription challenge) as a candidate dataset for meeting diarization, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-ami-cc-byllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the AMI Meeting Corpus and states that it is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence (CC BY 4.0), or otherwise states that its licence permits commercial use as long as attribution is given (for example "free to download, CC BY 4.0, commercial use allowed with credit"). FAIL if the answer does not mention AMI, gives no licence or permitted-use information for it, or states that AMI is non-commercial or research-only (for example calling it CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-SA).

05-access-chime-commercial-okllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the CHiME-6 (CHiME-5) dinner party data and states that the startup can use it commercially, either because it is now distributed on OpenSLR (SLR150) under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence (CC BY-SA 4.0), or because a commercial licence for it can be obtained. Mentioning the share-alike condition is welcome but not required. FAIL if the answer does not mention the CHiME-6/CHiME-5 data, gives no licensing information for it, or states that it is limited to research or non-commercial use, or that commercial use is impossible.

06-access-notsofar-cc-byllm

PASS if the final answer mentions the NOTSOFAR-1 meeting dataset and states that its data is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), or otherwise that its licence permits commercial use with attribution. FAIL if the answer does not mention NOTSOFAR-1, gives no licence or permitted-use information for it, or states that it is limited to research, non-commercial use or challenge participation only.

07-trap-libricss-replayedllm

PASS if the final answer does not present LibriCSS (the Microsoft continuous speech separation dataset made by playing back concatenated LibriSpeech utterances through loudspeakers in an office room and re-recording them with a distant microphone array) as a recording of real multi-party conversations or meetings. Not mentioning it passes; mentioning it while noting that it is simulated, replayed or read speech rather than real conversation also passes. FAIL if the answer recommends LibriCSS as real meeting or conversation recordings that meet the requirement for real multi-party conversations.

08-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists at least one of these less known English multi-party conversation corpora as a candidate: (a) the ICSI Meeting Corpus (about 70 hours of meetings recorded at the International Computer Science Institute, Berkeley, now also distributed by the University of Edinburgh under CC BY 4.0); (b) DiPCo, the Dinner Party Corpus from Amazon (recorded dinner-party conversations with far-field microphone arrays, CDLA-Permissive licence). FAIL if the answer mentions neither of them as a candidate.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
Download **`mwalmsley/gz_desi`** from Hugging Face: about 399k galaxies, images bundled with volunteer vote counts, and separate strong-bar, weak-bar and graded-merger labels. If you want something smaller to start with, `mwalmsley/gz2` (191k SDSS galaxies, 2.6 GB) has the same format. Everything below was checked on 2026-11-12 unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** at least 40,000 galaxies.
- **R2 (must):** labels from humans (volunteer votes or experts), not model output.
- **R3 (must):** detailed features: bars, spiral arms, bulge size, mergers.
- **R4 (nice):** images bundled with the labels.
- **R5 (must):** free and downloadable now. I assumed non-commercial thesis use and that you can publish your code.

## Shortlist
| # | Dataset | Access | Licence | Size | Fit | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GZ DESI (`mwalmsley/gz_desi`) | Open download; card asks for a free HF login | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 + release your model code | 399,413 images, 17.5 GB | Strong | today |
| 2 | Galaxy Zoo 2 (`mwalmsley/gz2`) | Same | Same | 191,174 images, 2.6 GB | Strong | today |
| 3 | GZ Evo (`mwalmsley/gz_evo`) | Same | Same | 805,979 images, 18 GB | Strong | today |
| 4 | Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 314k galaxies, 108 GB | Strong | today |
| 5 | Galaxy Zoo 2 images (Zenodo) + vote table | Direct download, two sources | CC BY 4.0 (images) | 243,434 images, 3.4 GB | Strong | today |
| 6 | GZ Euclid (`mwalmsley/gz_euclid`) | Open download | None stated | 172,277 images, 0.5 GB | Partial | today |
| 7 | Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS (Zenodo) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 71,052 galaxies, 7.9 GB | Partial | today |
| 8 | GZ Hubble (`mwalmsley/gz_hubble`) | Open download; HF login | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 + code release | 96,449 images, 6.4 GB | Partial | today |
| 9 | Galaxy Zoo Cosmic Dawn (Zenodo) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | about 45.7k images, 5.1 GB | Partial | today |
| 10 | Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge | Free account + accept rules | Competition rules | 61,578 training images | Partial | page exists today; terms and size from memory |

## Details

**1. GZ DESI** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_desi
- **Contents:** 424×424 images plus one column per answer; the card says "The values are the count of volunteers who selected each answer."
- **Why it fits:** columns include `bar-dr5_strong/weak/no`, `merging-dr5_merger/major-disturbance/minor-disturbance/none`, bulge size, spiral arm count and winding.
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_desi', split='train')`. Try `name='tiny'` first.
- **Catches:** there are three campaigns (dr12, dr5, dr8) with slightly different questions. Many DR5/DR8 galaxies have only about five votes, so filter on the `*_total-votes` columns.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".

**2. Galaxy Zoo 2** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz2
- **Contents:** SDSS images with vote counts for bar (yes/no), bulge size (four levels), spiral arm count and winding.
- **Catches:** bars are yes/no only, and mergers sit under the "odd feature" question (from memory). It is the most heavily used set in this field.
- **Paper:** Willett et al. 2013, https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458.

**3. GZ Evo** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_evo
- **Contents:** GZ2, DESI, CANDELS, Hubble and UKIDSS combined and pre-shuffled.
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so you need a masked or multi-head loss. This is more than a master's thesis usually needs.

**4. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** — https://zenodo.org/records/4573248
- **Why consider it:** this is the original release behind most of #1, under plain CC BY 4.0 with no code-release condition.
- **Access:** download `gz_decals_volunteers_5.parquet`, `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2.parquet` and the four PNG zips (21–33 GB each), then join on `iauname`.
- **Catch:** ignore `gz_decals_auto_posteriors.*`, which are model predictions. Not every image has volunteer labels.

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 images** — https://zenodo.org/records/3565489
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`. The labels are the "GZ2 – Table 1 – Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" CSV at https://data.galaxyzoo.org/, joined through the mapping file.
- **Catch:** the licence of the tables on data.galaxyzoo.org was not stated on the page I read.

**6. GZ Euclid** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid
- **Contents:** Euclid space-telescope cutouts with the newest schema: strong/weak bar, five bulge sizes, graded mergers, clumps.
- **Catches:** the card is empty and states no licence. The columns are vote counts and `total-votes`, which indicates volunteer labels, but nothing on the card confirms it. Ask the maintainer before relying on it.

**7. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS** — https://zenodo.org/records/13357341
- **Contents:** near-infrared images of GZ2 galaxies; "The catalog contains volunteer vote counts", using the same question tree as GZ2.
- **Catch:** spiral structure is weaker in the infrared, and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**8. GZ Hubble** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_hubble
- **Contents:** HST galaxies with volunteer vote counts.
- **Catch:** these are distant, small, noisy galaxies; only useful if your thesis covers higher redshift.

**9. Galaxy Zoo Cosmic Dawn** — https://zenodo.org/records/17200992
- **Contents:** two image zips (15,745 + 29,997) plus `gzcd_volunteer_classifications.parquet`.
- **Catches:** skip the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. It barely clears 40k, the galaxies are faint, and I did not inspect the question schema.

**10. Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge** — https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge
- **Contents (from memory):** 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote-fraction columns.
- **Access (from memory):** free account, then accept the competition rules.
- **Catch:** the IDs are anonymised and it is a subset of GZ2, so #2 or #5 is the better choice.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Kaggle terms and counts (#10):** the page exists but is drawn by JavaScript, so I could not read it. Check the Data and Rules tabs.
- **Galaxy Zoo GAMA-KiDS (about 49k, from memory):** I did not find a standalone release in the registries; look on data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **GZ CANDELS:** the Hugging Face copy (`mwalmsley/gz_candels`, 48,098 images) passed the existence check, but I did not check its fit beyond size; it is high-redshift HST imaging.

## Not recommended, and why
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/8360385): "created by training deep learning models on Galaxy Zoo volunteer responses". These are predictions with no images.
- **Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/15106473): "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and Galaxy10 SDSS:** roughly 18k and 22k images in 10 coarse classes (sizes from memory), so too small and no per-feature labels.
- **Galaxy Zoo 1:** human votes, but only elliptical/spiral/merger and no images.
- **GZ2 catalogue record on Zenodo** (https://zenodo.org/records/3566991): "files are restricted"; use data.galaxyzoo.org instead.
- **`mwalmsley/gz_jwst_cosmos`:** gated and no licence stated.
- **Third-party Galaxy Zoo re-uploads on Hugging Face:** unverified provenance.

## What I could not find
- **Expert-labelled sets:** none with detailed features reaches 40k. The largest I know are Nair & Abraham 2010 (about 14k) and EFIGI (about 4.5k), both from memory. They could work as a small expert test set.
- **Recent CNN papers per release:** the paper search returned none tied to these specific releases (one index did not answer). The Willett paper above comes from the dataset card.
- **CDS/VizieR copies** of the catalogues were not checked.

## Next step
Run `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz2', name='tiny')` to see the format, then move to `gz_desi` for the thesis. If the code-release condition or the non-commercial licence is a problem, use the Zenodo releases (#4 or #5) instead.

## Details

**1. GZ DESI** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_desi
- **Contents:** 424×424 images plus one column per answer; the card says "The values are the count of volunteers who selected each answer."
- **Why it fits:** columns include `bar-dr5_strong/weak/no`, `merging-dr5_merger/major-disturbance/minor-disturbance/none`, bulge size, spiral arm count and winding.
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_desi', split='train')`. Try `name='tiny'` first.
- **Catches:** there are three campaigns (dr12, dr5, dr8) with slightly different questions. Many DR5/DR8 galaxies have only about five votes, so filter on the `*_total-votes` columns.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".

**2. Galaxy Zoo 2** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz2
- **Contents:** SDSS images with vote counts for bar (yes/no), bulge size (four levels), spiral arm count and winding.
- **Catches:** bars are yes/no only, and mergers sit under the "odd feature" question (from memory). It is the most heavily used set in this field.
- **Paper:** Willett et al. 2013, https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458.

**3. GZ Evo** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_evo
- **Contents:** GZ2, DESI, CANDELS, Hubble and UKIDSS combined and pre-shuffled.
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so you need a masked or multi-head loss. This is more than a master's thesis usually needs.

**4. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** — https://zenodo.org/records/4573248
- **Why consider it:** this is the original release behind most of #1, under plain CC BY 4.0 with no code-release condition.
- **Access:** download `gz_decals_volunteers_5.parquet`, `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2.parquet` and the four PNG zips (21–33 GB each), then join on `iauname`.
- **Catch:** ignore `gz_decals_auto_posteriors.*`, which are model predictions. Not every image has volunteer labels.

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 images** — https://zenodo.org/records/3565489
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`. The labels are the "GZ2 – Table 1 – Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" CSV at https://data.galaxyzoo.org/, joined through the mapping file.
- **Catch:** the licence of the tables on data.galaxyzoo.org was not stated on the page I read.

**6. GZ Euclid** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid
- **Contents:** Euclid space-telescope cutouts with the newest schema: strong/weak bar, five bulge sizes, graded mergers, clumps.
- **Catches:** the card is empty and states no licence. The columns are vote counts and `total-votes`, which indicates volunteer labels, but nothing on the card confirms it. Ask the maintainer before relying on it.

**7. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS** — https://zenodo.org/records/13357341
- **Contents:** near-infrared images of GZ2 galaxies; "The catalog contains volunteer vote counts", using the same question tree as GZ2.
- **Catch:** spiral structure is weaker in the infrared, and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**8. GZ Hubble** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_hubble
- **Contents:** HST galaxies with volunteer vote counts.
- **Catch:** these are distant, small, noisy galaxies; only useful if your thesis covers higher redshift.

**9. Galaxy Zoo Cosmic Dawn** — https://zenodo.org/records/17200992
- **Contents:** two image zips (15,745 + 29,997) plus `gzcd_volunteer_classifications.parquet`.
- **Catches:** skip the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. It barely clears 40k, the galaxies are faint, and I did not inspect the question schema.

**10. Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge** — https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge
- **Contents (from memory):** 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote-fraction columns.
- **Access (from memory):** free account, then accept the competition rules.
- **Catch:** the IDs are anonymised and it is a subset of GZ2, so #2 or #5 is the better choice.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Kaggle terms and counts (#10):** the page exists but is drawn by JavaScript, so I could not read it. Check the Data and Rules tabs.
- **Galaxy Zoo GAMA-KiDS (about 49k, from memory):** I did not find a standalone release in the registries; look on data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **GZ CANDELS:** the Hugging Face copy (`mwalmsley/gz_candels`, 48,098 images) passed the existence check, but I did not check its fit beyond size; it is high-redshift HST imaging.

## Not recommended, and why
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/8360385): "created by training deep learning models on Galaxy Zoo volunteer responses". These are predictions with no images.
- **Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/15106473): "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and Galaxy10 SDSS:** roughly 18k and 22k images in 10 coarse classes (sizes from memory), so too small and no per-feature labels.
- **Galaxy Zoo 1:** human votes, but only elliptical/spiral/merger and no images.
- **GZ2 catalogue record on Zenodo** (https://zenodo.org/records/3566991): "files are restricted"; use data.galaxyzoo.org instead.
- **`mwalmsley/gz_jwst_cosmos`:** gated and no licence stated.
- **Third-party Galaxy Zoo re-uploads on Hugging Face:** unverified provenance.

## What I could not find
- **Expert-labelled sets:** none with detailed features reaches 40k. The largest I know are Nair & Abraham 2010 (about 14k) and EFIGI (about 4.5k), both from memory. They could work as a small expert test set.
- **Recent CNN papers per release:** the paper search returned none tied to these specific releases (one index did not answer). The Willett paper above comes from the dataset card.
- **CDS/VizieR copies** of the catalogues were not checked.

## Next step
Run `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz2', name='tiny')` to see the format, then move to `gz_desi` for the thesis. If the code-release condition or the non-commercial licence is a problem, use the Zenodo releases (#4 or #5) instead.

Download **`mwalmsley/gz_desi`** from Hugging Face: about 399k galaxies, images bundled with volunteer vote counts, and separate strong-bar, weak-bar and graded-merger labels. If you want something smaller to start with, `mwalmsley/gz2` (191k SDSS galaxies, 2.6 GB) has the same format. Everything below was checked on 2026-11-12 unless marked "from memory".

## What I assumed you need
- **R1 (must):** at least 40,000 galaxies.
- **R2 (must):** labels from humans (volunteer votes or experts), not model output.
- **R3 (must):** detailed features: bars, spiral arms, bulge size, mergers.
- **R4 (nice):** images bundled with the labels.
- **R5 (must):** free and downloadable now. I assumed non-commercial thesis use and that you can publish your code.

## Shortlist

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | GZ DESI (`mwalmsley/gz_desi`) | Open download; card asks for a free HF login | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 + release your model code | 399,413 images, 17.5 GB | Strong | today |
| 2 | Galaxy Zoo 2 (`mwalmsley/gz2`) | Same | Same | 191,174 images, 2.6 GB | Strong | today |
| 3 | GZ Evo (`mwalmsley/gz_evo`) | Same | Same | 805,979 images, 18 GB | Strong | today |
| 4 | Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 314k galaxies, 108 GB | Strong | today |
| 5 | Galaxy Zoo 2 images (Zenodo) + vote table | Direct download, two sources | CC BY 4.0 (images) | 243,434 images, 3.4 GB | Strong | today |
| 6 | GZ Euclid (`mwalmsley/gz_euclid`) | Open download | None stated | 172,277 images, 0.5 GB | Partial | today |
| 7 | Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS (Zenodo) | Direct download | CC BY 4.0 | 71,052 galaxies, 7.9 GB | Partial | today |

## Details

**1. GZ DESI** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_desi
- **Contents:** 424×424 images plus one column per answer; the card says "The values are the count of volunteers who selected each answer."
- **Why it fits:** columns include `bar-dr5_strong/weak/no`, `merging-dr5_merger/major-disturbance/minor-disturbance/none`, bulge size, spiral arm count and winding.
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_desi', split='train')`. Try `name='tiny'` first.
- **Catches:** there are three campaigns (dr12, dr5, dr8) with slightly different questions. Many DR5/DR8 galaxies have only about five votes, so filter on the `*_total-votes` columns.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".

**2. Galaxy Zoo 2** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz2
- **Contents:** SDSS images with vote counts for bar (yes/no), bulge size (four levels), spiral arm count and winding.
- **Catches:** bars are yes/no only, and mergers sit under the "odd feature" question (from memory). It is the most heavily used set in this field.
- **Paper:** Willett et al. 2013, https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458.

**3. GZ Evo** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_evo
- **Contents:** GZ2, DESI, CANDELS, Hubble and UKIDSS combined and pre-shuffled.
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so you need a masked or multi-head loss. This is more than a master's thesis usually needs.

**4. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS** — https://zenodo.org/records/4573248
- **Why consider it:** this is the original release behind most of #1, under plain CC BY 4.0 with no code-release condition.
- **Access:** download `gz_decals_volunteers_5.parquet`, `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2.parquet` and the four PNG zips (21–33 GB each), then join on `iauname`.
- **Catch:** ignore `gz_decals_auto_posteriors.*`, which are model predictions. Not every image has volunteer labels.

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 images** — https://zenodo.org/records/3565489
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`. The labels are the "GZ2 – Table 1 – Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" CSV at https://data.galaxyzoo.org/, joined through the mapping file.
- **Catch:** the licence of the tables on data.galaxyzoo.org was not stated on the page I read.

**6. GZ Euclid** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid
- **Contents:** Euclid space-telescope cutouts with the newest schema: strong/weak bar, five bulge sizes, graded mergers, clumps.
- **Catches:** the card is empty and states no licence. The columns are vote counts and `total-votes`, which indicates volunteer labels, but nothing on the card confirms it. Ask the maintainer before relying on it.

**7. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS** — https://zenodo.org/records/13357341
- **Contents:** near-infrared images of GZ2 galaxies; "The catalog contains volunteer vote counts", using the same question tree as GZ2.
- **Catch:** spiral structure is weaker in the infrared, and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**8. GZ Hubble** — https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_hubble
- **Contents:** HST galaxies with volunteer vote counts.
- **Catch:** these are distant, small, noisy galaxies; only useful if your thesis covers higher redshift.

**9. Galaxy Zoo Cosmic Dawn** — https://zenodo.org/records/17200992
- **Contents:** two image zips (15,745 + 29,997) plus `gzcd_volunteer_classifications.parquet`.
- **Catches:** skip the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. It barely clears 40k, the galaxies are faint, and I did not inspect the question schema.

**10. Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge** — https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge
- **Contents (from memory):** 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote-fraction columns.
- **Access (from memory):** free account, then accept the competition rules.
- **Catch:** the IDs are anonymised and it is a subset of GZ2, so #2 or #5 is the better choice.

## Known, not confirmed
- **Kaggle terms and counts (#10):** the page exists but is drawn by JavaScript, so I could not read it. Check the Data and Rules tabs.
- **Galaxy Zoo GAMA-KiDS (about 49k, from memory):** I did not find a standalone release in the registries; look on data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **GZ CANDELS:** the Hugging Face copy (`mwalmsley/gz_candels`, 48,098 images) passed the existence check, but I did not check its fit beyond size; it is high-redshift HST imaging.

## Not recommended, and why
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/8360385): "created by training deep learning models on Galaxy Zoo volunteer responses". These are predictions with no images.
- **Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue** (https://zenodo.org/records/15106473): "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and Galaxy10 SDSS:** roughly 18k and 22k images in 10 coarse classes (sizes from memory), so too small and no per-feature labels.
- **Galaxy Zoo 1:** human votes, but only elliptical/spiral/merger and no images.
- **GZ2 catalogue record on Zenodo** (https://zenodo.org/records/3566991): "files are restricted"; use data.galaxyzoo.org instead.
- **`mwalmsley/gz_jwst_cosmos`:** gated and no licence stated.
- **Third-party Galaxy Zoo re-uploads on Hugging Face:** unverified provenance.

## What I could not find
- **Expert-labelled sets:** none with detailed features reaches 40k. The largest I know are Nair & Abraham 2010 (about 14k) and EFIGI (about 4.5k), both from memory. They could work as a small expert test set.
- **Recent CNN papers per release:** the paper search returned none tied to these specific releases (one index did not answer). The Willett paper above comes from the dataset card.
- **CDS/VizieR copies** of the catalogues were not checked.

## Next step
Run `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz2', name='tiny')` to see the format, then move to `gz_desi` for the thesis. If the code-release condition or the non-commercial licence is a problem, use the Zenodo releases (#4 or #5) instead.

## Details
**1. Galaxy Zoo Evo.**
- **Contents:** all Galaxy Zoo campaigns combined, with the image and the volunteer vote counts in the same row (for example `bar-gz2_yes`, `bulge-size-gz2_dominant`, `merging-dr12_tidal-debris`).
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_evo', split='train')`. The card suggests logging in with a free Hugging Face account, but the dataset is not gated. A `tiny` config (6.6k images) exists for prototyping.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so the other columns are empty. Filter on the total-votes columns.

**2. GZ DESI volunteer subset.** This is the DECaLS/Legacy Survey part of #1 on its own, with 319,530 train and 79,883 test images. It has an explicit merging question. Access and licence are as for #1. Many galaxies from the fifth campaign have only about five votes.

**3. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the official release, with the PNGs shown to volunteers in four zips.
- **Use only** `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2` and `gz_decals_volunteers_5`. The file `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is model output and breaks your human-label rule.
- **Access:** download the catalogues and image zips, then join on `iauname`. Not every image has volunteer labels.
- **Paper:** [Walmsley et al. 2021, MNRAS](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab2093).

**4. Galaxy Zoo 2 (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the classic SDSS benchmark; bars, arm count and winding, and bulge size are all questions in the tree.
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`, then get "GZ2 - Table 1 - Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" from data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Catch:** merger is only an answer under the "odd feature" question (from memory). The separate Zenodo record for the tables (3566991) has restricted files, so use data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Paper:** [Willett et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458).

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 (HF).** The same survey as #4, already joined. This packaging has no merger column.

**6. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS.** Uses the same question tree as GZ2, with volunteer vote counts and 70,845 JPGs in the same record. The imaging is near-infrared and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**7–9. Hubble, Cosmic Dawn, CANDELS.** All have volunteer votes and bundled images, but the galaxies are distant, so bars and arms are harder to see.
- **Hubble:** no merger column in this packaging.
- **Cosmic Dawn:** exclude the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. I did not read its question tree.
- **CANDELS:** has merger and tidal-debris votes.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[Galaxy Zoo Euclid](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid) (HF):** exists, is not gated, and has 172,277 rows with vote columns including merging. The card is empty, no licence is stated, and the download is only 0.3 GB, so I could not confirm that full images are included or that the labels are volunteer votes. Check the viewer and ask the author before relying on it.
- **[Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge](https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge):** the page exists but the tool could not read it. From memory: 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote fractions, behind a free Kaggle account and acceptance of the competition rules. It is a subset of GZ2, so #4 or #5 is the better choice.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/8360385):** labels are predicted vote fractions from a model. Its volunteer-labelled part is #2.
- **[Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/15106473):** "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **[Galaxy10 DECaLS](https://zenodo.org/records/10845026):** about 17.7k images in 10 coarse classes (size from memory).
- **[Galaxy Zoo 1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.90206.v1):** only elliptical / spiral / merger, and no images.
- **[Nair & Abraham 2010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/186/2/427):** expert labels but only 14,034 galaxies and no bundled images. It could serve as an independent test set.
- **Third-party re-uploads on Hugging Face and Kaggle:** provenance and licence are unclear.

## What I could not find
- No expert-labelled set above 40k galaxies with detailed features turned up. At this scale the human labels are volunteer votes.
- The paper search indexes astronomy poorly, so I only have the describing papers as evidence of use. CDS/VizieR was not searched.

## Details
**1. Galaxy Zoo Evo.**
- **Contents:** all Galaxy Zoo campaigns combined, with the image and the volunteer vote counts in the same row (for example `bar-gz2_yes`, `bulge-size-gz2_dominant`, `merging-dr12_tidal-debris`).
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_evo', split='train')`. The card suggests logging in with a free Hugging Face account, but the dataset is not gated. A `tiny` config (6.6k images) exists for prototyping.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so the other columns are empty. Filter on the total-votes columns.

**2. GZ DESI volunteer subset.** This is the DECaLS/Legacy Survey part of #1 on its own, with 319,530 train and 79,883 test images. It has an explicit merging question. Access and licence are as for #1. Many galaxies from the fifth campaign have only about five votes.

**3. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the official release, with the PNGs shown to volunteers in four zips.
- **Use only** `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2` and `gz_decals_volunteers_5`. The file `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is model output and breaks your human-label rule.
- **Access:** download the catalogues and image zips, then join on `iauname`. Not every image has volunteer labels.
- **Paper:** [Walmsley et al. 2021, MNRAS](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab2093).

**4. Galaxy Zoo 2 (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the classic SDSS benchmark; bars, arm count and winding, and bulge size are all questions in the tree.
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`, then get "GZ2 - Table 1 - Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" from data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Catch:** merger is only an answer under the "odd feature" question (from memory). The separate Zenodo record for the tables (3566991) has restricted files, so use data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Paper:** [Willett et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458).

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 (HF).** The same survey as #4, already joined. This packaging has no merger column.

**6. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS.** Uses the same question tree as GZ2, with volunteer vote counts and 70,845 JPGs in the same record. The imaging is near-infrared and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**7–9. Hubble, Cosmic Dawn, CANDELS.** All have volunteer votes and bundled images, but the galaxies are distant, so bars and arms are harder to see.
- **Hubble:** no merger column in this packaging.
- **Cosmic Dawn:** exclude the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. I did not read its question tree.
- **CANDELS:** has merger and tidal-debris votes.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[Galaxy Zoo Euclid](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid) (HF):** exists, is not gated, and has 172,277 rows with vote columns including merging. The card is empty, no licence is stated, and the download is only 0.3 GB, so I could not confirm that full images are included or that the labels are volunteer votes. Check the viewer and ask the author before relying on it.
- **[Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge](https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge):** the page exists but the tool could not read it. From memory: 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote fractions, behind a free Kaggle account and acceptance of the competition rules. It is a subset of GZ2, so #4 or #5 is the better choice.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/8360385):** labels are predicted vote fractions from a model. Its volunteer-labelled part is #2.
- **[Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/15106473):** "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **[Galaxy10 DECaLS](https://zenodo.org/records/10845026):** about 17.7k images in 10 coarse classes (size from memory).
- **[Galaxy Zoo 1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.90206.v1):** only elliptical / spiral / merger, and no images.
- **[Nair & Abraham 2010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/186/2/427):** expert labels but only 14,034 galaxies and no bundled images. It could serve as an independent test set.
- **Third-party re-uploads on Hugging Face and Kaggle:** provenance and licence are unclear.

## What I could not find
- No expert-labelled set above 40k galaxies with detailed features turned up. At this scale the human labels are volunteer votes.
- The paper search indexes astronomy poorly, so I only have the describing papers as evidence of use. CDS/VizieR was not searched.

Load the `tiny` config of `gz_evo` or `gz_desi` to get your pipeline running. Then choose between #2 (convenient, but you must release your model code) and #3 (CC-BY, but a 104 GB download and a manual join).

The interactive comparison page is at `/private/tmp/e-ZPkd3O/home/cwd/dataset-shortlist.html`.

The card is empty, no licence is stated, and the download is only 0.3 GB, so I could not confirm that full images are included or that the labels are volunteer votes. Check the viewer and ask the author before relying on it.
- **[Kaggle Galaxy Zoo challenge](https://www.kaggle.com/c/galaxy-zoo-the-galaxy-challenge):** the page exists but the tool could not read it. From memory: 61,578 training JPGs with 37 GZ2 vote fractions, behind a free Kaggle account and acceptance of the competition rules. It is a subset of GZ2, so #4 or #5 is the better choice.

## Not recommended, and why
- **[Galaxy Zoo DESI 8.7M catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/8360385):** labels are predicted vote fractions from a model. Its volunteer-labelled part is #2.
- **[Euclid Q1 morphology catalogue](https://zenodo.org/records/15106473):** "measurements were made by Zoobot foundation models".
- **[Galaxy10 DECaLS](https://zenodo.org/records/10845026):** about 17.7k images in 10 coarse classes (size from memory).
- **[Galaxy Zoo 1](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.90206.v1):** only elliptical / spiral / merger, and no images.
- **[Nair & Abraham 2010](https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/186/2/427):** expert labels but only 14,034 galaxies and no bundled images. It could serve as an independent test set.
- **Third-party re-uploads on Hugging Face and Kaggle:** provenance and licence are unclear.

## What I could not find
- No expert-labelled set above 40k galaxies with detailed features turned up. At this scale the human labels are volunteer votes.
- The paper search indexes astronomy poorly, so I only have the describing papers as evidence of use. CDS/VizieR was not searched.

## What I assumed you need
- **R1** galaxy images usable for CNN training (must)
- **R2** detailed labels: bars, spiral arms, bulge size, mergers (must)
- **R3** at least 40,000 labelled galaxies (must)
- **R4** labels from humans, not model predictions (must)
- **R5** free and downloadable now (must)
- **R6** images bundled with the labels (nice to have)
- I assumed non-commercial academic use and that you can publish your code.

## Details
**1. Galaxy Zoo Evo.**
- **Contents:** all Galaxy Zoo campaigns combined, with the image and the volunteer vote counts in the same row (for example `bar-gz2_yes`, `bulge-size-gz2_dominant`, `merging-dr12_tidal-debris`).
- **Access:** `pip install datasets`, then `load_dataset('mwalmsley/gz_evo', split='train')`. The card suggests logging in with a free Hugging Face account, but the dataset is not gated. A `tiny` config (6.6k images) exists for prototyping.
- **Licence:** non-commercial, share-alike, and the card requires "all models trained on these datasets to be released as source code by publication".
- **Catch:** each galaxy only has votes for its own campaign's questions, so the other columns are empty. Filter on the total-votes columns.

**2. GZ DESI volunteer subset.** This is the DECaLS/Legacy Survey part of #1 on its own, with 319,530 train and 79,883 test images. It has an explicit merging question. Access and licence are as for #1. Many galaxies from the fifth campaign have only about five votes.

**3. Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the official release, with the PNGs shown to volunteers in four zips.
- **Use only** `gz_decals_volunteers_1_and_2` and `gz_decals_volunteers_5`. The file `gz_decals_auto_posteriors` is model output and breaks your human-label rule.
- **Access:** download the catalogues and image zips, then join on `iauname`. Not every image has volunteer labels.
- **Paper:** [Walmsley et al. 2021, MNRAS](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stab2093).

**4. Galaxy Zoo 2 (Zenodo).**
- **Contents:** the classic SDSS benchmark; bars, arm count and winding, and bulge size are all questions in the tree.
- **Access:** download `images_gz2.zip` and `gz2_filename_mapping.csv`, then get "GZ2 - Table 1 - Normal-depth sample with new debiasing method" from data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Catch:** merger is only an answer under the "odd feature" question (from memory). The separate Zenodo record for the tables (3566991) has restricted files, so use data.galaxyzoo.org.
- **Paper:** [Willett et al. 2013](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stt1458).

**5. Galaxy Zoo 2 (HF).** The same survey as #4, already joined. This packaging has no merger column.

**6. Galaxy Zoo UKIDSS.** Uses the same question tree as GZ2, with volunteer vote counts and 70,845 JPGs in the same record. The imaging is near-infrared and the galaxies overlap with GZ2.

**7–9. Hubble, Cosmic Dawn, CANDELS.** All have volunteer votes and bundled images, but the galaxies are distant, so bars and arms are harder to see.
- **Hubble:** no merger column in this packaging.
- **Cosmic Dawn:** exclude the `gzcd_zoobot_*` files, which are predictions. I did not read its question tree.
- **CANDELS:** has merger and tidal-debris votes.

## Known, not confirmed
- **[Galaxy Zoo Euclid](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_euclid) (HF):** exists, is not gated, and has 172,277 rows with vote columns including merging. The card is empty, no licence is stated, and the download is only 0.3 GB, so I could not confirm that full images are included or that the labels are volunteer votes. Check the viewer and ask the author before relying on it.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Download Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2) through the `galaxy-datasets` Python package.** It gives you about 210k SDSS galaxies with volunteer vote counts, and the images and labels arrive together in one call. I checked the sources online but did not run the download myself.

```python
# pip install galaxy-datasets
from galaxy_datasets import gz2

catalog, label_cols = gz2(root='data/gz2', train=True, download=True)
```

`catalog` is a pandas table with one row per galaxy, including the image path, and `label_cols` names the vote-count columns. There is also a PyTorch wrapper (`from galaxy_datasets.pytorch import GZ2`) and a Hugging Face copy at `mwalmsley/gz2`, whose card I did not inspect.

Why it fits your requirements:

- **Human labels:** every label is the number of volunteers who gave each answer; from memory, each galaxy has roughly 40 or more classifications.
- **Detailed morphology:** from memory of the GZ2 decision tree, it covers bar, spiral arms (count and winding), bulge prominence, edge-on bulge shape, and odd features including rings, mergers, disturbed and dust lanes.
- **Size:** about 210k galaxies, and the image set is only about 3.4 GB of JPEGs.
- **Free:** the package is GPL-3.0 and the underlying Zenodo image release is CC BY 4.0. Cite Willett et al. 2013 and SDSS.

Two things to handle in training:

- **Conditional questions:** volunteers were only asked about bars or arms if they first answered "features or disk". Mask or down-weight questions with few responses rather than treating a 0 as "no bar".
- **Soft labels:** predict vote fractions or counts rather than hard classes; forcing a majority-vote class throws away the uncertainty information.

**Alternative: Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (GZD-5)**, about 230k galaxies, also in the package as `gz_decals_5`. The imaging is deeper, and as I recall the questions are better for your purposes: strong/weak/no bar, and merger versus major or minor disturbance. The catch is that many galaxies have only about five volunteer responses, so you would need to filter by vote count; I haven't checked how many pass a strict cut. If you take it from Zenodo (record 4573248, CC BY 4.0, about 108 GB) instead, use the `gz_decals_volunteers_5` file and not `gz_decals_auto_posteriors`, which is model predictions.

**Avoid for your purpose:**

- **GZ DESI (8.7M galaxies):** as I recall, its headline catalogue is mostly model predictions.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and GalaxyMNIST:** human-labelled but only about 18k and 10k galaxies with coarse classes.
- **`mwalmsley/gz_evo` on Hugging Face:** combines several Galaxy Zoo campaigns, but it is licensed CC BY-NC-SA and I couldn't confirm its contents.

Sources:
- [galaxy-datasets (GitHub)](https://github.com/mwalmsley/galaxy-datasets)
- [Galaxy Zoo 2 images (Zenodo 3565489)](https://zenodo.org/records/3565489)
- [Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (Zenodo 4573248)](https://zenodo.org/records/4573248)
- [mwalmsley/gz_evo (Hugging Face)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mwalmsley/gz_evo)
- [mwalmsley datasets list (Hugging Face API)](https://huggingface.co/api/datasets?author=mwalmsley&limit=100)

- **Conditional questions:** volunteers were only asked about bars or arms if they first answered "features or disk". Mask or down-weight questions with few responses rather than treating a 0 as "no bar".
- **Soft labels:** predict vote fractions or counts rather than hard classes; forcing a majority-vote class throws away the uncertainty information.

**Alternative: Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (GZD-5)**, about 230k galaxies, also in the package as `gz_decals_5`. The imaging is deeper, and as I recall the questions are better for your purposes: strong/weak/no bar, and merger versus major or minor disturbance. The catch is that many galaxies have only about five volunteer responses, so you would need to filter by vote count; I haven't checked how many pass a strict cut. If you take it from Zenodo (record 4573248, CC BY 4.0, about 108 GB) instead, use the `gz_decals_volunteers_5` file and not `gz_decals_auto_posteriors`, which is model predictions.

**Avoid for your purpose:**

- **GZ DESI (8.7M galaxies):** as I recall, its headline catalogue is mostly model predictions.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS and GalaxyMNIST:** human-labelled but only about 18k and 10k galaxies with coarse classes.
- **`mwalmsley/gz_evo` on Hugging Face:** combines several Galaxy Zoo campaigns, but it is licensed CC BY-NC-SA and I couldn't confirm its contents.

Evidence (what the judge was shown; for an image, a description of what was sent)
**Download Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2).** It meets every requirement and is the standard benchmark for this task. I'm answering from memory and didn't check the links live, so confirm the record IDs and counts before relying on them.

**Why GZ2**
- **Size:** about 240k SDSS galaxies, as 424×424 colour JPGs.
- **Human labels:** volunteer votes only, roughly 40+ per galaxy, so the vote fractions are fairly low-noise.
- **Morphology detail:** a decision tree covering smooth/featured/artifact, edge-on, bar, spiral arms (presence, tightness, count), bulge prominence, bulge shape, roundedness, and odd features (merger, ring, lens, disturbed, dust lane).
- **Citations:** Willett et al. 2013 for the catalogue, Hart et al. 2016 for the debiased vote fractions.

**Where to get images and labels together**
1. **`galaxy-datasets` Python package** (Mike Walmsley, Galaxy Zoo team): `pip install galaxy-datasets`, then `from galaxy_datasets import gz2`. This downloads images plus a label table with train/test splits, and has PyTorch helpers. The same data is on Hugging Face under `mwalmsley/gz2`.
2. **Zenodo record 3565489:** the full GZ2 image set plus a filename mapping to join with the Hart et al. 2016 vote table from data.galaxyzoo.org.
3. **Kaggle "Galaxy Zoo – The Galaxy Challenge":** 61,578 training images with 37 vote-fraction columns in one zip. It is the easiest start and still above your 40k, but it is a subset; the Kaggle test-set labels aren't public.

**Alternative: Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (GZD-5)**
- **What it adds:** about 250k galaxies with deeper imaging, so faint bars and tidal features show better, and a dedicated merger question (merger / major disturbance / minor disturbance / none).
- **Where:** Zenodo record 4573248, or `gz_decals_5` in the same package.
- **Watch for the label source:** use only the **volunteer** catalogues (`gz_decals_volunteers_5`), not `gz_decals_auto_posteriors`, which are CNN predictions.
- **Watch for vote counts:** many galaxies have only about 5 votes, with about 40 for a subset. Filter by vote count or use a loss that accounts for it.

**Sets that fail your requirements**
- **Galaxy Zoo DESI** (8.7M galaxies): the labels are mostly model predictions.
- **Galaxy10 DECaLS** (17.7k), **Nair & Abraham 2010** (14k, expert) and **EFIGI** (4.5k, expert): all are under 40k. The two expert sets are still useful as an independent test set.

**Training tips**
- Predict vote fractions or counts rather than hard classes.
- Mask questions that few volunteers reached; bar votes mean nothing for a galaxy most people called smooth.

Prompt

I need free galaxy images with detailed morphology labels (bars, spiral arms, bulge size, mergers etc.) to train a CNN for my master's thesis: at least 40k galaxies, and the labels have to come from humans (volunteer votes or experts), not from another model's predictions. Ideally the images come bundled with the labels. What should I download?

tool"Skill"

01-recall-galaxy-zoo-2llm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists Galaxy Zoo 2 (also written GZ2; the SDSS-based Galaxy Zoo 2 catalogue of Willett et al. 2013, including the Hart et al. 2016 debiased table, the GZ2 image set on Zenodo, or the Kaggle "Galaxy Zoo - The Galaxy Challenge" subset built from GZ2) as a candidate dataset for human-labelled galaxy morphology, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

02-recall-galaxy-zoo-decalsllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists Galaxy Zoo DECaLS (also written GZ DECaLS or GZD; the Walmsley et al. 2022 release of volunteer classifications for about 314,000 galaxies imaged by the Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey, with volunteer-facing images on Zenodo) as a candidate dataset for human-labelled galaxy morphology, in any version. FAIL if the answer does not mention Galaxy Zoo DECaLS, mentions only Galaxy10 DECaLS, or mentions Galaxy Zoo DECaLS only to say it is unsuitable.

03-recall-galaxy-zoo-hubblellm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists Galaxy Zoo: Hubble (also written GZ: Hubble or GZH; the Willett et al. 2017 volunteer morphology classifications of about 114,000 galaxies imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope ACS in the AEGIS, COSMOS, GEMS and GOODS surveys) as a candidate dataset for human-labelled galaxy morphology. FAIL if the answer does not mention it, or mentions it only to say it is unsuitable.

04-access-gz2-free-downloadllm

PASS if the final answer mentions Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2) and states that its classification tables and/or its images can be downloaded free of charge without any application or approval, for example the tables from data.galaxyzoo.org and the image set (about 243,000 images) from Zenodo, or states that the GZ2 image set is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) licence. FAIL if the answer does not mention Galaxy Zoo 2, gives no information about how it is obtained, or states that it requires payment, an application or approval.

05-access-decals-zenodollm

PASS if the final answer mentions Galaxy Zoo DECaLS and states that its volunteer classification catalogues (and the images shown to volunteers) are free to download without an application, for example from Zenodo or the Galaxy Zoo data site, or states that the release is under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) licence. FAIL if the answer does not mention Galaxy Zoo DECaLS, gives no information about how it is obtained, or states that it requires payment, an application or approval.

06-trap-galaxy10-too-smallllm

PASS if the final answer does not present Galaxy10 DECaLS (the astroNN dataset of 17,736 DECaLS galaxy images in 10 broad classes) or the original Galaxy10 SDSS dataset (about 22,000 images in 10 classes) as meeting the requirement of at least 40,000 human-labelled galaxies with detailed morphology labels. Not mentioning Galaxy10 passes; mentioning it while noting that it is too small (under 40,000 galaxies) or only has 10 broad classes also passes. FAIL if the answer recommends Galaxy10 or Galaxy10 DECaLS as satisfying the 40,000-galaxy requirement, or describes it as containing 40,000 or more labelled galaxies.

07-long-tailllm

PASS if the final answer recommends or lists at least one of these less known human-labelled Galaxy Zoo releases as a candidate: (a) Galaxy Zoo: UKIDSS (volunteer classifications of about 71,000 galaxies in UKIRT Infrared Deep Sky Survey near-infrared imaging, with images on Zenodo); (b) Galaxy Zoo: CANDELS (volunteer classifications of about 49,555 galaxies in Hubble CANDELS imaging, Simmons et al. 2017). FAIL if the answer mentions neither of them as a candidate.
